source: cross-examiner verdicts from the research fleets (one agent per contested claim, both lenses)

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Ministry of Coal (the Nominated Authority, with ECoS approval) allocated Gondbahera Ujheni East to MP Natural Resources Pvt Ltd, with vesting on 10-10-2022. The mine was offered in the 2nd commercial round (MMDR-2) and had not been offered in any earlier tranche; the PIB table shows "Nil". Both primary records give the same vesting date. The later award, Gondbahera Ujheni (MMDR-6, vesting 08-06-2023, PRC 4.12), is also confirmed by allocation-trance-wise.pdf. There is no chronology problem, because the awarder is an institution and the claim does not rely on any individual's tenure. Date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The PIB release (ID 1975677, 8 Nov 2023) names the bidder "MP Natural Resources Private Limited" and says: "only one coal mine i.e. Gondbahera Ujheni East coal mine has been successfully won by the Adani Group i.e. MP Natural Resources Pvt Ltd." The MoC allocation file prints the same legal name ("MP Natural Resources PrivateLimited"). research/raw/adani-deep.json lists it as an Adani Enterprises SPV, taken from the AEL annual report. There is no name-collision risk. The node's identity.cin is null and should be filled.
verdicts.baseRate: This part of the claim is wrong. The PIB table lists 11 single-bid allocations made after a 2nd attempt. Only 7 of the 11 are at 5.00%: Gondbahera Ujheni East, Tokisud Block II, Kasta (East), Barra, Maiki North, Alaknanda and Sitanala. That means 6 others, not 10. The other four are Kuraloi (A) North at 15.25% (Vedanta), Ashok Karkatta Central at 6.50%, Marki Barka at 6.00% and Choritand Tiliaya at 11.25%. So 5.00% is the modal single-bid outcome (7/11, 64%): weak and non-discriminating. Adani's share of single-bid allocations is 1/11 (9%). Single-bid allocations were 11 of 91 commercial mines auctioned to Nov 2023 (about 12%). The claim's "10 others at same 5%" repeats the Ministry's loose sentence ("Other mines have also been successfully auctioned to others at the same percentage revenue share"), which the Ministry's own table contradicts.
verdicts.denialFound: The only official response is the Ministry's own PIB release 1975677 (8 Nov 2023, https://www.coal.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-11/PIB1975677.pdf). It says the 11 single-bid allocations were made with ECoS approval "on the basis of transparency in auction, reasonability of offer and number of rounds the mines have been offered", and that "no correlation has been established between Cavill Mining Pvt Ltd and Adani Group". I found no Adani Group response on Gondbahera Ujheni East. Scroll's related story on Gondbahera Ujheni and Cavill Mining says: "Questions were sent to the Adani Group, Cavill Mining, and the coal ministry. No responses had been received at the time of publication." So Adani was asked and did not respond (on the related block).
verdicts.innocentReading: The 2021 methodology allows a mine to go to ECoS after two failed attempts with fewer than two technically qualified bidders. Many blocks got no bids at all across seven rounds. A partially explored MP block drawing one bidder, at a price close to the floor, is the typical outcome for a single-bid block: 7 of the 11 single-bid mines, won by Vedanta/BALCO, JSW, Rungta, Jitusol, Maiki South and Twenty First Century, landed at exactly 5.00%. Run the same way, the check produces equal or stronger edges for rivals. Vedanta's Kuraloi (A) North at 15.25% and BALCO's Barra at 5.00% are also single-bid ECoS allocations. The edge records a documented award, not favouritism.
verdicts.reason: The award edge holds. Two primary MoC records (PIB 1975677 and allocation-trance-wise.pdf) confirm the winner, the block, the 5.00% offer, the single-bid ECoS route and the 10-10-2022 vesting date, and the Ministry itself names the winner as the Adani Group. So "documented" is the right tier. But the claim's own counterweight, "10 others at same 5%", is false against the source table: only 6 others are at 5.00%, and four went at 6.00–15.25%. Fix the text before publishing. The error slightly understates the counter; it does not change the tier.
verdicts.corrections:
1. In text, replace "(1 of 11 single-bid mines; 10 others at same 5%)" with "(1 of 11 single-bid ECoS allocations to Nov 2023; 7 of the 11, including this one, at 5.00%; the others at 6.00–15.25%)". Also note that the Ministry's sentence claiming all others were at the same share is contradicted by its own table.
2. Add a Ministry contra or context edge citing PIB 1975677's justification ("reasonability of offer and number of rounds"). Record that Adani did not respond to Scroll's questions on the related Gondbahera Ujheni story.
3. In d, say explicitly that the later Gondbahera Ujheni award (vesting 08-06-2023, MMDR-6) was not a single-bid allocation. It was contested by Cavill Mining and GMDC, and it is not in the PIB single-bid table.
4. Qualify "floor-adjacent" with the methodology's floor (4% revenue share) or drop the word.
5. Fill identity.cin for energy:mp-natural-resources and link it to the AEL parent (coal:c065 own edge) using the AEL annual-report subsidiary list, not only the PIB phrase.
6. In coal.json, the source title calls allocation-trance-wise.pdf "re-opened 2026-09-25". Both PDFs were re-fetched and parsed on 2026-09-25 and match.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Cavill Mining bid second for Gondbahera Ujheni East, which let MP Natural Resources clear the two-bidder rule, vesting 10-10-2022. That fails on the dates. Cavill was incorporated on 24 Apr 2022 (Scroll, from MCA filings). Its only reported bids were in the March 2023 tranche (16th overall, 7th commercial), on North West of Madheri and Gondbahera Ujheni. Gondbahera Ujheni East vested on 10-10-2022 after a second-attempt SINGLE bid referred to ECoS. The cited PIB 1975677 lists it as row 2 of the "11 coal mines ... allocated ... based on single bid after 2nd attempt". So that block had no second bidder, and Cavill is not linked to it anywhere. The edge's 'from' of 2023-11-01 is also wrong. The allegation dates from Scroll on 4 Apr 2023. Congress (Jairam Ramesh) repeated it in Nov 2023, and MoC rebutted it on 8 Nov 2023.
verdicts.identityTest: Three identities are wrong. (a) The block is North West of Madheri (Chandrapur, Maharashtra, about 200 MT), not Gondbahera Ujheni East (MP). (b) The winner there was MH Natural Resources Pvt Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Adani Enterprises, at 5.5%. It was not MP Natural Resources at 5%. Cavill's second Adani contest was Gondbahera Ujheni (not 'East'), won at 7%. That auction had three bidders, including state-owned GMDC. (c) The accuser is Scroll.in (4 Apr 2023), then Congress/Jairam Ramesh. It is not The Reporters' Collective or Adani Watch. TRC's site search for 'cavill' returns "No matching results", and its Coal Files and Mara II Mahan stories do not mention Cavill. Scroll's actual allegation also runs to a different owner. Utkarsh Shah held 80% of Cavill's Rs 1,00,000 capital; after his death his son Adarsh Shah became director. That makes Cavill a sister company of Adicorp Enterprises, the firm Hindenburg flagged. Scroll never claims Adani OWNS Cavill, so pred 'own' (grp:adani -> cavill) states something even the accuser does not say. The cavill node has no CIN; it should be pulled from MCA.
verdicts.baseRate: Adani's March 2023 wins mostly faced a single rival. Scroll: "In three of the four blocks it won, the Adani Group faced only one other bidder". That covers Power Mech at Purunga and Gangaramchak at Dahegaon Gowari as well as Cavill at NW Madheri. So two-bidder contests are common in low-interest tranches. What sets this case apart is the specific overlap of shared address, shared promoter and a Rs 1-lakh, zero-experience bidder. A two-bidder auction on its own proves nothing. Separately, single-bid allocations went to 11 firms, and Adani got 1 of the 11 (PIB).
verdicts.denialFound: MoC, PIB 1975677, 8 Nov 2023 (https://www.coal.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-11/PIB1975677.pdf): "no correlation has been established between Cavill Mining Pvt Ltd and Adani Group ... it cannot be established that Cavill Mining Pvt Ltd is an affiliate of Adani Group." The CCI dismissed the bid-rigging complaint covering MP/MH Natural Resources and Cavill (NW Madheri, Gondbahera Ujheni). It found that GMDC's independent participation "significantly weakened any inference of collusion" (legalnewsindia, 2 Aug 2025: https://www.legalnewsindia.com/cci-adani-group-rp-sanjiv-goenka-cartelisation-coal-block-auctions/799/). Scroll put questions to Adani Group, Cavill and MoC: "No responses had been received at the time of publication." No direct statement from Adani Group was found.
verdicts.innocentReading: Utkarsh Shah was a long-time acquaintance of Gautam Adani and a real-estate promoter. His family could have set up a small SPV to try commercial coal, as many new entrants did in 2022-23. Cavill bid independently and lost at 5.5%. At Gondbahera Ujheni it faced both Adani and GMDC. The shared address with Adicorp only shows common ownership by the Shah family, not control by Adani. It meets none of the tender's four 'affiliate' tests, and both MoC and CCI found no link.
verdicts.reason: The claim is refuted as written. Its only cited primary source (PIB 1975677) contradicts its core mechanism. That document lists Gondbahera Ujheni East as a single-bid allocation after a second attempt, so no second bidder could have 'cleared the two-bidder threshold' there. The PIB also never mentions Rs 1 lakh, TRC, Adani Watch, or which block Cavill bid on. The real allegation (Scroll.in, 4 Apr 2023) concerns North West of Madheri, which MH Natural Resources won at 5.5%. The accuser, block, Adani subsidiary, revenue share, date and predicate are all wrong. A properly sourced version can survive at 'alleged': Scroll as named accuser, plus Congress; MoC denial and CCI dismissal as contra.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Change pred from 'own' to an association or alleged-link predicate. Better, route the link as grp:adani -> adicorp <- Shah family -> cavill, because Scroll alleges common ownership with Adicorp, not ownership by Adani. 2. Change the block from 'Gondbahera Ujheni East' to 'North West of Madheri (Chandrapur, Maharashtra)', and note that Cavill also bid on Gondbahera Ujheni (not East) alongside GMDC. 3. Change the Adani entity from MP Natural Resources to MH Natural Resources Pvt Ltd (Adani Enterprises subsidiary). The winning share is 5.5%, not 5%. The tranche is March 2023, not vesting 10-10-2022. 4. Change the accuser from 'Reporters' Collective/Adani Watch' to Scroll.in, 'Adani got coal mine in auction where only other bidder was firm linked to Hindenburg storm', 4 Apr 2023, https://scroll.in/article/1046739/adani-got-coal-mine-in-auction-where-only-other-bidder-was-firm-linked-to-hindenburg-storm. Also cite Congress/Jairam Ramesh, Nov 2023. Remove the reporters-collective.in home-page source. 5. Change 'from' from 2023-11-01 to 2023-04-04. 6. Add a CCI dismissal (reported Aug 2025) to the contra alongside c023. Drop '1 of 11 single-bid allocations' from the contra, because it concerns a different block and is not responsive. 7. Fill in the cavill node: incorporated 24-04-2022, Ahmedabad; paid-up Rs 1,00,000; 80% Utkarsh Shah (deceased), director Adarsh Shah; shares an address with Adicorp Enterprises; CIN still to be pulled from MCA. Change the node sub-label from 'Second bidder for Gondbahera Ujheni East'. 8. In the linked edge coal:c021, correct benefit.how. 'Only one other technically qualified bidder (Cavill Mining)' is false, because per the PIB Gondbahera Ujheni East was a single bid after the second attempt.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Jaipur court found in July 2025 that PKCL had recovered more than Rs 1,400 cr from RRVUNL for road transport it should have paid for. The Madhyamam story (24 Nov 2025, reporting Scroll.in) refers to "a July judgment" and says "The Jaipur court case, spanning from 2020 to 2025", so the judgment is July 2025. The road haulage ran from March 2013 onward, after mining began. The suit was filed in July 2020 and PKCL has existed since the 2008 CMDA, so the dates overlap. The source says the High Court stay came 13 days later but gives no exact date. It does not say 14 July, so the from-date in c033 is not supported by this source.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The source names "Parsa Kente Collieries Limited, in which Adani Enterprises holds 74 per cent and Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited (RRVUNL) 26 per cent". That matches the node's description and there is no risk of a name clash. The court node is a small problem. Madhyamam calls it "a Jaipur district court" / "district court" and never uses the words "commercial court". The node label "Commercial Court, Jaipur" may come from Scroll or be correct (a commercial suit worth Rs 65 cr would normally go to a commercial court at district level), but the opened source does not say it. No CIN is recorded for PKCL.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not a shared-property edge. It is one specific judicial finding against one named entity, so base rate does not apply. On symmetry: the source notes that RRVUNL refused interest in Feb 2018 under a BJP government and that the suit was filed in July 2020 under Gehlot's Congress government. The dispute runs across both parties' governments and has no obvious partisan slant. MDO-model criticism in the article (Priyanshu Gupta) is general to the sector, but the Rs 1,400 cr finding is specific to PKCL.
verdicts.denialFound: None found (the opened source does not say whether anyone asked). The Madhyamam/Scroll relay has no statement from Adani Enterprises or PKCL and does not say they were contacted. The only contra on record is PKCL's appeal and the Rajasthan HC stay (c033). WebSearch budget was exhausted and fallback search engines returned nothing, so the Scroll original and any Adani comment in it could not be checked.
verdicts.innocentReading: The road haulage was paid under an interim arrangement both sides agreed to, confirmed in a March 2013 letter. RRVUNL undertook to reimburse the transporter's charges within 15 days. So the Rs 1,400 cr was paid by agreement, and the source itself says the arrangement "fell outside the written contract, which did not mention road transport". The court's view that PKCL should have carried the cost is an inference from PKCL's unmet duty to build the railway siding. That point was not what the suit was about: "The litigation, however, did not directly challenge this ₹1,400 crore". The suit concerned about Rs 65 cr in interest. RRVUNL filed almost no evidence, and the finding and directions are stayed on appeal. The Rs 1,400 cr is also a gross reimbursement, not a proven wrongful gain.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives at reported tier. Madhyamam, crediting Scroll.in and quoting the judgment at length, confirms each element. Rs 1,400 cr: "had claimed and recovered road transportation costs that it was contractually obliged to bear" and "Those charges eventually exceeded ₹1,400 crore". The penalties: "It ordered the company to pay a ₹50 lakh fine and directed the state government to ask the Comptroller and Auditor General to audit the deal". The stay: "These directions were stayed by the Rajasthan High Court 13 days later". July 2025: "a July judgment". The claim text already says it relies on one secondary source and that the directions are stayed, which is the right tier: a credible outlet relaying quoted parts of a court judgment. It cannot be documented until the judgment itself (or the Scroll original plus a second independent outlet) is opened. It is not refuted because each fact in the claim matches the source.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Court node: Madhyamam says "Jaipur district court", not "commercial court". Either get the Scroll original or the judgment to confirm "Commercial Court", or relabel the node "Jaipur district (commercial) court" and note that the source calls it a district court. 2) Add to the claim or its d field that the Rs 1,400 cr finding was incidental to PKCL's Rs 65 cr interest suit ("the litigation did not directly challenge this ₹1,400 crore"). Also add that the charges were paid under a mutually agreed March 2013 interim arrangement outside the written CMDA, and that the finding came from a trial court whose directions are stayed. 3) benefit.amountCr=1400 is gross reimbursement, not a proven net gain. Keep confidence at "estimated" and add that the figure is a stayed trial-court finding. 4) c033's from date "2025-07-14" is not supported by this source, which gives no exact judgment or stay date. Mark it approximate or source it from the HC order. 5) Record the denial as "none found; the source does not say whether Adani/PKCL were asked". 6) upgradeIf: open the Scroll.in original, which may include a request for Adani's comment, and the judgment PDF.

verdicts.dateTest: NTPC (the awarder) awarded import-coal supply contracts to Adani Enterprises in two rounds in 2022. The article (Shreya Jai, Business Standard, last updated 6 Jun 2022) covers the June round and says the March tenders were ISSUED in March: "In March, when the coal crisis erupted, NTPC had issued five tenders for importing 5.75 mt of coal, and all the contracts went to Adani Enterprises." It gives no award date for the March round, so "awarded ... in Mar 2022" is not supported. The awards probably came in Mar–May 2022. The June award was reported on 4–6 Jun 2022. Both fall inside the Union power ministry's 10% blending directive of 2022 and inside the edge window (from 2022-03-01, to 2022-06-30). This is an institution-to-institution award, so there is no tenure mismatch. The date test passes, but the March date should read "tenders issued Mar 2022", not "awarded Mar 2022".
verdicts.identityTest: Both ends are unambiguous. NTPC Ltd is the state-owned generator the source names: "India's largest power generating company (genco) NTPC". Adani Enterprises Ltd is named directly in the source, not a different Adani entity such as Adani Power or Adani Global. The other technical bidders (Adi Tradelink, Chettinad Logistics, Mohit Minerals) are named correctly. There is no name-collision risk. Passes.
verdicts.baseRate: Reference class: NTPC's 2022 import tenders that were reported. Adani won all 5 of 5 in March, and the source only says "multiple contracts" for the 6 in June. Of the 4 technical bidders, AEL is the only one reported winning. So within NTPC the pattern discriminates: one of four bidders took everything. But the denominator is incomplete. The source says NTPC was ordering "close to 20 mt" in total, while these two rounds come to 12 mt. How the rest was split, and the L1 prices per tonne, are not public. Across PSU buyers the pattern does not hold. CIL's July 2022 medium-term tender went to PT Bara Daya over AEL (c043), so the rate among central-PSU buyers is 2 of 3 rounds, not 100%. AEL is India's largest thermal-coal trader and importer, so it winning a high share of large volume-and-logistics tenders is expected. Publish the denominator as: NTPC 11 tenders reported, at least 5 confirmed all-AEL; about 12 of about 20 mt; CIL medium-term lost.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Not asked: the Business Standard article carries no comment from NTPC or Adani Enterprises and does not say either was contacted. The article only notes NTPC executives' earlier remark that the coal would come from Indonesia, not Australia. Record this as "no response sought in source". (The web-search budget was used up during this check, so a later NTPC or AEL statement cannot be ruled out.)
verdicts.innocentReading: The Union power ministry ordered gencos to blend 10% imported coal before the monsoon, which forced a rush of short-tender imports. In that setting, the largest Indian coal trader, with established Indonesian supply contracts and port and logistics assets, could plausibly be L1 in every lot, while smaller traders (Adi Tradelink, Mohit Minerals, Chettinad) might have failed on price or volume. The cost burden (fuel at Rs 7–8/unit against Rs 2 for CIL coal) comes from the mandate and global prices, which the source says were about 5 times CIL-notified prices. It is not evidence of an above-market AEL price, because no per-tonne L1 price has been published.
verdicts.reason: The one cited source, a credible outlet with a named reporter (Shreya Jai, Business Standard, Jun 2022), confirms the core edge almost word for word. It confirms the NTPC→AEL award, 6.25 mt for Rs 8,308 cr, the earlier 5.75 mt for Rs 8,422 cr with "all the contracts went to Adani Enterprises", four technical bidders "the same ... as in the latest round", and the power ministry's 10% blending directive. That clears the "reported" bar. It does not clear "documented": there is one outlet and no NTPC award notice. The claim survives, but three statements go beyond the source. (a) "all import tenders ... Jun 2022": the source says "all" only for March. For June it says NTPC "awarded multiple contracts" out of six tenders, and NTPC was procuring about 20 mt, so AEL did not get all of NTPC's imports. (b) "awarded in Mar 2022": the source says the tenders were issued in March. (c) "Beneficiary Adani ~Rs 16,730 cr": this is gross contract value (8,422 + 8,308), not benefit or margin.
verdicts.corrections: text: change "NTPC awarded all import tenders in Mar 2022 ... and Jun 2022" to "All five NTPC import tenders issued Mar 2022 (5.75 mt, Rs 8,422 cr) went to AEL; in the Jun 2022 round (six tenders) NTPC awarded multiple contracts for 6.25 mt (Rs 8,308 cr) to AEL". Change "Beneficiary Adani ~Rs 16,730 cr" to "gross contract value to AEL ~Rs 16,730 cr (not margin)". Add the denominator: "NTPC was procuring ~20 mt in total; the allocation of the remainder is not reported". The `d` field already phrases June correctly; keep it and fix the March wording to "issued". benefit.confidence: keep "estimated" but relabel amountCr as gross revenue. Also note in benefit.how that the Rs 7–8/unit cost comes from the mandate and global prices, not an AEL premium. Add denial: "none; source records no comment sought from NTPC or AEL". Add innocentReading: largest coal trader, L1 on price under an urgent mandate. upgradeIf is fine (award notices and L1 per-tonne prices). Add to killIf: "Award notices show June tenders split among bidders, or AEL price above rival bids not being L1".

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the edge says: DRI (s) enforced against Adani Enterprises (t) over 2019-01-01 to 2021-08-31. That window is the FT's own sample of 30 shipments. It is not a DRI enforcement window. Per Reuters via Business Today, DRI's probe began in 2014. It sought Singapore documents from 2016, the Bombay HC quashed the Letters Rogatory in 2019, the SC stayed that in Jan 2020, and DRI filed on 9 Oct 2023. Neither source says DRI examined any 2019-21 cargo. The d field also contains an internal conflict: the FT's $4.8bn paid to the three intermediaries runs "since July 2021", which is mostly after the edge's end date of 2021-08-31. Dates for the facts themselves check out: FT story Oct 2023 (ThePrint, the Thursday after Adani's Monday 9 Oct preemptive statement), Reuters/BT 17 Nov 2023. The edge's date range belongs to a different actor.
verdicts.identityTest: Partially holds. ThePrint links the allegation to Adani Enterprises: "would mean that Adani Enterprises over-paid for imported coal". Business Today/Reuters only says "an Adani company" and "Adani Group companies", and names Adani Global Pte (Singapore). It does not name Adani Enterprises as the respondent in the DRI Supreme Court filing. The 2016 circular named five Adani companies, not just AEL. There is no name-collision risk. However, the source node energy:dri is the wrong actor for the FT findings. The FT, not DRI, compiled the 30-shipment, $139m-to-$215m analysis.
verdicts.baseRate: The DRI 2016 circular named 40 importers, 5 of them Adani companies (about 12.5%), so being under DRI's coal-valuation probe is not unique to Adani. The FT sample was chosen by the FT and covers Adani only. No comparison of the same Indonesia-declared vs India-declared values for other large importers (Tata, Essar, JSW, NTPC traders) is in hand, so there is no base rate for how big the export/import gap is. Mirror-trade gaps between Indonesian export declarations and importer declarations are common across the coal trade. A 52% gap on 30 hand-picked cargoes does not discriminate until the same test is run on rival importers. Symmetry: the lens was not applied to rival importers. Adani explicitly complains that the FT "singled out" the group from DRI's list of 40.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. Adani Group's preemptive statement (Mon 9 Oct 2023), quoted by ThePrint (https://theprint.in/business/adani-group-overpaid-for-coal-imports-then-charged-indians-extra-for-power-claims-ft-report/1801571/): "old and baseless allegations", "a clever recycling and selective misrepresentation of publicly available facts", "the issue of overvaluation in the import of coal was conclusively settled by India's highest court of law", and "false and baseless". Business Today/Reuters (https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/dri-seeks-permission-to-restart-probe-into-adani-group-over-overvaluation-of-coal-imports-report-406047-2023-11-17): Adani "had 'fully co-operated' with the authorities by providing details and documents sought more than four years ago." Both are already recorded as c046. MoP general statement (c047, PIB 1983084): regulators will not pass through inflated fuel costs. This was not a direct answer to the FT.
verdicts.innocentReading: The gap may come from the Indonesian side. Indonesian export declarations are often understated relative to invoices, for example through benchmark (HBA/HPB) royalty-based declarations, under-reporting by miners, or grade and calorific-value differences. Normal intermediary trading adds further margin: credit terms, demurrage, blending and quality risk. None of this requires inflated Indian import values. Separately, many Adani power PPAs (e.g. Mundra) were Section-63 competitively bid tariffs, where fuel cost is not simply passed through invoice-for-invoice. Regulators (CERC/SERC) check fuel-cost claims. So the Rs 12,000 cr "consumer cost" is a political estimate, not a finding. The DRI probe also named 39 other importers and has not produced an adjudicated finding against Adani.
verdicts.reason: The facts in the text are confirmed by the sources. ThePrint quotes the FT: 30 sailings, 3.1 mt, $139m + $3.1m vs $215m, $73m, 52%, Hi Lingos/Taurus/Pan Asia, $4.8bn since Jul 2021. Business Today/Reuters has the 1,300 shipments, the 9 Oct DRI filing, Rahul Gandhi's "Rs 12,000 crore" quote and Adani's "fully co-operated". The problem is the edge's structure. It is keyed s=energy:dri, pred=enforce, from/to 2019-2021, which states that DRI enforced against Adani Enterprises over FT's 2019-21 sample window. No source says that. The FT analysis is journalism. DRI's 1,300-shipment probe dates from 2014/2016 and concerns an earlier import period. The Rahul Gandhi figure is a politician's claim. Putting these three together under a DRI enforcement edge implies an official finding on 2019-21 cargoes that none of them makes. It also duplicates c044, which has the same s/t/pred and is the correct documented DRI edge. As an attributed FT/Gandhi allegation with the c046/c047 contras, "alleged" is the right tier. The edge as keyed does not stand.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change s from energy:dri to a media/accuser node (e.g. media:financial-times; Rahul Gandhi/INC as a second asserting party). Use a non-enforcement predicate for the allegation, or make it a narrative claim attached to c044 rather than a separate DRI->AEL enforce edge. 2) If the edge stays under DRI, dates must be from 2014/2016 per c044, not 2019-01-01 to 2021-08-31. The 2019-21 window must be labelled as the FT sample period only. 3) Drop "DRI filing covers 1,300 shipments" from the FT sentence, or say explicitly that DRI's 1,300 shipments come from its own pre-2016 probe and are separate from the FT's 30 cargoes. Reuters wording: "Indian authorities have reviewed 1,300 shipments... alleged in court filings that it 'grossly overstated'". 4) Fix the internal date conflict: the $4.8bn "since July 2021" runs past to=2021-08-31. Either drop it or date it separately. 5) Target: note that ThePrint names Adani Enterprises but Reuters names only "an Adani company"/Adani Global Pte, so t should be co:adani-enterprises with the caveat "FT/ThePrint attribution". 6) Make it explicit that the Rs 12,000 cr is Rahul Gandhi's political claim, with no methodology given. 7) Keep tier=alleged. The contras c046 (Adani denial) and c047 (MoP) are present and satisfy the spec.

verdicts.dateTest: Passes. Hindenburg Research (active 2017 until its closure on 15 Jan 2025) published its Adani report on 24 Jan 2023, inside its operating window. Adani's rebuttal came on 29 Jan 2023; the SEBI Adicorp order is quoted as saying "corporate announcement dated January 29, 2023". The SEBI Adicorp final order is dated 18 Sep 2025 (it reads "DATE: September 18, 2025" and is digitally signed by Varshney on 2025.09.18). The settlement order is dated 22 Sep 2026 (Business Standard: "the settlement order dated September 22 noted"; the related show-cause notice (SCN) is dated February 15, 2024). Every date in the text matches its source.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes, with no risk of name collision. The source node is Hindenburg Research (Nathan Anderson), a US short-seller. The SEBI order names the 24 Jan 2023 Hindenburg report and the Adani noticees with their PANs: APSEZ AAACG7917K, Adani Power AABCA2957L, Adicorp AAACB7826J, Gautam Adani ABKPA0965H and Rajesh Adani ABKPA0962A. The target is the group node grp:adani, which is correct for a report aimed at the whole group. One schema quibble: SPEC defines 'enforce' as agency→subject, and a short-seller is not an agency. SPEC does list short-sellers as valid 'alleged' sources, so this is tolerable, but the label should make clear it is a private report and not a proceeding.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a base-rate edge. It records a single named party's specific allegation. Hindenburg's targets were in many countries (Nikola, Icahn, Block, Super Micro, Carvana as its final report), so singling out Adani was not India-specific. Across roughly 24 SEBI investigations, only three proceedings have a published outcome: two orders finding no violation (18 Sep 2025) and one settlement (22 Sep 2026). A fourth Hindenburg-adjacent settlement, PMC Projects (Karan Adani and CFO, Rs 13.65 lakh each, 10 Sep 2026), is not mentioned. The denominator of published outcomes is therefore about 3 to 4 out of 24, not "all but the 24th".
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindenburg_Research) says the group accused Hindenburg of "a calculated attack" on India, and Hindenburg replied that Adani "dodged key questions". The SEBI Adicorp order (https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/sep-2025/order_matter_adicorp.pdf) quotes Adani's 29 Jan 2023 exchange filing: "Adicorp is not a related party, and transactions with Adicorp are not 'related party transactions' under laws of Indian or accounting standards". The Fortune source does NOT contain the "calculated attack on India" quote, so the c002 citation of Fortune for that phrase is unsupported. Wikipedia is the only listed support for it.
verdicts.innocentReading: A short-seller with a disclosed short position has a financial interest in the price falling. SEBI's own orders say the RPT transactions were not "related party transactions" under the pre-2021 definition, and that the 2021 LODR amendment applied only going forward. On that reading this is a regulatory-definition gap, not concealment, and the Supreme Court's expert committee said it was not a regulatory failure. The settlement is a standard s.15JB settlement with no finding of guilt, for Rs 1.51 cr, covering an FY13 disclosure lapse and auditor peer-review certificate lapses.
verdicts.reason:
The core edge holds and is correctly tiered as alleged. Hindenburg did publish on 24 Jan 2023 that the group "has engaged in a brazen stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme over the course of decades" (Wikipedia verbatim), and the required denial exists as contra c002. The appended status summary is the weak part, because it chains true facts into an implication none of the sources makes.

(a) The allegation headlined is "stock manipulation via offshore shells". The proceedings cited as closing it are RPT-classification cases: Adicorp, Milestone/Rehvar and Vakoder. The offshore-shell/FPI beneficial-ownership and price-manipulation strands have no published outcome. Fortune itself says "the regulator's orders do not clear the ports-to-power conglomerate of other allegations raised by the short seller".

(b) "Both public SEBI RPT strands" is miscounted. On 18 Sep 2025 there were two separate orders, Adicorp (confirmed in the primary PDF) and Milestone/Rehvar (Fortune: "two orders"), plus the 22 Sep 2026 settlement. That is three published RPT outcomes, not two.

(c) The settlement was not purely an RPT matter. Business Standard says it also covered audit and limited-review reports for 2015–2021 "signed ... without a valid peer review certificate".

(d) "The 24th SEBI probe's outcome is unpublished" implies the other 23 have published outcomes. SEBI said 23 were "complete" (Business Standard, 11 Aug 2024), which means the investigations finished, not that outcomes were published. Most outcomes are not public.

(e) None of the claim's three srcs supports the Rs 1.51 cr settlement or the 24th-probe status. Those facts rest on the Business Standard 2026 and 2024 URLs, which are not in srcs. I confirmed the Business Standard 22 Sep 2026 article by curl (WebFetch returned 403): "Five Adani group companies have settled adjudication proceedings ... for a cumulative amount of ₹1.51 crore".

None of these problems breaks the edge, but the text must be fixed before publication.
verdicts.corrections:
1. text: replace "Both public SEBI RPT strands later closed with no violation (18 Sep 2025) and a Rs 1.51 cr no-fault settlement (22 Sep 2026)" with "SEBI's published RPT proceedings ended in two no-violation orders on 18 Sep 2025 (Adicorp; Milestone/Rehvar) and a Rs 1.51 cr settlement on 22 Sep 2026 without admission of guilt (FY13 Vakoder RPT disclosure plus auditor peer-review lapses)".
2. text: replace "the 24th SEBI probe's outcome is unpublished" with "outcomes of the offshore-fund/FPI beneficial-ownership and price-manipulation strands, and of most of the 24 investigations SEBI said were complete or near-complete (11 Aug 2024), have not been published". Also add Fortune's caveat that the orders "do not clear" the group of other allegations.
3. srcs: add https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/sebi-settles-proceedings-against-5-adani-firms-over-disclosure-violations-126092200998_1.html for the Rs 1.51 cr figure and https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/hindenburg-row-sebi-breaks-silence-only-1-probe-remaining-on-adani-group-124081100495_1.html for the probe count.
4. c002: Fortune does not contain the "calculated attack on India" quote. Keep Wikipedia as the source and add the SEBI Adicorp order PDF, which quotes Adani's 29 Jan 2023 exchange filing.
5. killIf: the RPT closures (c004, c005, c006) do not address the stock-manipulation/offshore-shell core, so they should be listed as partial and not counted toward the kill condition.
6. Optional: consider mentioning the PMC Projects settlement (c007, 10 Sep 2026) as a further published Hindenburg-adjacent outcome.
7. Optional: change the lab to "Hindenburg short report (private allegation)" to mark that the 'enforce' predicate here comes from a non-agency source.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is that Hindenburg Research published a post on 10 Aug 2024 accusing SEBI chair Madhabi Puri Buch and her husband Dhaval Buch of conflicts. Hindenburg's own post (hindenburgresearch.com/sebi-chairperson/) is dated 10 August 2024. Buch was a SEBI whole-time member from Apr 2017 to Oct 2021 and chair from 2 Mar 2022 to 28 Feb 2025, so the post falls inside her term as chair. One caveat: the alleged GDOF/IPE Plus fund stake dates from 2015, before she joined SEBI, and the Buchs say they redeemed it in 2018. So "SEBI chair ... held stakes" does not mean she held them while she was chair. The contra dates check out: SEBI's statement is dated 11 Aug 2024 (Business Standard, published 11 Aug 2024, 7:27 PM IST), and LiveLaw confirms the Lokpal common order of 28 May 2025 on complaints dated 13 Aug, 11 Sep and 8 Oct 2024.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. Madhabi Puri Buch is named by office in every source. Hindenburg Research is the short-seller founded by Nate Anderson, which closed in Jan 2025. Neither party has a name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable. This is a single, specific allegation by a named party, not a property shared across a group of comparable entities. On symmetry: no other SEBI chair has faced a comparable short-seller allegation. Recusal plus disclosure is the standard SEBI conflict framework and applies to all members.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, two denials are on the record, and both are already attached as contras. (1) SEBI's statement of 11 Aug 2024 (Business Standard): "It is noted that relevant disclosures required in terms of holdings of securities and their transfers have been made by the chairperson from time to time. The chairperson has also recused herself in matters involving potential conflicts of interest." SEBI called the Blackstone/REIT favouritism allegation "inappropriate". https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/hindenburg-row-sebi-breaks-silence-only-1-probe-remaining-on-adani-group-124081100495_1.html (2) Wikipedia records that "The couple later denied the claims." (3) The Lokpal order of 28 May 2025 found "no material suggesting quid pro quo or conflict of interest" and called the complaints "untenable, unsubstantiated and bordering on frivolity" (LiveLaw).
verdicts.innocentReading: The Buchs invested in the IPE Plus fund in 2015 as private citizens, before Madhabi joined SEBI. Their account is that the fund's CIO was a personal friend and that they exited in 2018. Their holdings were disclosed to SEBI, and she recused herself where there was a conflict. Dhaval Buch's Blackstone advisory role was in supply-chain work, not real estate. SEBI's REIT rule changes were board or institutional decisions reached through public consultation. The Lokpal accepted this reading and dismissed the complaints.
verdicts.reason: The claim text survives. It correctly attributes an unproven allegation to a named party, Hindenburg, on the right date (10 Aug 2024, confirmed by Hindenburg's own post). Every source supports the part of the claim it is cited for. Wikipedia says the report accused Buch and her husband "of having a stake in dubious offshore entities used to artificially inflate shares of companies owned by the Adani Group". Hindenburg's post names "GDOF Cell 90 (IPEplus Fund 1)" and says Agora Advisory "generated INR 19.8 million (U.S. $261,000) revenue from consulting", which supports the "consulting-fee conflicts" wording. The claim also carries two contras, a SEBI denial and a Lokpal dismissal, so the 'alleged' tier meets the SPEC. The problem is in the record's 'd' field. It says Hindenburg's 10 Aug post alleged that Dhaval Buch received "~Rs 4.78 crore from Mahindra and Blackstone". The fetched Hindenburg post does not mention Mahindra or Rs 4.78 crore. From memory rather than a source retrieved here, the Rs 4.78 crore Mahindra figure comes from a separate Congress allegation (Pawan Khera, around 10 Sep 2024), and Mahindra denied it. That misattribution must be fixed, but the edge itself does not need to be killed.
verdicts.corrections: (1) In 'd', remove "Dhaval Buch received consulting fees (~Rs 4.78 crore from Mahindra and Blackstone)" from the Hindenburg allegation. Replace it with what Hindenburg actually alleged: Agora Advisory (India), 99% owned by Madhabi Buch, earned INR 19.8 million ($261k) in consulting revenue while she was at SEBI; Agora Partners (Singapore) was transferred to her husband; and Dhaval Buch was appointed senior advisor to Blackstone in July 2019, which coincided with SEBI REIT changes. If the Mahindra Rs 4.78 crore allegation is kept, move it to a separate edge attributed to Congress/Pawan Khera (Sep 2024) with Mahindra's denial as its contra, after a source for it has been retrieved. (2) Change the predicate. The SPEC defines 'enforce' as agency→subject, and Hindenburg is a short-seller, not an enforcement agency. Relabel the edge as an allegation, or document that 'enforce' is used for private accusers under the 'alleged' tier. (3) Add a clarification that the alleged fund stake dates to 2015–2018, before Buch became chair, so "SEBI chair ... held stakes" is not read as a holding during her term as chair. (4) c011's evidence field (lab "Buch/SEBI denial") holds only the SEBI institutional statement. Add a source for the Buchs' personal joint statement of 11 Aug 2024.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is: OCCRP published, on 31 Aug 2023, an allegation that two investors held 8% to nearly 14% of the free float of four Adani companies at their peak in Jun 2016. OCCRP was operating in Aug 2023, and the 2016 holding window falls inside the period the leaked records cover. The edge's 'from' of 2023-08-31 matches the publication date, and the SC's 3 Jan 2024 characterisation and the 16 Jul 2024 review dismissal come after it. The chronology is consistent and nothing collapses.
verdicts.identityTest: Source node energy:occrp is the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project, and the AIR article names it in full. The target grp:adani is the group. The four companies OCCRP names are Adani Power, Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports and Adani Transmission. The two investors are Nasser Ali Shaban Ahli and Chang Chung-Ling. They are not nodes in this edge, so there is no name-collision risk. Vinod Adani is named by OCCRP as signing the 2011 Excel advisory agreement.
verdicts.baseRate: Holding Indian equities through Mauritius FPIs was very common in 2016, so the Mauritius route alone does not discriminate. What does discriminate is that two individuals with documented director and shareholder ties to the promoter family held between 8% and nearly 14% of the free float of four listed companies in the same group, through funds that took advisory instructions from a promoter-family company. That is rare and specific. On symmetry: the same lens applied to a rival group would need comparable leaked fund records, and none were examined. This affects how much weight the claim carries, not whether it is true.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. Adani Group, 31 Aug 2023: "We categorically reject these recycled allegations. These news reports appear to be yet another concerted bid by Soros-funded interests supported by a section of the foreign media to revive the meritless Hindenburg report... we reject these reports in their entirety." The group said the claims rest on DRI over-invoicing cases closed a decade earlier, which reached finality in the SC in March 2023. Source: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/adani-group-rejects-recycled-allegations-made-by-george-soros-funded-occrp/articleshow/103230293.cms . OCCRP's own article quotes Adani calling the allegations "baseless and unsubstantiated" and saying the listed entities "are in compliance with all applicable laws including the regulation relating to public share holdings". It also reports that Chang told the Guardian he "knew nothing about any secret purchases", and that Ahli and Vinod Adani did not respond. Everyone was asked. The existing contra edge enforce:c014 (the SC characterisation) also stands.
verdicts.innocentReading: Ahli and Chang may be independent foreign investors who used their own money (OCCRP concedes "There is no evidence that Chang and Ahli's money for their Adani Group investments came from the Adani family. The source of the funds is unknown"). An advisory contract with an Excel/Vinod Adani entity would not by itself make them promoter-group 'persons acting in concert' under the minimum-public-shareholding rules. The SC held that such third-party reports are not conclusive proof. SEBI's FPI beneficial-ownership inquiry is the arbiter, and this file does not record an adverse finding from it.
verdicts.reason: The substance survives against the primary OCCRP article (https://www.occrp.org/en/investigations/documents-provide-fresh-insight-into-allegations-of-stock-manipulation-that-rocked-indias-powerful-adani-group). It says: "at the peak of their investment in June 2016, the two funds held free-floating shares of four Adani Group companies ranging from 8 to nearly 14 percent", the two men have "close ties to the Adani family", and "there is evidence that Chang and Ahli's trading in Adani stock was coordinated with the family". 'Alleged' is the right tier: OCCRP is the named asserting party, and there is a contra (SC c014, plus the Adani denial found here). The edge's weakness is its sourcing. The only cited source, AIR News, confirms only that OCCRP issued a report and that the SC said such reports "cannot be regarded as conclusive proof". It says nothing about Mauritius, the two investors, the 8–14% figure or June 2016, which is why sourceCheck is 'partially'. This can be fixed by citing the primary OCCRP URL. It is not a reason to kill the edge.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add to srcs the primary OCCRP URL (https://www.occrp.org/en/investigations/documents-provide-fresh-insight-into-allegations-of-stock-manipulation-that-rocked-indias-powerful-adani-group). Keep AIR only as the source for the SC characterisation. 2) Change the wording "up to 8–14% free float" to "between 8% and nearly 14% of the free float of each of four Adani companies (Adani Power, Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Adani Transmission) at the Jun 2016 peak". 3) Add OCCRP's own caveat to the edge text: "no evidence the money came from the Adani family; source of funds unknown". Also state the coordination evidence precisely: the funds received instructions from Excel, a company controlled by Vinod Adani, which signed the 2011 advisory agreement. 4) Delete the gap note ("Adani's rejection statement not opened"). Add a contra edge grp:adani -> claim:enforce:c013 quoting the 31 Aug 2023 "categorically reject these recycled allegations... reject these reports in their entirety" statement (ET URL above). Update the gaps entry at line ~2816 of research/raw/energy/enforce.json. 5) Change the energy:occrp node's d-string tag from "[documented]" to show that only the SC quote is documented. The OCCRP allegation itself is 'alleged'.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Financial Times reported ~$5bn in over-priced coal imports routed through offshore intermediaries, 2023 ('from' 2023-10-12). Separately, FT with OCCRP documents reported that 2014 TANGEDCO shipments were upgraded on paper and re-priced, published 22 May 2024. The dates fit: Adani Global Pte was the supplier to TANGEDCO in Jan–Oct 2014, and Newslaundry dates the FT story to 'last year' relative to May 2024. The opened source does not give the month 'Oct' or the 12 Oct date, so that date rests on outside knowledge. The period of the $5bn figure is in doubt. Newslaundry says '2021-2023'. My recollection, which I could not check because FT is paywalled and unfetchable, is that FT's figure covered roughly 2019–2021. The claim text leaves the period out and flags the gap, which is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: No problem with name collisions. The source names 'the Adani Group' for the $5bn and 'Adani Global Pte Ltd' as TANGEDCO's supplier in 2014. TANGEDCO is the Tamil Nadu state utility. Pointing the edge at the group node grp:adani is acceptable. A more precise version would name Adani Global Pte Ltd, the Singapore trading arm, as the supplier in the 2014 shipments.
verdicts.baseRate: The DRI's 2016 coal over-valuation probe covered about 40 importers, including Essar, Reliance ADAG entities and JSW, so over-invoicing of Indonesian coal imports was an industry-wide allegation. Being a subject of the DRI case would not single Adani out. This claim is narrower: FT and OCCRP published shipment-level documents specific to Adani (the MV Kalliopi L and at least 24 other 2014 shipments). The DRI's symmetrical lens would produce similar edges for rival importers, but the FT/OCCRP document trail is Adani-specific.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and the claim records it (contra c016). Newslaundry (22 May 2024) quotes Adani calling the allegations "false and baseless" and saying "The suggestion that Adani Global Pte Ltd supplied to TANGEDCO inferior coal...is incorrect"; Adani said the coal was tested at multiple points. TANGEDCO "did not respond to questions sent by OCCRP" (asked, no reply). Source: https://www.newslaundry.com/2024/05/22/new-evidence-bolsters-allegations-adani-group-overcharged-for-coal
verdicts.innocentReading: Coal quality and price can legitimately differ between supplier invoices and the final delivery, for example through blending, re-testing at the load or discharge port, or bundled freight, insurance and trading margins. Adani says independent agencies tested the coal at several points. Intermediary markups are normal in commodity trading. The DRI case has not been decided on its merits: the Bombay High Court blocked it in 2019 and it is pending before the Supreme Court. No court or adjudicator has found over-invoicing.
verdicts.reason: The opened source says what the claim says. Newslaundry quotes FT as reporting that Adani 'appears to have paid over $5 billion to middlemen for coal imported far in excess of market prices'. It also says 'at least 24 other shipments ... between January and October 2014 were originally priced as low-quality coal but ultimately sold by Adani to the local state power company for triple the cost', with grades 'below 3500' against '6,000 kcal/kg' and prices '$28 per metric ton' against 'US$91.91 per metric ton'. The claim is attributed to named parties (FT/OCCRP), is unproven, and carries a documented contra (c016). That meets the 'alleged' bar exactly. It is not a conjunction problem because every element is stated in one source. It is not documented, because there is no adjudication, filing or court finding on the substance. sourceCheck is 'partially' for three reasons: the FT original could not be opened, the Oct 2023 date is not in the opened source, and the secondary source's period for the $5bn figure ('2021-2023') probably does not match FT's.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Keep the $5bn period out of the claim text until the FT original is checked. If a period is added, check it against FT (my unverified recollection is roughly 2019–2021), not Newslaundry's '2021-2023'. (2) Add a source that supports from=2023-10-12, since the opened source only says 'last year'. Better still, add the OCCRP 2024 piece as a second source for the 2014 TANGEDCO data. (3) 'Re-graded ... in transit' is our own gloss. Reword to 'invoiced by the intermediary as <3,500 kcal/kg and by Adani to TANGEDCO as 6,000 kcal/kg'. (4) Optionally name Adani Global Pte Ltd as the supplier in the 2014 shipments. (5) Modelling note: FT is a newspaper, not an enforcement agency. 'enforce' only fits under a loose reading of 'investigation'. Consider linking this claim to the DRI enforce edge and treating FT as the reporter.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: DRI opened a coal over-invoicing probe (2016 notice/circular), Adani won in Bombay HC in 2019 (IE/NDTV Profit, 17 Oct 2019), DRI appealed to SC, and the next hearing was listed "August 6". The article is dated 22 May 2024, so 6 Aug 2024 is a reasonable inference, though the source gives no year. The dates are internally consistent. One gap: ThePrint (Oct 2023, already cited in coal.json) says the SC stayed the Bombay HC order in Jan 2020, "effectively restarting the investigation". A CNBC-TV18 headline of 8 Jan 2020 also says "Supreme Court stays Bombay High Court relief on DRI plea." The claim skips this step, so "blocked by Bombay HC 2019" is presented as the settled position without mention of the stay. The Reuters/Business Today piece of Nov 2023 and OCCRP/Newslaundry of May 2024 both still describe the evidence route as blocked, so the reporting conflicts but the claim does not collapse. "from 2016-01-01" is approximate: the source says "nearly a decade ago" and cites "a 2016 notice".
verdicts.identityTest: "grp:adani" is a group-level node, but the litigant in Bombay HC was Adani Enterprises Ltd (IE: "Bombay HC rules in favour of Adani Enterprises"). The overseas records sought belonged to Adani Global Pte (Singapore). The source only says "Adani Group" and "Adani". There is no name-collision risk. Pointing the edge at the group is acceptable, but the d-field should name Adani Enterprises as the respondent. DRI (Finance Ministry) is correctly identified.
verdicts.baseRate: This was not an Adani-specific probe. DRI's 2016 circular named 40 importers, five of them Adani companies (ThePrint), and Newslaundry calls it an "industry-wide case". Essar and others were in the same net, and the Delhi HC CBI order of Dec 2023 named Adani and Essar. Cases pending in the Supreme Court for 5 or more years are routine given the SC backlog, and DRI adjudications commonly take years. So "pending and unresolved" does not by itself single Adani out. What does stand out is the documented litigation to block letters rogatory, and the report that Adani took about 3 years to file a counter-affidavit.
verdicts.denialFound: Adani Group was asked. In its Oct 2023 pre-emptive statement it said the SC had in Jan 2023 "dismissed as withdrawn" DRI's appeal, with the observation "we appreciate the stand taken by the Government in not entering into futile litigation". It added: "Clearly, the issue of overvaluation in the import of coal was conclusively settled by India's highest court of law." Source: https://theprint.in/business/adani-group-overpaid-for-coal-imports-then-charged-indians-extra-for-power-claims-ft-report/1801571/. The repo's coal.json records that the Jan 2023 withdrawal was a different matter (Knowledge Infrastructure). Also on the record: Adani denies wrongdoing and says Indian customs assessed the shipments before release (Business Today/Reuters, 17 Nov 2023). In the source article, OCCRP asked Adani, and the spokesperson called the allegations "false and baseless". Against Adani's "settled" position, Parliament was told in Mar 2023 that the DRI investigation had not concluded (The Hindu, 13 Mar 2023).
verdicts.innocentReading: The Bombay HC quashed the letters rogatory on procedural grounds ("due process had not been followed"). That was a due-process ruling on a sovereign request for evidence, not a finding on the merits. Contesting such requests is normal for any defendant, and in the SC backlog appeals routinely sit for years. The lack of a conclusion reflects litigation delay across a 40-importer industry probe, not proof that anyone suppressed the case. Adani's position is that the SC has already settled the matter.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the core facts. Newslaundry/OCCRP, 22 May 2024: "the probe was prevented from progressing in 2019 after Adani won a case in Bombay's High Court that blocked the DRI from seeking details about shipments... from abroad. The DRI then appealed to India's Supreme Court, where the case has languished without progress" and "The next hearing is scheduled for August 6." That is one credible outlet relying on published documents, which meets the "reported" bar. The Mar 2023 parliamentary reply that the investigation was "not concluded" corroborates the non-conclusion. Google News checks for 2024–Sep 2026 surfaced no SC order or DRI adjudication, so "no outcome located" holds as an absence finding. It is ours, though, and not in the source. The claim survives, but only as a partial source match with fixes needed. It leaves out the Jan 2020 SC stay, it leaves out Adani's contra that the matter was "conclusively settled", and its closing line "an investigation opened and never concluded" goes beyond the evidence: the correct wording is "no conclusion located", not "never concluded".
verdicts.corrections: (1) text: replace "an investigation opened and never concluded" with "no SC order or DRI adjudication located to Sep 2026". (2) text/d: add "SC stayed the Bombay HC order in Jan 2020 (ThePrint, Oct 2023); DRI in Oct 2023 again asked the SC to allow Singapore evidence collection". (3) d: name Adani Enterprises Ltd as the Bombay HC petitioner and Adani Global Pte as the holder of the records sought. (4) d: note the probe was industry-wide (40 importers, 5 Adani companies). (5) Add a contra edge from grp:adani to claim:enforce:c017 carrying the Oct 2023 "conclusively settled by India's highest court" statement (ThePrint URL), with the note that the Jan 2023 withdrawal related to a different matter. (6) Add corroborating sources: Business Today/Reuters 17 Nov 2023 (https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/dri-seeks-permission-to-restart-probe-into-adani-group-over-overvaluation-of-coal-imports-report-406047-2023-11-17) and The Hindu 13 Mar 2023 parliamentary reply that the DRI probe was not concluded. (7) Mark "6 Aug 2024" as year inferred from the article date, since the source says only "August 6". (8) "from": the 2016 date is right for the circular; keep it but label it approximate.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out: RECPDCL (the bid process coordinator the Ministry of Power appointed by Gazette No. 221, dated 13.1.2023) issued the LoI to AESL on 3 Dec 2024. The claim says 4 Dec, which is wrong. T&D India, the cited source, published on 4 Dec and says: "RECPDCL issued the letter of intent to Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (AESL) on December 3, 2024." CERC Order 252/TL/2025 (para 13) agrees: "a Letter of Intent (LoI) was issued to Adani Energy Solutions Limited by the BPC on 3.12.2024". The rest of the timeline holds. RfP first issued 11.7.2023. First-round price bids opened 29 May 2024, PGCIL L1 (T&D India, 1 Aug 2024). Annulment reported 19 Aug 2024. RfP re-published 17.8.2024. Re-bid technical bids opened 8.10.2024 and initial price offers 27.11.2024. The e-reverse auction on 28.11.2024 had no participants. BEC report dated 2.12.2024. SPV acquired and effective date 20.1.2025. The sequence has no tenure or ownership overlap problem.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass, with one correction. The winner is Adani Energy Solutions Ltd (formerly Adani Transmission Ltd), which is how CERC 252/TL/2025 names it. It won through the SPV Rajasthan Part-I Power Transmission Ltd. The re-bid's Sterlite entity was "Sterlite Grid 37 Limited" (Sterlite Power, now Resonia). The IndiGrid entity was "IndiGrid 2 Limited". The awarding end is misassigned. The LoI came from RECPDCL, the BPC and a subsidiary of REC Ltd (node co:rec-limited). The Ministry of Power only notified the BPC and the scheme. There is no name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: The re-bid drew four bidders, and all four qualified for e-RA. The three private initial offers sat within 1.6% of each other: AESL Rs 35,570 mn (L1), Sterlite Grid 37 Rs 35,600 mn (L2), IndiGrid 2 Rs 36,150 mn (L3). PGCIL came last at Rs 40,820 mn (L4) (CERC 252/TL/2025, para 10–11). No bidder took part in the reverse auction, so the lowest initial offer won. That is a normal outcome in a competitive TBCB round, not a pattern that singles anyone out. The annulment was not a one-off aimed at one bidder either. CERC 341/AT/2024 (19 Dec 2024) records the same BPC's BEC applying discretion both ways. It annulled this scheme because the L1 price was too high. On the same logic it went ahead with Khavda Ph-IV Part C for Sterlite Grid 38 at 37.29% above estimate, and records another discovered tariff at 97.27% above the assessed figure, on grounds of "urgency". Viewed the same way, that discretion benefited Sterlite in the other case, not Adani.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial or statement from AESL, PGCIL, RECPDCL or the Ministry of Power found. verdicts.innocentReading: PGCIL's first-round L1 quote (about Rs 37,000 mn/yr according to T&D India's paywalled explainer, as surfaced in search) was 55.41% above the CERC-norm estimate. The BEC therefore recommended annulment on price grounds. The re-bid had four bidders, including PGCIL. It produced a lower tariff: AESL Rs 35,570 mn vs PGCIL's original ~37,000, a saving of roughly Rs 140 crore a year over a 35-year TSA. PGCIL itself raised its re-bid to Rs 40,820 mn. AESL won as the lowest bidder, only Rs 3 crore/yr below Sterlite. So the annulment lowered the cost to consumers. The record does not show it steering the award.
verdicts.reason: The award itself is confirmed, but the framing is wrong. The claim says "Reason for annulment not on record here", sets PGCIL-as-L1 next to the annulment, and labels the edge "(re-bid)", all of which hint that the round was redone to benefit AESL. That hint is refuted by primary records. CERC 341/AT/2024 records the annulment reason: lowest quote 55.41% above the CERC-norm estimate, annulled on the BEC's recommendation. CERC 252/TL/2025 shows AESL lowest of four, with PGCIL L4 at Rs 40,820 mn, and no one bidding in the e-RA. That meets the record's own killIf ("Annulment was on procedural grounds unrelated to bidder identity and AESL's re-bid was lowest on the record"). The LoI date is also wrong: 3 Dec 2024, not 4 Dec.   - Scheme count, private: 57% in FY24 (PGCIL won 10 of 23), 42% in FY25 (PGCIL won 26 of 45), and PGCIL still leads the count in FY26.
- **Qualification is not a discriminator:** in FY25, 17 bidders qualified, AESL for 36 schemes and Resonia for 35. Leadership in HVDC-heavy years comes down to 2–4 firms (only four bidders took part in the Rajasthan HVDC re-bid: PGCIL, AESL, Sterlite and IndiGrid).

- **Symmetry:** the same lens applied to PGCIL (a central PSU) gives a larger concentration figure (53–64%), and nobody reads that as capture. Concentration here comes from scale, not from a single group.

verdicts.dateTest: Bangladesh interim government / BPDB accused Adani Power of withholding Indian tax benefits in breach of the 5 Nov 2017 PPA and implementation agreement. The accusation was made in BPDB letters of 17 Sep and 22 Oct 2024 (a third on 4 Dec 2024 per TBS) and reported by Reuters on 19 Dec 2024. The interim government has held office since 8 Aug 2024, so the dates overlap and the test passes. from=2024-09-01 is acceptable (the Sep 2024 panel); 2024-09-17 is more precise for the tax accusation. The closing clause is stale: 'concerns reportedly resolved' (Daily Star, 2 Jul 2025) was overtaken by Business Standard on 19 Nov 2025. Adani had started Singapore arbitration over payment disputes; the Bangladesh High Court barred it until the court-appointed committee reports, and the parties were 'still in negotiations over payment disagreements'.
verdicts.identityTest: Accuser: Reuters attributes the accusation to 'Bangladesh's interim government'. The underlying letters are from BPDB, and power adviser Muhammad Fouzul Kabir Khan is named on the record. energy:govt-bangladesh is acceptable, though energy:bpdb is the actual letter-writer. Subject: Reuters says the contract was 'signed on Nov. 5, 2017 between Adani Power and the state-run Bangladesh Power Development Board'. The Godda plant is owned and operated by Adani Power (Jharkhand) Ltd, which the Daily Star (supply cut, Nov 2024) and TBS name as the Godda operator. The mapping to energy:adani-power-jharkhand is sound in substance, but the node has no CIN, so resolution rests on the plant-operator link (grid:c071). No name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: Being reviewed is non-discriminating: Yunus's government appointed a panel in Sep 2024 to examine all major energy deals signed under Hasina, and the 2010 no-tender Quick Enhancement law under which many IPPs were awarded was scrapped in Nov 2024. Among Hasina-era power contracts under review, being scrutinised is close to 100%. The specific allegations, non-pass-through of SEZ tax exemptions and a unit cost 55% above the average of Indian power sold to Dhaka, are specific to Godda and discriminating. No symmetric comparison against other Indian exporters (e.g. NTPC/PTC tariffs to Bangladesh) is in the record beyond the 55% average, and that average itself is the comparator.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, asked. (1) Reuters, 19 Dec 2024: 'A company spokesperson said in response to Reuters' questions that it had upheld all contractual obligations and had no indication Dhaka was reviewing the contract. The company did not answer questions about the tax benefits' (https://www.thedailystar.net/business/global-economy/news/adani-under-bribery-scrutiny-pressed-bangladesh-reopen-power-deal-3779901). This is c073. (2) Not in the graph and more substantive: TBS reports that Adani's 5 Feb 2025 letter said 'from March 2023 to December 2024, it had shared $94.5 million in coal-related tax benefits with BPDB'. It 'forwarded a document from India's Income Tax Department stating that APJL is not eligible for any additional income tax benefits under SEZ status', and asserted it does not receive blanket tax benefits because the plant was not online by 2021 (https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/infrastructure/adani-deal-govt-body-renegotiating-tax-rebate-surcharge-coal-price-1087866). Reuters also notes: 'Adani Power has not been accused of wrongdoing in Bangladesh.'
verdicts.innocentReading: This may be a contract-drafting dispute, not a breach. Bangladesh's own court-ordered review committee (per TBS) found that the PPA and implementation agreement as signed make pass-through of tax benefits 'very unlikely': if India waives taxes, Bangladesh must formally seek India's approval before the benefit passes. Adani says it passed on USD 94.5m in coal-related tax benefits and that the Indian tax authority confirms APJL gets no additional SEZ income-tax benefit. The 55% cost gap fits a 2017 imported-coal tariff indexed to international coal prices, compared against an average that includes cheaper Indian power sources. It is not by itself evidence of overcharging. A new government reopening its predecessor's no-tender contracts during a dollar shortage is ordinary leverage-seeking, and Reuters reports Dhaka explicitly hoped to use the US indictment as leverage.
verdicts.reason: The core accusation is quoted almost verbatim from the only substantive source. It was made by a named sovereign party (the interim government / BPDB, with the power adviser on record), and Adani's denial is recorded (c073). That meets the bar for 'alleged'. It is not refuted, but three stated facts are inaccurate or stale. (a) '55% above other Indian coal imports': the source says '55% above the average of all Indian power sold to Dhaka'. (b) '~USD 28.6m/yr' is Reuters' single-year estimate of potential savings for the year to 30 Jun 2024 (0.35 cents per unit x 8.16bn units), not an annual withheld amount. (c) 'concerns reportedly resolved' was contradicted in Nov 2025 by Adani's Singapore arbitration and the High Court bar. The graph also omits Adani's substantive rebuttal: the 5 Feb 2025 letter on USD 94.5m of coal-related tax benefits passed on and the Income Tax Department document on SEZ ineligibility.

Add a contra edge from APJL (or co:adani-power) to claim:grid:c072, tier reported: 5 Feb 2025 letter claiming USD 94.5m of coal-related tax benefits shared Mar 2023-Dec 2024, with an Income Tax Department document that APJL is ineligible for additional SEZ income-tax benefits (TBS, https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/infrastructure/adani-deal-govt-body-renegotiating-tax-rebate-surcharge-coal-price-1087866). 6. d: add Reuters' caveat 'Adani Power has not been accused of wrongdoing in Bangladesh'. 7. Optional: from=2024-09-17 (first BPDB letter); note that the review committee was formed by High Court directive (TBS); add the Nov 2025 Business Standard and TBS URLs to srcs.

verdicts.dateTest: PASS with a quote-dating error. The claim: Reporters' Collective (Shreegireesh Jalihal) alleged on 23 Sep 2024 that MSEDCL's twin-source tender (NIT 13 Mar 2024) favoured Adani. The article is dated 23 Sep 2024 ("Published on: Sep 23, 2024"). It says the tender was issued on 13 March 2024 ("On March 13, 2024, the state-owned Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited ... issued a tender") and that Adani won on 15 Sep ("On September 15, 2024, the Adani Group bagged the tender"). MERC Order in Case 155/2024 (26 Sep 2024) confirms the NIT date of 13 Mar 2024, financial bids opened 7 Aug 2024, the e-reverse auction on 9 Sep 2024 and MSEDCL's adoption petition on 13 Sep 2024. Adani's LoI release came out on about 14-15 Sep. The actor, the act and the window all line up. The error: the phrase 'cleared the path for Adani Group ... like a glove' does not appear in the 23 Sep article. It comes from the video page, which begins "Gautam Adani has been indicted in the US..." and so was published after 20 Nov 2024. Attributing that quote to "Reporters' Collective (23 Sep 2024)" misdates it.
verdicts.identityTest: PASS. MSEDCL is named in full in both the article and the MERC order as petitioner ("Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd."). The bidder and winner is Adani Power Limited according to MERC section 5.9.6, with Adani Green supplying the solar power according to the Adani release. There is no name-collision risk. Reporters' Collective is a named outlet and the byline is named. One schema problem: a news outlet is not an agency, and the SPEC defines `enforce` as "investigation, proceeding, audit, order", agency→subject. A journalistic investigation is a stretch of that predicate. The label should make clear that this is a media allegation, not an enforcement action.
verdicts.baseRate: Among bidders, 4 of 4 bids were technically qualified: Adani Power (5000 MW solar + 1600 MW thermal), JSW Energy, MB Power (MP) and Torrent Power (each 2500 + 800). Source: MERC order 26 Sep 2024, §5.9.6-5.9.7 ("all the above bidders were found to be technically qualified"). MERC §14.5 records "4 bids with 2.5 times bid capacity". So the twin-source condition did not leave Adani as the only bidder. Three rivals qualified, and Adani was the only one to bid the full quantum. What the condition did exclude is pure-play solar and pure-play thermal developers, which is a large share of the RE field. That exclusion is the real and discriminating part of the allegation. Among state tenders in 2024, composite thermal+solar procurement was rare: GoM's own letter calls it "innovative", and no model bidding document existed for it. Only Maharashtra and Rajasthan (RUVITSL) used it, so the design is discriminating, not industry-wide. Symmetry check: the same lens applied to Rajasthan (c093) is already in the graph. RUVITSL later scrapped its bundled tender and re-bid thermal only (TRC follow-up 'Rajasthan Govt's Tender Spot For Adani'). No opposition-run state was found using a twin-source design, so no symmetric comparison was available.
verdicts.denialFound: (a) Adani Power spokesperson, quoted in the 23 Sep 2024 article, deflected rather than denied: "These questions can only be answered by the tendering authority." (https://www.reporters-collective.in/trc/two-power-tenders-by-bjp-ruled-states-favour-adani-group). This is already captured as grid:c092. (b) MSEDCL: the article says "The Collective sent detailed queries to both state electricity distributors but neither have responded despite repeated reminders." So MSEDCL was asked and did not respond. (c) Maharashtra government and Ministry of Power: the article does not say they were asked. The claim's statement that they "did not respond" is not supported. (d) Counter-evidence in the primary record, missing from the graph: the MERC Order in Case No. 155 of 2024 (26 Sep 2024), §14.5, says "The Commission notes that MSEDCL has conducted transparent process of competitive bidding which is in accordance with the guidelines notified by the Government of India. Further 4 bids with 2.5 times bid capacity has been received which represent competition amongst the bidders." §5.8.2 gives MSEDCL's rationale ("higher per unit cost of thermal power will be offset by the cheaper tariff for the solar power... enhance MSEDCL's ability to meet its RPO obligations"). §5.9.5 records GoM's letter of 6 Sep 2024 calling the design "an innovative measure ... securing interest of consumers by way of discovery of combined lower effective tariff". Adani's Rs 4.08/kWh bid beat L2 JSW, and MERC says the composite tariff is below MSEDCL's average power purchase cost of about Rs 4.97. URL: https://www.eqmagpro.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Order-in-Case-No.155-of-2024_compressed.pdf (MERC order, mirrored).
verdicts.innocentReading: MSEDCL needed about 4,829 MW of thermal and 5,500 MW of solar for resource adequacy and round-the-clock supply. It bundled 1,600 MW thermal with 5,000 MW solar in one reverse auction so that cheap solar (Rs 2.70) would offset costly new thermal (Rs 5.39), while also meeting its RPO. The regulator approved the bid documents (12 Jul 2024) and found the process competitive: four qualified bidders, 2.5x subscription, and a tariff (Rs 4.08) below the average purchase cost. The fit with Adani's portfolio follows from Adani being India's largest combined thermal+solar private player. The design would favour whoever is largest in both segments, and JSW, Torrent and MB Power still competed. What the innocent reading does not explain: why states that can buy solar and thermal separately chose a design that excludes pure-play RE bidders, and why GoM's approval of the composite procurement and its deviation from the model documents (6 Sep 2024) came after financial bids had already been opened (7 Aug 2024).
verdicts.reason: The core edge holds. A named outlet (Reporters' Collective, Shreegireesh Jalihal, 23 Sep 2024) alleges in print that MSEDCL's twin-source condition "whittled down the competition for Adani Group", and the tender date, winner, rivals and Prayas criticism are all accurately drawn from that article. The claim is therefore a correct `alleged` edge and should not be killed. It is not clean, though. (1) It says the Maharashtra government and MoP "did not respond", but the source says only that the two state distributors were sent queries and did not reply. Recording a non-response from parties the source never says were asked breaks the absence rule. (2) The quoted phrase 'cleared the path ... like a glove' comes from a video page published after the November 2024 US indictment, not from the 23 Sep article. (3) The only contra is Adani's deflection. The graph is missing the primary-record counter-evidence (MERC order of 26 Sep 2024: four qualified bidders, 2.5x subscription, a tariff below average purchase cost, and an explicit finding that the process was transparent and followed GoI guidelines). That weakens the allegation's implied exclusion of rivals and must be shown as prominently as the claim. The tier stays `alleged` only if these fixes are made.
