The source confirms the EC date: "on March 28, 2024, Adani Power applied for an environmental clearance for expansion of its coal-fired thermal power plant in Rajasthan's Kawai." It does not support "Apr 2024". It says "A little over a month after Adani Group applied for green clearance ... RUVITSL issued a tender." Trade press (SolarQuarter, 6 May 2024) puts bid documents out from 2 May 2024, with bids due 24 Jun 2024. So the tender date is May 2024, and the record's from=2024-04-01 is wrong. The order of events (EC application, then tender about five weeks later) holds. The edge is also out of date. RUVITL's board ratified cancelling the bundled 11,200 MW tender in Nov 2024 (Reporters' Collective, "Rajasthan Govt's Tender Spot For Adani"). A thermal-only 3,200 MW re-tender followed on 1 Oct 2025, and RERC rejected that procurement by order dated 18 Nov 2025 (Down To Earth, 11 Dec 2025). The line "Adani described as frontrunner (tender not finalised)" is stale, and the record has to[] = null and no supersede.
verdicts.identityTest: The identities match. RUVITSL/RUVITL (Rajasthan Urja Vikas and IT Services Ltd) is the Rajasthan state discom-holding company named in the source. The Kawai applicant is Adani Power (the plant was then operated under Adani Power Rajasthan), and the source screenshots the EC application. There is no name-collision risk. The graph edge itself is wrong, though. It uses pred "enforce" from energy:reporters-collective to energy:state-rajasthan, but SPEC defines enforce as agency to subject (investigation, proceeding, audit, order). A news outlet is not an enforcement agency. This is an allegation of tender favouritism by the state (RUVITSL) toward Adani Power, and the edge's own benefit.who is co:adani-power.
verdicts.baseRate: The outlet itself concedes the twin-source condition was not exclusive to Adani: "Besides Adani Group, only a few companies operate at that scale in both solar and thermal power generation", and "Others such as JSW Group are also trying to do the same though they lag behind the Adani Group." Among large Indian private generators with GW-scale coal and solar (Adani, JSW, Tata Power, plus NTPC as a PSU), the bundled condition narrows the field to a handful of firms, not to one. So "fits only Adani" does not hold. The discriminating features are the in-state siting rule, the new-plant-only solar rule and the exact 3,200 MW match to Kawai. Those do point toward Adani, but they are the outlet's inference. Symmetry: Maharashtra (then BJP-Shiv Sena-NCP) ran a similar bundled 6,600 MW tender that Adani won. Both are BJP-run states, so this article gives no opposition-state comparison. Bundled RE-plus-thermal procurement was a new design, which the outlet calls "one of the first of its kind".
verdicts.denialFound: Adani Power spokesperson, to Reporters' Collective (23 Sep 2024): "These questions can only be answered by the tendering authority. The ongoing expansion plan at our Kawai Plant is independent of the outcome of the RUVITSL tender, which is yet to be awarded." https://www.reporters-collective.in/trc/two-power-tenders-by-bjp-ruled-states-favour-adani-group (recorded as grid:c094). RUVITSL and the Rajasthan government were asked and did not respond ("neither have responded despite repeated reminders"). In the later piece, RUVITL, the Rajasthan government and the Adani Group again did not respond to queries (https://www.reporters-collective.in/trc/rajasthan-govt-tender-spot-for-adani). RUVITL's recorded reason for cancelling in Nov 2024 was that bidders asked to "segregate" the two sources to allow "increased participation & competitive tariff".
verdicts.innocentReading: Rajasthan wanted firm round-the-clock supply and a higher renewable share, so it copied Maharashtra's new bundled solar-plus-thermal design. The in-state siting rule serves ordinary state-industrial-policy goals: local jobs, land, ISTS avoidance and state MoU commitments. Kawai is the only large private coal site in Rajasthan with land and a water/coal linkage ready for expansion, so any 3,200 MW (4x800 MW) in-state thermal requirement would coincide with it. The 4x800 MW figure is also standard supercritical sizing. Adani filing for an EC before the tender is consistent with a capacity plan that is independent of the tender, as Adani says. The design was later dropped after bidder feedback, and the regulator blocked the coal procurement. Neither outcome fits a completed steer to Adani.
verdicts.reason: The claim mis-states its own source, so it cannot stand as written. (1) The date is wrong: the source says "a little over a month after" 28 Mar 2024, and trade press dates the tender to 2 May 2024, not Apr 2024. (2) "Fits only Adani" is not in the source, which says only "a few companies" operate at that scale and names JSW. The source's actual framing is "tailored to match" and "granting added advantage". (3) The record leaves out a documented outcome that undercuts the "frontrunner" framing. The bundled tender was cancelled (board ratification Nov 2024) on a stated competition rationale and never awarded. The thermal-only successor was rejected by RERC on 18 Nov 2025. (4) Predicate "enforce" from a media outlet is a schema misuse. The core allegation is still attributable to a named outlet with published tender excerpts and the EC screenshot, and it carries a contra. So a corrected version can stay at alleged. It must not be upgraded, and it needs a supersede recording the cancellation.
verdicts.corrections: text: replace "Apr 2024" with "May 2024 (bid docs from 2 May 2024)". Replace "fits only Adani" with "tailored to match Adani's Kawai expansion and Rajasthan solar MoU; outlet concedes 'only a few companies' (e.g. JSW) could qualify". from: change 2024-04-01 to 2024-05-02. to: set 2024-11 (bundled tender cancelled, board-ratified Nov 2024). pred: change "enforce" to "analytic"/allegation form, or restructure as s=energy:state-rajasthan (RUVITSL) -> t=co:adani-power with the allegation attributed to Reporters' Collective in the label. "enforce" is reserved for agency to subject. d: remove "frontrunner at publication" as a current-state fact, or date-stamp it 23 Sep 2024. Add a supersede/contra node covering: (a) RUVITL cancellation, citing bidder requests to segregate for "increased participation & competitive tariff" (https://www.reporters-collective.in/trc/rajasthan-govt-tender-spot-for-adani), and (b) the thermal-only 3,200 MW re-tender (1 Oct 2025) and the RERC rejection order of 18 Nov 2025 (https://www.downtoearth.org.in/energy/rerc-says-no-to-new-3200-mw-coal-power-citing-consumer-interest-and-cheaper-alternatives). Add the SolarQuarter 6 May 2024 tender notice as a primary-adjacent source for the tender terms and date (https://solarquarter.com/2024/05/06/rajasthan-urja-vikas-and-it-service-ltd-initiates-competitive-bidding-for-3200-mw-thermal-and-8000-mw-solar-power-procurement/). Update upgradeIf/killIf: no award was made, so the upgrade path is dead. The allegation now rests only on tender design.

verdicts.dateTest: PASS. The claim reads: N. Chandrababu Naidu, TDP chief and Leader of Opposition (not CM), called the Polavaram re-tender 'reserve tendering' on or before 24 Sep 2019. His CM windows are 2014-06-08 to 2019-05-29 and 2024-06-12 onward, so he spoke from opposition, which matches the claim's '(TDP)' label. The GO for the tender is dated 16/17 Aug 2019. Tender and pre-bid were in Sep 2019. TNM published on 24 Sep 2019 ('Published on : 24 Sep 2019'). CAG shows the agreement as 'Lumpsum agreement No.01/2019-20, dated 08.11.2019' and the award as Nov 2019. The allegation came before the agreement, which is consistent with a statement made about the tender stage. CAG Report No. 4 of 2025 covers the period up to March 2023. Government replies are dated June 2024 and Nov 2024. The Nov 2024 exit conference therefore took place under Naidu's own government.
verdicts.identityTest: PASS. The TNM award target is 'Megha Engineering and Infrastructures Limited (MEIL)'. CAG names 'M/s Megha Engineering & Infrastructure Limited (M/s MEIL)' in footnotes 91 and 100 and places it in Hyderabad. It is the same entity; the small spelling differences are CAG's. Naidu is identified by office with dates. There is no name-collision risk. The previous contractor, Navayuga Engineering Company Ltd, is correctly kept separate.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a discriminating edge, and not meant to be one. It is an attributed opposition allegation that a specific award was rigged, not a statistical pattern. Useful context: in India, an incoming opposition alleging favouritism in the ruling party's big contract awards is close to universal, so the allegation alone has almost no evidential weight. The weight comes from CAG. The comparable reverse tender in the same programme (the Max Infra package, about Rs 58 cr saved) had more than one bidder, so the single-bidder result is unusual within the reference class. Symmetry: MEIL was also a major AP contractor under Naidu's own 2014-19 government (lift schemes), and it stayed on as Polavaram contractor after Naidu returned in 2024 (MEIL's diaphragm-wall completion page). The 'favour' lens therefore reaches both regimes, and the allegation reads as partisan and aimed at the procedure rather than the firm.
verdicts.denialFound: No direct MEIL denial found. Web search budget was exhausted, and a DuckDuckGo/Bing fallback via curl returned nothing, so absence is not proven. MEIL does not appear to have been asked in the TNM piece. The accused government's counter is on the record in two places. (1) YSRCP government, TNM 24 Sep 2019: it 'claimed that it saved Rs 780 crore public money through re-tendering... MEIL had come up with a proposal quoting a price that was 12.6% lower than the previous contractor' (https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/polavaram-re-tendering-ap-govt-seeks-award-work-meil-claims-it-saved-rs-780-cr-109396). This is already captured as c007. (2) Government reply to CAG, June 2024: 'though single bidder had participated in the reverse tendering, the work was awarded... as the bid amount quoted by the bidder was 12.60 per cent less than the estimated contract value (ECV) and ₹628.43 crore savings accrued'. APGENCO, Jan 2023: 'the single bidder was considered as per the approval of CoT, GoAP'. On tender conditions: 'modified on the best interest of government... so that competent contractors participate instead of weak contractors' (CAG Report No. 4 of 2025, para 3.1.2.2).
verdicts.innocentReading: After cancelling Navayuga, the government wanted a contractor that could finish a stalled national project quickly. It tightened pre-qualification (financial and experience criteria) to screen out weak contractors after problems with earlier contractors. An e-procurement upload failure shortened the bid window to 16 days. Only the largest Telugu-state EPC firm with a comparable record (Kaleshwaram) could qualify. The government then went ahead with the single bid, which came in 12.6% below ECV, rather than re-tendering and losing another season. CAG itself says 'some of the additional conditions incorporated by the Department are in the spirit of timely completion of the work'. On this reading the result is procedural non-compliance and a lost competitive price, not a tender reserved for MEIL.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Change 'favouring MEIL' to 'alleging "unfair preference while awarding the contract" (to MEIL) and calling it "reserve tendering"' so the quoted words are separated from the inferred target.
2. Change 'the saving claim "incorrect"' to 'the claim of a 12.60% saving below ECV (Rs 628.43 cr, Part A) "incorrect", because contingent add-on works were awarded at SSR 2020-21 rates (Rs 233.26 cr undue advantage)'. CAG did not rule on the Rs 780 cr aggregate.
3. Replace 'but did not find for whom it was reserved' with: 'CAG found stringent tender conditions (deviating from the July 2003 GO, without prior approval) and a 16-day bid window (vs the 21 days prescribed) restricted participation, leaving a single bidder who could meet the modified conditions. It made no finding that the conditions were designed for MEIL. The AP government (Nov 2024, under Naidu) accepted the observation.'
4. Amount: CAG gives Rs 4,359.11 cr in para 3.1.2.2 and Rs 4,359.12 cr in fn 101 and para 3.2.2. Keep 4,359.12 but note the Rs 0.01 cr discrepancy. The agreement date 08.11.2019 is confirmed (No. 01/2019-20).
5. Add a CAG citation to c006's srcs array. The record currently cites only TNM, while the claim text relies on CAG findings.
6. Note in d that the Nov 2024 government acceptance came from Naidu's government, so the accuser and the conceding party are the same, and that MEIL was retained on Polavaram after 2024.
7. Direction is Naidu to claim:hydro:c003 as contra, which fits the spec. Keep it.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: CBI (agencies) opened a case over CVPPPL's award of the Kiru civil-works contract to Patel Engineering. Award 2019 (both sources). FIR 2022 (Tribune: "FIR registered in 2022"; BS: "The FIR, which was originally filed in 2022"). Chargesheet 22 May 2025. Malik was Governor Aug 2018 to Oct 2019 (BS), which overlaps the 2019 award, so the chronology holds. Defect: the edge is `enforce` (agency to subject) but has "from": "2019-01-01". That is the award year. CBI took no action in 2019, so the enforcement edge should start at the 2022 FIR.
verdicts.identityTest: CVPPPL (Chenab Valley Power Projects Pvt Ltd, the NHPC and JKSPDC JV) and Patel Engineering Ltd (NSE PATELENG) are both named explicitly in both sources, so there is no risk of mixing them up with another company. Caveat: BS lists the accused as Malik, Navin Kumar Choudhary (then CVPPPL chairman), M S Babu, M K Mittal, Arun Kumar Mishra and Patel Engineering Ltd. CVPPPL as a company is not named as an accused. The `enforce` target is really CVPPPL's award decision and its officials, not the JV itself. The node CIN is null.
verdicts.baseRate: A CBI FIR plus chargesheet is a specific, discriminating event, not a property shared by most hydro awards. The part that does not discriminate is the implied mechanism: PSU and JV boards often revisit or reverse earlier procurement decisions (to avoid re-tender delay, or on the tender committee's advice). Being reversed by a later board meeting is not in itself a sign of wrongdoing.
verdicts.denialFound: Patel Engineering: none found. Neither source carries a company response, and neither says whether the company was asked. BSE and NSE announcement APIs returned 403 or empty this pass, and the web-search budget was used up, so an exchange clarification from April 2022 or May 2025 was not ruled out. CVPPPL/NHPC: none found. Malik: BS says he "has consistently denied any wrongdoing in the alleged ₹2,200-cr scam, saying the probe is looking to target him instead of the real culprits"; Tribune says he was hospitalised and could not comment. Record c058 (no response recorded) is accurate as far as it goes.
verdicts.innocentReading: The 47th board meeting decided to cancel and re-tender by e-tender with reverse auction. The 48th board meeting then reversed that and let the existing tender go ahead, for example to avoid delaying a strategically prioritised Chenab project. The contract went to the bidder already in that process. On this reading the board's own later decision was carried out, not ignored. The CBI's case must then be that the 48th-meeting reversal was improperly obtained, which is a narrower allegation that has not been tested at trial.
verdicts.reason: The claim quotes the source selectively in a way that changes what it means. It says the 47th-meeting re-tender decision "was not implemented", which reads as the board being ignored. The Tribune's full sentence is: "the same was not implemented (according to the decision taken in the 48th board meeting)". Business Standard says outright: "the 48th meeting reportedly reversed the decision, ultimately awarding the contract to Patel Engineering." So a later board meeting reversed the decision. The benefit.how "Award without the reverse auction the board had ordered" and the label "board's re-tender decision not implemented" leave out the fact that the board withdrew that order itself. The existing killIf ("board later validly rescinded") is already half-met on the record: the rescission happened, and only its validity is disputed. The core edge survives: CBI registered an FIR in 2022 and filed a chargesheet in May 2025 over the Rs 2,200 cr Kiru civil-works award to Patel Engineering in 2019, confirmed by two outlets. The accused parties are named, and there is a contra, so `alleged` is the right tier once the text is fixed. As written, the edge is refuted.
verdicts.corrections: 1) text/d: replace "this 'was not implemented'" with "per the FIR, this was not implemented 'according to the decision taken in the 48th board meeting' — i.e. a subsequent board meeting reversed it (BS: 'the 48th meeting reportedly reversed the decision') — and the contract went to Patel Engineering (2019); CBI alleges the process/e-tendering guidelines were irregular." 2) lab: change to "Alleged: 48th board meeting reversed 47th-meeting re-tender decision; award to Patel Engineering under CBI investigation". 3) benefit.how: change to "Award under the continued tender after the board's 48th meeting reversed its own re-tender/reverse-auction decision (alleged irregular by CBI)". 4) killIf: rewrite as "Court finds the 48th-meeting reversal was validly taken on legitimate grounds" (the rescission itself is already on record). 5) from: change "2019-01-01" to the 2022 FIR date (month or day not confirmed in these sources; use "2022"). Keep the 2019 award date in the text. 6) Consider putting the named officials (Choudhary, Babu, Mittal, Mishra) and Patel Engineering as the enforce subjects, or add their edges; CVPPPL itself is not a named accused. 7) Keep the tier at alleged. c058 stays, but note that exchange filings were not checkable (portals returned 403).

verdicts.dateTest: Actor and act: Malik (as Governor) says he was offered Rs 300 cr to clear two files, one of them Kiru. Tenure: 2018-08-23 to 2019-10-30. Tribune: "Malik, who was the governor of Jammu and Kashmir from August 23, 2018 to October 30, 2019". The contract was awarded in 2019 (Tribune: "to a private company in 2019"), so the alleged offer falls inside his tenure. The test passes. Two date faults remain. (a) `from: 2019-01-01` has no source. Neither outlet dates the offer or the moment he first made the claim public, which was a later statement, not 2019. (b) The record is stale as of 2026-09-25: Malik died on 5 Aug 2025 (Wikipedia: "died after a prolonged illness on 5 August 2025, at the age of 79"). Neither the claim nor the node records this. The chargesheet date is fine: BS is dated 22 May 2025 and Tribune says "officials said Thursday", and 22 May 2025 was a Thursday.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass for the person. Both outlets identify him by office and dates: "Governor of J&K, August 2018 to October 2019". Satya Pal Malik is a unique public figure, so there is no name-collision risk. CVPPL is the same company the sources call "Chenab Valley Power Projects Private Limited (CVPPPL)", but its CIN is still null. The predicate is the real problem. SPEC says `enforce` goes agency→subject. Malik is not an agency, and his allegation is not aimed at CVPPL. It is aimed at unnamed people who he says offered the bribe. So an edge reading Malik enforce→CVPPL is wrong in both predicate and direction.
verdicts.baseRate: The graph's usual base rate does not really apply to a single named allegation. Even so, the discriminating fact holds up: a sitting Governor publicly saying he was offered a bribe tied to one specific contract, and that contract later drawing a CBI chargesheet, is rare. It is not an industry-wide property. Symmetry check: the same lens on any governor-era contract would only produce an edge where a named official made a public, dated bribe claim, so the method is not creating the finding by itself.
verdicts.denialFound: From the accused offerors: none found. Neither source names who made the offer ("offeror unidentified" is correct as far as these sources go), so nobody was reported as asked or as denying. From Malik about his own charging (c026), confirmed. BS: "Malik ... has consistently denied any wrongdoing in the alleged ₹2,200-cr scam, saying the probe is looking to target him instead of the real culprits". Tribune: "Malik said his residence was raided by the CBI instead of investigating the people he had complained about". My WebSearch budget ran out during this pass, so I could not search for a response from anyone Malik named in his earlier public statements. That lead is still open: check whether anyone he later named issued a denial or legal notice. I have not verified any such denial and none is asserted here.
verdicts.innocentReading: Malik's bribe claim and his inclusion in the chargesheet can both be true without contradicting each other, and neither needs retaliation to explain it. In 2019 the Governor held executive power in J&K. Any charge over the award process, including the unimplemented 47th-board-meeting re-tender decision, would naturally name the officials whose approvals are on file, whether or not someone separately tried to bribe him. Saying he refused a bribe does not clear him of process irregularities, and being charged does not show his bribe claim was false. The "nonetheless" wording implies a tension the sources do not state.
verdicts.reason: The core content checks out in two independent outlets. Tribune: "had claimed that he was offered a Rs 300-crore bribe for clearing two files, including the one pertaining to the project". BS: "offered a bribe of Rs 300 crore to approve two files, one of which was related to this project". Both report the 22 May 2025 chargesheet naming him and his denial. `alleged` is the right tier: it is a named person's unproven assertion, and it has a contra (c059). The claim survives only after corrections. (1) Calling him "the complainant", and saying in `d` that "CBI's investigation followed his complaint", goes beyond the sources. They report only that he "had claimed" the offer and that he "complained about" certain people, which is his own framing. Neither says the 2022 FIR came from his complaint. This is a conjunction problem: his claim, plus a 2022 FIR, plus a chargesheet naming him, adds up to "CBI charged the whistleblower", which neither source says. (2) The predicate and direction are wrong. (3) `from` has no source. (4) His death on 5 Aug 2025 is missing, which makes the killIf impossible to meet.
verdicts.corrections: 1. pred: `enforce` Malik→energy:cvppl breaks the SPEC direction rule (agency→subject). Either re-model it as an assertion edge to the claim it answers (Malik `contra` → claim:hydro:c022, merged with c026, since it is his exculpatory account), or keep it as an alleged edge whose target is an unresolved node for the unidentified offeror. Do not use CVPPL as the target. 2. text/d: replace "CBI charges the complainant" and "CBI's investigation followed his complaint" with "CBI's chargesheet names Malik, who had earlier publicly claimed the bribe offer. The sources do not state whether the 2022 FIR arose from his claim." Remove "nonetheless". 3. from: remove 2019-01-01. Either leave the offer date as unknown within 2018-08-23→2019-10-30, or use the dated first public statement once a source for it is found. 4. Add to the claim and to the energy:satya-pal-malik node: "Died 5 Aug 2025 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satya_Pal_Malik); proceedings against him abate. The case continues against the others." 5. killIf: "Court rejects the allegation" can no longer happen against Malik. Change to "Chargesheet or trial record finds no bribe offer, or contradicts the two-files account". Keep upgradeIf as "offeror identified in the chargesheet or trial record". 6. Record the missing offeror denial as a gap ("offeror unnamed in the sources; not asked"). 7. Minor: the text cites c026, which answers c022, not c025. Say so explicitly, or link c026 to both.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Sikkim cabinet (SKM government, CM Prem Singh Tamang, in office since May 2019) decided to transfer SPICL's 60.08% of Sikkim Urja Ltd to Greenko Energies Pvt Ltd on 3 Feb 2024. The actor's tenure overlaps the date. The date differs between sources. Mongabay (11 Mar 2025, Simrin Sirur): "The final decision by the cabinet was made on February 3, 2024, after it received an offer from Greenko". ThePrint (1 Oct 2024): "On 2 February, 2024, the Sikkim cabinet, in a controversial move, decided to divest the entire 60.08 percent stake of SPICL to Greenko Energies Private Limited". The record's 'd' field already notes the one-day gap. The sequence holds: the GLOF destroyed the plant on the night of 3–4 Oct 2023, the cabinet decided in Feb 2024, the EAC approved the rebuild on 10 Jan 2025 ("The EAC gave its nod to rebuild the dam on January 10 this year"), and the petition was filed on 24 Feb 2025. There are no anachronisms.
verdicts.identityTest: The source node is the State of Sikkim acting through the Sikkim Power Investment Corporation Ltd (SPICL), its investment arm. The target named by both outlets is "Greenko Energies Private Limited, part of the Greenko Energy Holdings" (ThePrint). Mongabay calls it "a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Mauritius-based Greenko Energy Holdings". The existing minority holder is named differently. ThePrint (12 Oct 2023) says "35 percent is owned by Greenko Mauritius", while Mongabay says Greenko Energies "held around 34%". So "already 35% holder" is true of the group, not necessarily of the legal entity that received the stake. There is no risk of a name collision. The group-level node energy:greenko is acceptable, but the entity-level wording should be precise.
verdicts.baseRate: A state handing a flood-destroyed, heavily indebted asset to the existing co-promoter or minority shareholder, in return for that party taking over the debt, is the normal way distressed JV assets are resolved. The incumbent partner usually has a right of first refusal, and outside bidders have little reason to want a wrecked site carrying about Rs 10,000 cr of lender exposure. The pattern of transferring to the incumbent partner therefore does not single anyone out. What does single the deal out, and gives it its news value, is the lack of any tender or valuation reported, the 50-year horizon, and the transfer of an asset that earned Rs 1,207 cr in revenue in FY23 without cash consideration.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial from Greenko. Mongabay: "Mongabay India reached a Greenko spokesperson for comments on the allegations mentioned in the petition but no response was received at the time of publication." The SKM spokesperson and the state's legal representatives were also asked and gave no response. The state's public justification is on record: CM Tamang said "the state government took this step to remain debt-free" (https://india.mongabay.com/2025/03/disinvestment-from-dam-challenged-in-court-in-fragile-himalayan-state/). This is captured as contra c033.
verdicts.innocentReading: The plant was destroyed on 4 Oct 2023. SPICL and SUL together owed lenders (PFC, REC, SBI) more than Rs 10,000 cr. The cabinet note put the cost of reviving the plant at about Rs 4,000 cr, which a small state could not raise. Taking over Rs 3,079.74 cr of liabilities and funding reconstruction is itself valuable consideration from Greenko. The state gives up equity in return for a free power share (6%, rising to 15%) without any further capital risk. On this reading the state offloads a liability, and Greenko is not handed a windfall.
verdicts.reason: Both sources confirm the core transfer: Sikkim's 60.08% stake went to Greenko Energies Pvt Ltd in early Feb 2024. ThePrint is an independent second outlet on the transfer and its date. Mongabay confirms every figure in the claim verbatim: Rs 3,079.74 cr of dues handed to Greenko, 6% power share rising to 15% over 50 years, Rs 4,000 cr capital infusion, and EAC approval on 10 Jan 2025. Mongabay also shows that the state and Greenko were asked for comment. The figures come from a petition quoting a cabinet note, which counts as one credible outlet with published documents, so the correct tier is reported, not documented. "No cash consideration reported" is an accurate statement of what is absent from the sources, not an assertion of fact. The claim survives, but some wording needs tightening.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Date: write "2/3 Feb 2024 (ThePrint 2 Feb; Mongabay 3 Feb)" in the text, not a flat "3 Feb". 2) Entity: the recipient is Greenko Energies Pvt Ltd, while the existing ~35% holder is Greenko Mauritius per ThePrint (Mongabay says ~34%). Change "already 35% holder" to "Greenko group already held ~34–35% via Greenko Mauritius". 3) Free power: specify "6% free power for the first two years after re-commissioning (tentatively from 2027-28), rising to 15% over 50 years". 4) Sourcing: attribute the Rs 3,079.74 cr and Rs 4,000 cr figures to the cabinet note as quoted in the Bhutia petition (Mongabay). 5) Framing: keep "no cash consideration reported" but add "liabilities assumed are the consideration". Set benefit.confidence to "low", not "unknown", and note that no valuation or tender was reported. 6) Predicate: "award" suggests a competitive award. Consider "divest"/"transfer" if the schema allows. 7) Sources: the task's srcs list the ThePrint Oct 2023 article, but the c031 record in hydro.json lists Wikipedia as its third source. Reconcile them, and add ThePrint 12 Oct 2023 to c031 as the source for the 35% holding.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, written out: the Sikkim govt/SDMA disputed the GLOF finding of the central committee (headed by R.K. Jain, ex-CWC chairman; report to the Jal Shakti ministry June 2024), per ThePrint on 1 Oct 2024. The insurance policy, with its Rs 500 cr GLOF cap, was in force before the 3-4 Oct 2023 event, and ThePrint reported the cap on 12 Oct 2023. The dates are consistent, with two problems. (a) The edge has from=2023-10-04, which is the flood date. The documented dispute dates from the June 2024 report and the state's representation against it. Set from to 2024-06 or 2024-10-01. (b) The innocentReading says the state is maximising recovery "for a public-majority company". But on 2 Feb 2024 (the 1 Oct 2024 article says cabinet divested on this date; hydro.json elsewhere records 3 Feb) the Sikkim cabinet decided to transfer SPICL's entire 60.08% stake to Greenko, together with Rs 3,079.74 cr of loans and dues. So by the time the state contested the finding, the main beneficiaries of a payout were likely Greenko and the lenders (PFC/REC/SBI), not a public-majority SUL. Whether the transfer was completed is not established.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. R.K. Jain is named in the source as a former Central Water Commission chairman heading the committee. Sikkim Urja Ltd (formerly Teesta Urja) is the claimant: "Sikkim Urja Limited (SUL) has filed an insurance claim of over Rs 2,500 crore". The state's position is voiced by named people: Prabhakar Rai (SDMA director), Durga Kamla Rai (SDSO chairman), and a state government representation. There is no name-collision risk. Minor: "Sikkim govt insists cloudburst" is a paraphrase. The source says "flash flood induced by heavy rain and landslide" and "significant rainfall leading to avalanches and secondary flooding".
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating as a suspicion signal. Nearly every insurance claimant argues for the peril that pays in full, and nearly every insurer argues for the capped one. The Asia Insurance Post piece of 24 Oct 2023 shows reinsurers and GIC Re taking the GLOF/Rs 500 cr line early, which suits their interest just as closely. The symmetry test fails for a one-sided reading: GLOF lowers the payout by government-owned GIC Re and other insurers, and the central committee sits under a central ministry. So "position aligns with payout" applies equally to the other side. The edge is only fair if it states that symmetry.
verdicts.denialFound: Asked, no response. ThePrint wrote: "ThePrint reached V.B. Pathak, Sikkim Chief Secretary, via calls and messages. This report will be updated if and when a response is received". The same applied to SDSO chairman Durga Kamla Rai. There is no recorded approach to SUL, Greenko or the insurers. The state's substantive counter-position is on record, though. It said the report was "based upon the hypothesis that the event was a GLOF event and then interpreting data to align with this conclusion", and it cites an IMD orange alert for 3-4 Oct. Source: https://theprint.in/india/sikkim-govt-central-panel-split-over-what-caused-2023-floods-at-stake-is-rs-2500-cr-insurance-claim/2291910/. I found no later settlement, arbitral award or official denial of the insurance motive; the web-search budget was exhausted and only one extra DuckDuckGo query was run.
verdicts.innocentReading: Rain-and-landslide or cloudburst framing was widespread in the first days after the event, in media and official statements, before any insurance stakes were public. The SDMA and SDSO have their own technical view: they cite the IMD orange alert and point to temporary hydraulic blockages. Hydrologists (including commenters in Asia Insurance Post) describe a compound rain-plus-GLOF event. A claimant arguing for the covered peril is ordinary contractual conduct, and the insurers and central bodies are equally interested in the opposite reading.
verdicts.reason:
Every factual part checks out against ThePrint (1 Oct 2024; Moushumi Das Gupta), quoted verbatim:
- sum assured "Rs 11,400 crore"
- "coverage for damages by GLOF is capped at Rs 500 crore"
- "100 percent coverage of the sum assured for losses resulting from flash floods or cloudburst-induced floods"
- claim "over Rs 2,500 crore"
- R.K. Jain committee, 40 million m3, about 10,000 m3/s inflow against 7,500 m3/s spillway, IMD shows no heavy rain upstream.

The 12 Oct 2023 ThePrint piece corroborates the cap and the sum assured, and Asia Insurance Post (24 Oct 2023) independently confirms the reinsurers' Rs 500 cr position. The payout link is not our invention: the source's headline and an unnamed Sikkim official make it. As analytic it clears the bar because it carries an innocentReading and implies no wrongdoing. It survives only in a corrected form. As written, it presents a one-sided interest alignment without the symmetric insurer/centre interest, and its innocentReading is out of date: the state had decided to divest its stake to Greenko before it contested the finding.

2. text/d: replace "Sikkim govt insists cloudburst" with "Sikkim SDMA (director Prabhakar Rai) and state government say flash flood induced by heavy rain and landslide; state cites IMD orange alert 3-4 Oct 2023 and calls the panel's method hypothesis-led". Name the ministry: the committee reported to the Ministry of Jal Shakti in June 2024.

Note that the 2 Feb 2024 cabinet decision (per the 1 Oct 2024 article; hydro.json elsewhere records 3 Feb) moved the 60.08% SPICL stake and Rs 3,079.74 cr of dues to Greenko, so payout beneficiaries likely include Greenko and PFC/REC/SBI. verdicts.dateTest: Hindenburg Research published the Adani report on 2023-01-24 ("Published on January 24, 2023", updated February 5, 2023). Hindenburg existed from 2017 until it disbanded in January 2025, and Adani Group was a going concern throughout, so the dates overlap. The contra lit:c010 (413-page response) is dated 2023-01-29, after the report, which is the right order. The edge has "to": null. That is acceptable for an allegation that still stands, but Hindenburg dissolved in Jan 2025, so the actor node no longer exists as an operating entity.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The source node is the US short-seller Hindenburg Research LLC (Nathan Anderson), the publisher at hindenburgresearch.com. The target is "adani", the group-level node. That is correct because the report targets the group as a whole ("7 key listed companies") and not one CIN. Vinod Adani, the alleged controller of the shells, is named in the text but is not given an edge here, so there is no risk of mixing up family members.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a discriminating property question. This is a single named-party allegation, not an inference from a shared trait, so no base rate applies. On symmetry: activist short reports against large Indian groups are rare. The same lens would treat any short-seller report the same way, as alleged with a contra.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. On 2023-01-29 Adani released a 413-page response calling the report a "calculated attack on India, the independence, integrity and quality of Indian institutions, and the growth story and ambition of India" (Guardian 2023-01-30) and Hindenburg's conduct "calculated securities fraud" (Bloomberg 2023-01-29). Both are cited in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adani_Group. Hindenburg answered that the response was "obfuscation under the garb of nationalism" (Bloomberg 2023-01-30). Later counter-record: the SC-appointed expert committee found "prima facie" no regulatory failure (2023-05-19). The Supreme Court on 2024-01-03 refused an SIT/CBI probe and directed SEBI to finish its last 2 of 24 investigations. SEBI issued Hindenburg a show-cause notice (June 2024) alleging use of non-public information. Reported but not opened here: SEBI final orders of September 2025 disposing of some Hindenburg-related Adani proceedings.
verdicts.innocentReading: A short-seller holding a disclosed position publishes an adversarial research report. The allegations are the author's own claims, made with a financial interest, and regulators and courts have not upheld them. The boring reading is that this is a commercially motivated short thesis. Some of its facts (offshore FPI holdings, related-party links) may be true without adding up to manipulation or fraud in law. The claim already says this by using the alleged tier and naming the short position.
verdicts.reason:
Every element of the claim appears verbatim in the primary source (https://hindenburgresearch.com/adani/, fetched live):
- "the INR 17.8 trillion (U.S. $218 billion) Indian conglomerate Adani Group has engaged in a brazen stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme over the course of decades"
- "We have identified 38 Mauritius shell entities controlled by Vinod Adani or close associates"
- "its 7 key listed companies have 85% downside purely on a fundamental basis owing to sky-high valuations"
- "we have taken a short position in Adani Group Companies through U.S.-traded bonds and non-Indian-traded derivative instruments"
- "We have included 88 questions"

The claim is correctly attributed to a named party and carries a documented contra (lit:c010, the Adani 413-page rebuttal of 2023-01-29, confirmed in Wikipedia/Adani_Group with Bloomberg and Guardian cites). That meets the SPEC bar for "alleged". Upgrading it is not supported, because no regulator or court has upheld the allegations. Killing it is not supported either: it is a real, dated, attributed allegation, and its killIf condition (SEBI clearing all 24 matters, unchallenged) has not been shown to be met.
verdicts.corrections:
(1) Precision: "85% downside" should read "85% downside for 7 key listed companies on a fundamental/valuation basis". As written in the text it can read as a fraud-driven price target. Record field "d" says "85%+", but the source says "85%", so drop the "+".
(2) "38+ Mauritius shells": the source says "38 Mauritius shell entities" plus other entities in Cyprus, the UAE, Singapore and the Caribbean. Either keep "38" or say "38 in Mauritius plus others".
(3) Benefit block: add a note that Hindenburg's July 2024 reply to SEBI's show-cause notice reportedly disclosed about USD 4.1m gross from an investor relationship (Kingdon) and about USD 31k from its own short. This is from memory and not verified in this session, so leave amountCr null until it is sourced.
(4) Contra chain: add the SC expert-committee finding (2023-05-19), the SC judgment (2024-01-03) and the SEBI show-cause notice to Hindenburg (2024) as further contra/enforce edges. Open the September 2025 SEBI orders to test killIf (sebi.gov.in returned 403 in an earlier sweep).
(5) Predicate "enforce" is defined as agency→subject. Hindenburg is a private short-seller, not an agency. Keep it only as the closest available predicate, and state in "d" that this is a private allegation, not an enforcement action.
