verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: OCCRP (with the Guardian and FT) published, on 2023-08-31 (Guardian/FT dated 30-31 Aug 2023), documents alleging that Nasser Ali Shaban Ahli and Chang Chung-Ling traded Adani stock through Mauritius funds (Global Opportunities Fund feeding EIFF / EM Resurgence Fund). The trading window OCCRP describes is roughly 2013-2018, with holdings peaking at about $430M. OCCRP existed and was active throughout, and the Adani listed entities existed across the whole window. The "from" date of 2023-08-31 correctly marks the publication date, not the conduct. The SC judgment date of 2024-01-03 is correct (Vishal Tiwari v UoI; Indian Kanoon doc 188573380). The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: Source node: OCCRP, the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project. The byline on the original is Anand Mangnale, Ravi Nair and NBR Arcadio. The identity is unambiguous. Target node: "adani", the group. OCCRP names the Adani Group, Vinod Adani (who is in the promoter group, as Adani admitted in March 2023), and two named individuals, Ahli and Chang. The target resolves correctly to the group, with no name collision. One structural defect: the edge uses predicate "enforce", which SPEC defines as agency→subject for an "investigation, proceeding, audit, order". OCCRP is a journalism non-profit, typed in the file as ty:agency / fam:market. It has no enforcement power, so the edge tells the graph that an enforcement action exists when none does.
verdicts.baseRate: The property is being the subject of a multi-outlet (OCCRP+Guardian+FT) documentary investigation alleging hidden promoter-linked FPI holdings. Among top-50 Indian listed groups this is rare (under 5%), so the edge discriminates. The underlying structure is not rare: opaque Mauritius or Cayman FPIs with concentrated single-group holdings were common. That is why SEBI's August 2023 FPI granular-disclosure rule (for FPIs with over 50% of equity AUM in one group or over Rs 25,000 cr in India) applied across the whole industry. SC para 29 also noted that the FPI Regulations originally allowed opaque structures. So having Mauritius FPI holders is non-discriminating. The discriminating element is the specific promoter-proxy link that OCCRP alleges, via the Vinod Adani advisory fee.
verdicts.denialFound: A denial exists and is easily captured. The Adani Group statement of 2023-08-31, carried by the Economic Times, reads: "We categorically reject these recycled allegations. These news reports appear to be yet another concerted bid by Soros-funded interests supported by a section of the foreign media to revive the meritless Hindenburg report." The statement also calls the timing "suspicious, mischievous and malicious" and says "we reject these reports in their entirety." Source: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/adani-group-rejects-recycled-allegations-made-by-george-soros-funded-occrp/articleshow/103230293.cms . The Adani Group Wikipedia page cites the same article, and it sits one paragraph away from the text the edge relies on. The parties were asked before publication. OCCRP's original says "Ahli and Chang did not respond to OCCRP's requests for comment," that Chang told the Guardian he "knew nothing about any secret purchases of Adani stock," and that "Vinod Adani did not respond to requests for comment." The SC (2024-01-03, para 39-40) held that the OCCRP report "cannot be relied on as conclusive proof of the inadequacy of the investigation by SEBI." It also recorded SEBI's submission that the report "lacks documentary support."
verdicts.innocentReading: Ahli and Chang are long-standing business associates acting as independent investors through legitimately registered Mauritius FPIs, which were permitted opaque structures under the FPI rules of the time. If they are not "promoters" or persons acting in concert, the promoter group stayed within the 75% cap and no securities law was breached. OCCRP itself frames it this way: "The question of whether this arrangement is a violation of the law rests on whether Ahli and Chang should be considered to be acting on behalf of Adani 'promoters'." The advisory fee paid to a Vinod Adani company could be an ordinary commercial arrangement. No SEBI order in hand finds that the named funds were promoter-controlled.
verdicts.reason:
The substance holds. I opened the OCCRP original (HTTP 200), and it says exactly what the claim says: named individuals traded Adani stock through Mauritius funds, with a possible breach of minimum-public-shareholding / promoter-disclosure law. The claim hedges correctly with "allegedly", which matches OCCRP's own conditional framing. The SC 2024-01-03 language is confirmed verbatim on Indian Kanoon. An attributed allegation by a named party (OCCRP/Guardian/FT), met by a named denial (Adani Group, 2023-08-31) and a court's refusal to treat it as proof, is exactly what the alleged tier is for. Neither lens refutes the core. The record is still defective in three fixable ways, and none of them changes the tier:
- The contra lit:c014 says "denial not captured", but the denial is one click away. Without a real contra, an alleged edge does not meet SPEC.
- The predicate "enforce" misstates what OCCRP is. It is journalism, not enforcement.
- The edge srcs are Wikipedia only. The Gautam Adani article even overstates the case as "documents which prove", which is stronger than OCCRP's hedged wording. The SC quote is attributed in the claim text, but its source (Indian Kanoon) is attached only to the node, not to the edge.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Replace lit:c014. It should be a real contra: s="adani", t="claim:lit:c013", pred="contra", tier="documented" (the statement's existence is documented), from="2023-08-31", with the "categorically reject these recycled allegations ... Soros-funded interests" quote and the ET URL. Add a second contra from the SC (Vishal Tiwari v UoI, 2024-01-03, paras 39-40, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/188573380/), for example s="SC" pred="contra", with the "cannot be relied on as conclusive proof" quote.
2. Add primary sources to lit:c013's srcs: the OCCRP original (https://www.occrp.org/en/investigations/documents-provide-fresh-insight-into-allegations-of-stock-manipulation-that-rocked-indias-powerful-adani-group), the Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/aug/31/modi-linked-adani-family-secretly-invested-in-own-shares-documents-suggest-india), the FT (https://www.ft.com/content/8d46b435-9725-46d4-80be-2cb3e276c4c9), and Indian Kanoon for the SC quote. Keep Wikipedia as secondary only.
3. Delete "Original not opened in this sweep" from d. It has now been opened.
4. Make d more precise. Name Nasser Ali Shaban Ahli and Chang Chung-Ling, give peak holdings of about $430M, and state the paid advisory link to a Vinod Adani company. Record OCCRP's own conditional: a violation only if they are acting for the promoters, which would push insiders above the 75% MPS cap.
5. Predicate: "enforce" (agency→subject) is wrong for a journalism consortium. Either change the source node's type (ty "agency" is misleading; OCCRP is not a regulator) or use a non-enforcement predicate, if the SPEC allows one. At minimum, flag in lab/d that this is an investigative report and not a proceeding.
6. upgradeIf/killIf: keep them. Note that the SC recorded SEBI's two pending investigations "due to inputs being awaited from foreign regulators" (para 30). I could not verify their current status in this pass because the web-search budget was exhausted. Check any SEBI order since 2024 on the Mauritius FPIs (EIFF / EM Resurgence) before publishing.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, stated as actor/act/object/date: on 2024-11-20 the SEC filed a civil complaint and the EDNY unsealed criminal charges against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Cyril Cabanes over an alleged bribery scheme connected to Adani Green's September 2021 USD 750m note offering. The SEC press release is dated November 20, 2024, and says "The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York today unsealed criminal charges". Gautam Adani chaired Adani Green, and Sagar Adani was an executive director there, for the whole alleged period (about 2020–2024). Cabanes is described as "a former Azure Power board member". The windows overlap, so this passes. The status has moved since then. Wikipedia (not independently verified) says that in May 2026 the NYT reported DOJ was moving to drop the criminal charges. It also says that in September 2026 Judge Garaufis ruled they cannot be dropped until DOJ complies with his instructions, and that the Adanis agreed to accept SEC service in January 2026. The case is therefore still live, so to=null is correct for now.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. The SEC release names "Gautam Adani and Sagar Adani (Adani Green Energy Ltd.) and Cyril Cabanes (Azure Power Global Ltd.)". The node gadani is Gautam Adani, Chairman of the Adani Group, so there is no name collision. Two caveats. (a) The edge target is gadani only, but the text also names Sagar Adani and Cabanes. Cabanes belongs to Azure Power, a rival, not the Adani Group, so the text should not read as though all three acted for Adani Green. (b) The node doj merges DOJ-EDNY and the SEC. That is acceptable because the label says "US DOJ / SEC", but the civil and criminal tracks are now on different paths: DOJ is trying to dismiss while the SEC case continues.
verdicts.baseRate: This is discriminating. A US federal indictment plus SEC fraud complaint against the chairman of an Indian listed energy group is very rare. No other Indian renewables promoter in the reference class has one. Symmetry check: the same US action also charged Azure Power (a rival IPP) executives, including Cabanes. The lens was applied to the competitor too, not selectively to Adani.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is a primary source. The Adani Group media statement of 21 Nov 2024 says: "The allegations made by the US Department of Justice and the US Securities and Exchange Commission against directors of Adani Green are baseless and denied." It adds that the group will "seek all possible legal recourse". URL: https://www.adani.com/newsroom/media-releases/media-statement-1 . The repo also cites Forbes, 30 Nov 2024 ("Adani decries 'baseless' US indictment"): https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2024/11/30/billionaire-gautam-adani-decries-baseless-us-indictment-accusing-him-of-250-million-bribery-scheme/ (403 to fetch, but already cited in other domain files). The contra lit:c018 is therefore wrong to say the denial was "not captured".
verdicts.innocentReading: An indictment and a civil complaint are unproven allegations. The defendants deny them. DOJ under the current administration has reportedly moved to drop the criminal case, which may yet end without any adjudication on the merits. The state power-sale agreements behind the SECI manufacturing-linked tender were also signed by several states through the normal SECI intermediation process. Those signatures alone do not show bribery.
verdicts.reason: Both sources I opened support the substance. The SEC press release is a primary record. It confirms the date (2024-11-20), the named actors, the "hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes to Indian government officials", the USD 750m September 2021 offering with about USD 175m from US investors, and the parallel EDNY charges. Wikipedia supports the "over $250 million" figure in the record's d field. An attributed indictment or complaint fits the 'alleged' tier exactly. The only defect is the required contra. lit:c018 says the denial was not captured, but a primary Adani Group denial exists and was reachable. The contra needs fixing; the claim itself is not refuted. Note that the existence of the proceeding is itself documented, from the SEC primary record. Only the bribery conduct is at the 'alleged' tier.
verdicts.corrections:
1. lit:c018: replace it with a real contra: tier 'reported' (or 'documented' as the party's own primary statement). Set d to the 21-Nov-2024 quote "baseless and denied … seek all possible legal recourse", and srcs to https://www.adani.com/newsroom/media-releases/media-statement-1 plus the Forbes 30-Nov-2024 URL. Drop "denial not captured". Update the lit:c017 text to "Contra (lit:c018): Adani Group denial, 21 Nov 2024".
2. lit:c017 text: attribute Cabanes to Azure Power Global, not to the Adani scheme generally. Suggested wording: "SEC charged Gautam and Sagar Adani (Adani Green) and Cyril Cabanes (Azure Power)…". Make clear that EDNY's criminal counts against Gautam Adani are securities/wire-fraud conspiracy and securities fraud, not FCPA. The FCPA counts were against Azure-linked defendants. This is from background knowledge; the fetched Wikipedia text loosely says "five criminal counts of bribery".
3. Add a status note: January 2026, the Adanis agreed to accept SEC service. May 2026, the NYT reported DOJ moving to drop the criminal charges. September 2026, Judge Garaufis held that charges cannot be dropped until DOJ complies with his instructions. Source: Wikipedia; verify with the docket, 1:24-cr-433 EDNY.
4. killIf: rewrite to "Dismissal on the merits or acquittal". Also add that a voluntary DOJ Rule 48(a) dismissal would end the criminal track without clearing the allegation, and the SEC civil action would continue.
5. Replace Wikipedia as the second source with the EDNY/DOJ press release or the indictment, docket 24-cr-433.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Hindenburg Research alleged, on 2024-08-10, that Madhabi Puri Buch and Dhaval Buch held stakes in IIFL-run offshore funds (IPE Plus / Global Dynamic Opportunities Fund) that were tied to Vinod Adani. The allegation date is right. The Wikipedia Hindenburg page cites the primary report "Whistleblower Documents Reveal SEBI's Chairperson Had Stake…" dated 2024-08-10, and it is still live at https://hindenburgresearch.com/sebi-chairperson/ (HTTP 200). Buch was SEBI chair from March 2022 to February 2025, so the report came out during her tenure. The date of the underlying holding is a problem. The Buchs' rebuttal (Livemint, 2024-08-11) says the money went in in 2015, "almost 2 years before Madhabi joined SEBI, even as a Whole Time Member", and was redeemed in 2018 when Anil Ahuja left as CIO. The Lokpal complaint summary (ET, 2025-05-28) gives the investment as about Rs 5 crore on 12 June 2015. So the holding window was about 2015 to 2018. It overlaps her time as a Whole Time Member (from April 2017) but not her time as chair (from March 2022) or SEBI's Adani probe (from January 2023). The claim text "SEBI chair and husband held stakes" uses her 2024 title and could be read as saying she held the stake while chair. That reading is wrong on dates.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. Madhabi Puri Buch is a unique name, and her office and dates match: SEBI WTM from 2017, chair 2022–2025. Hindenburg Research LLC (Nathan Anderson, founded 2017, wound down January 2025) is also unambiguous. There is no risk of confusing either with someone else. The fund manager is IIFL (India Infoline, now 360 ONE). The primary report says: "these nested funds are managed by Indian Infoline ('IIFL'), now called 360 One". So "IIFL-managed" is supported.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a comparable-class edge. It is one named short-seller's accusation against one regulator. Symmetry check: Hindenburg made similar conflict and short-seller accusations against US targets (Nikola, Icahn, Supermicro), so accusing a regulator this way is not unique to India or to a government-aligned figure. Nothing about the base rate makes the edge non-discriminating. It simply records that an allegation was made.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, found. The Buchs issued a joint statement on 2024-08-10 calling the allegations "baseless" (The Hindu, 2024-08-10, https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/sebi-chief-madhabi-buch-husband-deny-hindenburg-allegations-as-baseless/article68510890.ece). A 15-point rebuttal followed on 2024-08-11 (Livemint, https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/hindenburgadani-case-sebi-chief-madhabi-puri-and-husband-dhaval-buch-respond-to-allegations-attempting-to-attack-11723375754189.html). It says the investment was made in 2015 "almost 2 years before Madhabi joined SEBI", that "when, in 2018, Mr. Ahuja left his position as CIO of the fund, we redeemed the investment", and that "at no point in time did the fund invest in any bond, equity, or derivative of any Adani group company". Buch called the report "character assassination" (The Hindu, 2024-08-11). The Adani Group called it "malicious, mischievous". On 2025-05-28 the Lokpal (six-member bench under Justice A.M. Khanwilkar, 116-page order) dismissed the complaints. The order says: "with not a shred of evidence of any wrongdoing is plainly unjustified and solely politically motivated" (ET, https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/lokpal-gives-clean-chit-to-former-sebi-chief-madhabi-buch-calls-complaints-politically-motivated/articleshow/121467824.cms).
verdicts.innocentReading: In 2015, as private citizens in Singapore, the couple invested in a fund because its CIO was Dhaval Buch's childhood friend. They exited in 2018, years before she became chair and before the Adani probe began. According to the Buchs and Ahuja, the fund never held Adani securities. They say the holdings were disclosed to SEBI. The Lokpal found no evidence of wrongdoing.
verdicts.reason: Both cited sources say what the claim says. The Wikipedia Buch page states: "They alleged that these same funds, managed by IIFL Wealth, were used by Vinod Adani to artificially inflate shares of companies owned by the Adani Group." The primary Hindenburg report is reachable and confirms the date, the IIFL role and the actors. As an attributed short-seller allegation that names a party and carries a contra (lit:c021) plus a dismissal (lit:c022), it meets the bar for 'alleged'. It should not go higher: the only adjudication on record, the Lokpal order of 2025-05-28, went against the allegation. The claim is not refuted, but two things need fixing. First, the edge misuses the 'enforce' predicate: the SPEC defines enforce as agency→subject, and Hindenburg is a private short-seller, not an agency. Second, the text leaves out the 2015–2018 holding window, which is what decides whether a conflict could have touched the Adani probe as chair.
verdicts.corrections: (1) pred: 'enforce' is wrong because Hindenburg is not an agency. Use the closest valid predicate, or keep the edge only if the schema is extended with an allegation predicate. At minimum, flag this to the schema owner. Do not present it as an enforcement action. (2) text/d: add the holding window: "stake invested 12 Jun 2015 (~Rs 5 cr per Lokpal complaint summary), redeemed 2018 per the Buchs, i.e. before her March 2022 chairship and before SEBI's Adani probe; overlapped her WTM tenure from April 2017". Replace "SEBI chair and husband held stakes" with "Buch (SEBI chair at the time of the report) and her husband had held stakes 2015–2018". (3) srcs: add the primary report https://hindenburgresearch.com/sebi-chairperson/ (2024-08-10). (4) The killIf condition, "funds held no Adani exposure while she was chair", is met on the Buchs' own account because the stake was redeemed in 2018. Reword killIf to cover the WTM period (2017–2018) so the edge is not killed on a technicality. (5) lit:c022: the date is known to the day, 2025-05-28 (ET, 116-page order, Khanwilkar bench), so replace "month-level" with from=2025-05-28 and add the ET URL. The Lokpal order is a primary record, so c022 could go up to documented once the order or ET is cited. (6) lit:c021: the first "baseless" statement is dated 2024-08-10 (The Hindu); the detailed rebuttal and "character assassination" are 2024-08-11. Set from=2024-08-10 and add The Hindu and Livemint URLs as primary-press sources instead of relying only on Wikipedia.

verdicts.dateTest: CAG (Gujarat PSU audit report) flagged GSPC selling gas to Adani Energy below its spot purchase cost. The report was tabled in the Gujarat Assembly on Friday 30 March 2012, per The Hindu, 31 March 2012. The sales fall within the audit period (the KG-basin findings cite 2007-11). Modi was Chief Minister of Gujarat from 7 Oct 2001 to 22 May 2014, so the dates overlap. The claim's "2012" is correct at year level. It can be sharpened to from=2012-03-30, the tabling date.
verdicts.identityTest: Wikipedia says only "a Gujarat state-run gas company" and "Adani and other businesspeople". The Hindu, which Wikipedia cites, names the parties: Gujarat State Petroleum Corporation (GSPC), a Gujarat state PSU, and "Adani Energy". In 2012 that was Adani Energy Ltd, the group's city-gas-distribution arm, later Adani Gas and now Adani Total Gas. The group-level node "adani" is acceptable, but a subsidiary node would be more precise. The "other businesspeople" is specifically Essar Steel, which got a Rs 12.02 crore capacity-charge waiver. The CAG node is correct: the Comptroller and Auditor-General, through its state audit wing. No name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: The finding does not single out Adani. The same CAG report says GSPC suffered trading losses from "undue favours extended to buyers by way of non-recovery of 'Take or Pay' charges and sale of gas and oil at prices below purchase cost", which covers several buyers, Essar Steel among them. CAG reports on state PSUs routinely flag below-cost sales and "undue benefit" in every state, whichever party governs, so an audit observation alone is common. What is specific here is a named fixed price for Adani Energy, lower than GSPC's spot purchase cost, with a quantified benefit of over Rs 70 crore. The finding is partially discriminating, not unique.
verdicts.denialFound: Gujarat government response (dated, and more specific than lit:c024): Cabinet spokesman Jaynarayan Vyas "said the report was based only on accounting figures. Certain decisions required to be taken from time to time for the larger benefit of the people did not come into the CAG's consideration", and he expected the Public Accounts Committee to "give a clean chit". Source: The Hindu, 31 Mar 2012, https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/cag-slams-modi-regime-for-financial-irregularities/article3263639.ece. I found no Adani-specific response to the GSPC finding, and the article does not say whether Adani was asked. The general cronyism denial in lit:c024 rests on BBC, 2 Dec 2022 (https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-63817883), per the Wikipedia footnote. That page was unreachable here, so the quote is not verified.
verdicts.innocentReading: GSPC likely signed a fixed-price, long-term supply contract with Adani Energy's city-gas business when spot LNG prices were lower. It then kept supplying at the contract price after spot prices rose, so a trading loss came from contract terms rather than a discretionary gift. That fits the CAG's broader finding that GSPC was badly run as a gas trader and lost money on several buyers. It also fits the state's reply that the audit was an accounting-only view. A CAG observation is an audit finding that the PAC had not yet considered, not a finding of corruption.
verdicts.reason: The claim holds. Wikipedia is only a tertiary source, but its footnote is The Hindu (Manas Dasgupta, 31 Mar 2012), which I retrieved with curl. It says directly: "The CAG report said the GSPC purchased natural gas from the spot market at the prevailing prices and sold it to Adani Energy at a fixed price much lower than the market price, benefiting the private company to the tune of over Rs. 70 crore." It also says the CAG criticised GSPC for "extending 'undue benefits' to the Chief Minister's 'favoured few,' mainly Adani Energy and Essar Steel". That is one credible outlet reporting on a published audit document, which meets the bar for "reported". It does not reach "documented": the CAG report itself was not opened, and I found no second independent outlet (the search budget was exhausted). The record's weaknesses are fixable. It cites Wikipedia instead of The Hindu, leaves out the amount and the exact date, and its contra is an undated general denial even though a dated Gujarat government response exists.
verdicts.corrections: 1) srcs: replace or add The Hindu, "CAG slams Modi regime for financial irregularities", 31 Mar 2012, https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/cag-slams-modi-regime-for-financial-irregularities/article3263639.ece. Keep Wikipedia only as a pointer. 2) from: "2012-03-30" (report tabled in the Gujarat Assembly on the last day of the budget session). Remove the "year-level only" caveat. 3) benefit.amountCr: 70 (the source says "over Rs. 70 crore"); confidence: "reported". benefit.how: "GSPC bought gas on the spot market and sold it to Adani Energy at a fixed price much lower than market (CAG)". 4) d/text: name GSPC and Adani Energy Ltd, and replace "other businesspeople" with "Essar Steel (Rs 12.02 cr capacity-charge waiver)". Note that the CAG said GSPC sold below cost to buyers in general. 5) t: consider a subsidiary node for Adani Energy Ltd (now Adani Total Gas) instead of group-level "adani". 6) Add a contra, or amend lit:c024: Gujarat government (Jaynarayan Vyas, 30/31 Mar 2012) said the report was based only on accounting figures and ignored decisions taken for the public benefit. Source: The Hindu, same URL. Make s = the Gujarat government node. Keep lit:c024 but cite BBC 2 Dec 2022 directly, and mark its denial "not specific to the GSPC finding; Adani response to the CAG finding: none found, not reported as asked". 7) killIf remains valid. The Hindu says GSPC also sold below cost to buyers in general, so the uniform-pricing reading is not ruled out until the report itself is read. upgradeIf: the CAG Report (Commercial), Government of Gujarat, year ended 31 March 2011, GSPC performance-audit chapter, or a second independent outlet from March 2012.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Karnataka Lokayukta (N. Santosh Hegde) submitted its illegal-mining report accusing CM B.S. Yeddyurappa on 2011-07-27. Actor window: Yeddyurappa was Chief Minister from May 2008 to his forced resignation in late July/August 2011. The Tribune (2016, PTI) says: "forced to resign as the CM in August 2011 following indictment by then Lokayukta Santosh Hegde". The CBI chargesheet period is given as "during Yeddyurappa's chief ministership from 2008 to 2011". The windows overlap, so the date test passes. The Tribune dateline is "Bangalore, July 27": "Karnataka Lokayukta Santosh Hegde's report on illegal mining, submitted to the state government here today, accused Chief Minister BS Yeddyurappa of corruption."
verdicts.identityTest: Target: the person node (B.S. Yeddyurappa, sitting CM) is unambiguous. Source node: Karnataka Lokayukta, report submitted by registrar MKN Mule to Chief Secretary SV Ranganath, is unambiguous. Nuance: the money did not go to Yeddyurappa personally. The donation went to "the Prerna Trust run by Yeddyurappa's two sons (including Raghavendra...)", and the land was sold by "Yeddyurappa's kin" / "CM's sons". The payer's identity can now be partly resolved. The 2016 Tribune/PTI report says the 2012 CBI chargesheet named "Prerana Trust, managed by Raghavendra, South West Mining Company and Bellary-based JSW Steel" as co-accused. Deccan Herald's summary also describes the case as a quid pro quo that favoured JSW Steel, with South West Mining Ltd as the payer. So the "Jindal group" is the JSW (Sajjan Jindal) group, not JSPL or Jindal Stainless, at reported tier. No CIN has been opened yet.
verdicts.baseRate: The report named many parties: ex-CM H.D. Kumaraswamy (JD(S)), the Reddy brothers, minister V. Somanna, Congress MP Anil Lad, and about 100 companies. Being named in it therefore does not discriminate on its own. The CM-specific counts do. Only Yeddyurappa's family trust is said to have received a Rs 10 cr donation and a land premium of about 14x guidance value (Rs 20 cr vs Rs 1.4 cr), so the edge discriminates. Symmetry: the same report indicted Kumaraswamy (opposition JD(S)) and named a Congress MP, and the claim graph should carry those edges in the same way. The lens is not partisan.
verdicts.denialFound: A response was found, and it is on the claim's own source page, so the record's statement "Denial not captured" is wrong. The Tribune, 28 Jul 2011 (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2011/20110728/main1.htm), quotes Yeddyurappa: "It appears that there is a repetition of old points on (illegal) mining in the report. Most of the points are pending before the Supreme Court and the high court." A later search summary says Yeddyurappa "rejected" the charge that the payments to Prerana Trust were made in anticipation of favours. Outcome (contra): on 2016-10-26 a special CBI court (Judge R.B. Dharmagouder) acquitted Yeddyurappa, his two sons, his son-in-law and nine others in the Rs 40 crore mining-bribery case (Prerana Trust / South West Mining / JSW). The court held that "The prosecution has been unsuccessful in establishing the guilt of the accused, not only under the Prevention of Corruption Act, but also under the Indian Penal Code" (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/yeddy-3-of-family-acquitted-in-rs-40-crore-mining-bribery-case-315374). Deccan Herald reported that the court found no "iota of evidence" of abuse of official position (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/578267/yeddyurappa-12-accused-not-conspirators.html; this page did not render when fetched and is cited from the search summary). Whether the CBI appealed was not checked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Corporate donations to educational or social trusts are common. A private land sale above guidance value can happen when there is location or development demand; guidance values in Bengaluru were often far below market in 2008-11. Yeddyurappa's own response was that the report repeated points already before the courts. In 2016 a trial court found that the prosecution had not proven conspiracy or abuse of office. None of this changes the fact that the Lokayukta made the accusation on 2011-07-27, and that fact is what this enforce edge asserts.
verdicts.reason: The edge survives because it records an official act, not guilt. The Lokayukta accused the sitting CM on 2011-07-27, and the cited Tribune report quotes Hegde on the record with every figure: Rs 10 crore to Prerana Trust from South West Mining ("affiliated to the Jindal group"), and a plot near Bangalore airport sold for Rs 20 crore against a Rs 1.4 crore guidance value. The chronology holds. "Reported" is the correct tier: one credible outlet with a named source (Hegde, speaking to the media). The record around the edge has two material errors, though. (1) It says the denial was "not captured", but Yeddyurappa's response is printed on the same source page. (2) It leaves out that a special CBI court acquitted Yeddyurappa and his family of these very counts on 2016-10-26. That meets the record's own killIf ("Courts discharged him on these counts"). The acquittal does not kill the edge, because the report's accusation stays a historical fact. It does falsify the benefit block, which presents Rs 28.6 cr as a benefit to Yeddyurappa. Publish the edge only with these corrections.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Text/d: replace "Denial not captured" with Yeddyurappa's response from the same Tribune page: "It appears that there is a repetition of old points on (illegal) mining in the report. Most of the points are pending before the Supreme Court and the high court." 2. Add a contra edge answering claim:mines:c045 for the special CBI court acquittal of 2016-10-26 (all 13 accused, including Yeddyurappa, sons B.Y. Raghavendra and B.Y. Vijayendra, and son-in-law R.N. Sohan Kumar). Source: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/yeddy-3-of-family-acquitted-in-rs-40-crore-mining-bribery-case-315374. Consider an energy:cbi enforce edge for the 2012 chargesheet that named Prerana Trust, South West Mining and JSW Steel. 3. killIf: rewrite it. The acquittal has occurred, and it does not kill an edge whose claim is "the report accused". Suggested: "Kill only if the report is shown not to contain these findings." Move the acquittal into the contra/outcome. 4. benefit: the named beneficiary is wrong. The trust was run by the sons and the land was sold by the sons, so set benefit.who to the Prerana Trust / sons, or drop it. Mark amountCr 28.6 as "alleged by Lokayukta; accused acquitted 2016"; it should not stand as an estimated benefit. 5. Text: say the land was sold by "CM's sons/kin", not by the CM. 6. South West Mining node: the CBI chargesheet (via PTI/Tribune 2016) names it together with JSW Steel, so add alias "South West Mining Ltd". Record the group as JSW (Sajjan Jindal) at reported tier, pending CIN lookup, and update collisionRisk accordingly. 7. Note the amount discrepancy: the Lokayukta reported Rs 10 cr to Prerana, while the CBI chargesheet reportedly says Rs 20 cr to Prerana within Rs 40 cr total kickbacks. 8. Change "resigned within days (from search summaries, not opened)" to "forced to resign in August 2011 following the indictment", citing the opened 2016 Tribune/PTI article.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Karnataka Lokayukta (Justice N. Santosh Hegde) found that H.D. Kumaraswamy showed misconduct in granting two mining leases while he was CM. The report was submitted on 2011-07-27. Kumaraswamy was CM from 3 Feb 2006 to about 8 Oct 2007. The best-known of the two leases, Sri Sai Venkateshwara Minerals (550 acres, Sandur), dates to 2007. That falls inside both his tenure and the report's 2006-10 investigation window, so the dates overlap. His current post, Union Minister of Heavy Industries and Steel, is correctly dated 2024-06-10 onward (the day portfolios were allocated). The edge's from=2011-07-27 is the report date, which is correct. Both the claim and the node already say 2006-07; any "2006-08" tenure in secondary search summaries is wrong and should not be copied.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The Tribune names "JD(S) leader and former Chief Minister HD Kumaraswamy". He is a unique public figure, so there is no name-collision risk. The target node pol:hd-kumaraswamy (office: Union Minister of Heavy Industries and Steel 2024-06-10 onward; former CM Karnataka, JD(S)) is the same person. The source node, energy:karnataka-lokayukta under Justice Santosh Hegde, is the body that wrote the 27 Jul 2011 report.
verdicts.baseRate: The finding does not single out one party. The same report named sitting BJP CM Yeddyurappa (indicted under the Prevention of Corruption Act), BJP ministers Janardhana and Karunakara Reddy, V. Somanna and H. Sriramulu, Congress MP Anil Lad's family, and about 100 companies and 787 officials. It covered 134 leases granted between 2001 and 2008 under Congress, JD(S) and BJP chief ministers. Applying the same test to a rival gives the same kind of edge (see c045 for BSY and c047 for the Reddys). Having an edge from this report is therefore not unusual for a Karnataka politician of the period. But the specific finding of "misconduct" in two leases he personally sanctioned is specific to him, not generic.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, a denial exists. The claim's "Denial not captured" is out of date. The Week (31 Aug 2024) quotes Kumaraswamy: "a note-sheet sent to me had three lines of typed matter and a handwritten line―'M/s Sai Venkateshwara'―just before my signature. The line was not in my handwriting." He also said "The SIT has filed no report even after seven years", and that in 2015 he took anticipatory bail rather than being arrested. He has also publicly attacked the Lokayukta SIT's head, an ADGP, calling him a "blackmailer" (Deccan Herald, Sept 2024; that page returned 403, so this is from the search snippet only). Source: https://www.theweek.in/theweek/statescan/2024/08/31/union-minister-h-d-kumaraswamy-cries-foul-as-the-illegal-mining-related-case-against-him-gathers-pace.html. I found no contemporaneous 2011 response.
verdicts.innocentReading: He says the lease-approval file was altered: the beneficiary's name was added by hand above his signature, and it is not his handwriting. On this reading, bureaucrats inserted the choice of lessee, and the CM signed a routine note-sheet during the 2001-08 rush of lease grants that the report itself blames on "pressures and political compulsions" across governments. The report also did not recommend action against him, because he held no public post in 2011. It only said the government was free to act on his "misconduct". No court has yet made a finding against him. The Governor's prosecution sanction was sought in Nov 2023 and again in Aug 2024, and was still pending as of Feb 2025 per search results.
verdicts.reason: The main fact holds and is quoted in the source. The Tribune of 28 Jul 2011 (opened, HTTP 200) says: "In Kumaraswamy's case, the probe found \"misconduct\" on his part in granting 2 mining leases." It also says: "Hegde said the former Chief Minister was named in his report in connection with mining leases that he had controversially sanctioned to two companies during his tenure." A second, independent outlet opened via WebFetch (The Week, 31 Aug 2024) quotes the report directly: "However, it is open for the government to take appropriate action against him for his misconduct". It adds that the report "would not recommend action against Kumaraswamy, as he was not holding a public post". Dates and identity both pass. Two independent credible outlets meet the SPEC bar for documented. The claim's caveats are what need fixing: a denial does exist, and the prosecution track is traceable (a Lokayukta SIT case, with the Governor's sanction pending). The claim also leaves out that the report itself declined to recommend action against him.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Add The Week, 31 Aug 2024 as a second source (URL above). That lets the tier go up to documented under the SPEC's two-outlet rule. If you want the report text itself opened first, keep it at reported. 2. Replace "Denial not captured" with his denial: the note-sheet line "M/s Sai Venkateshwara" was "not in my handwriting" (The Week 2024). Add a matching contra edge from pol:hd-kumaraswamy to claim:mines:c046. 3. Add that the report did not recommend action against him because he held no public post in 2011; it said only that the government was free to act on his "misconduct". 4. Replace "outcome of any prosecution unverified" with the actual status: a Lokayukta SIT case over the Sri Sai Venkateshwara Minerals lease (2007, 550 acres, Sandur); he took anticipatory bail in 2015; the SIT sought the Governor's sanction on 2023-11-21 and again on 2024-08-19; it was still pending as of Aug 2024 per The Week and as of Feb 2025 per search results (not opened). 5. Name at least one of the two leases (SSVM) in the claim text. 6. killIf is fine as written ("Sanction for prosecution refused or case closed on merits").

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Karnataka Lokayukta (Justice N. Santosh Hegde) named G. Janardhana Reddy in its illegal-mining report, submitted on 2011-07-27. Reddy was a Karnataka cabinet minister in the Yeddyurappa BJP government from 2008 until the cabinet changed in August 2011. That means he was in office on the report date, so the dates overlap. The source is datelined "Bangalore, July 27" (The Tribune, 28 Jul 2011). The 'from' value of 2011-07-27 is correct. The Sept 2011 CBI arrest is correctly marked as not coming from an opened source.
verdicts.identityTest: The source says "the two Reddy brothers, Janardhana and Karunakara, both Cabinet ministers in Karnataka" and "Reddy brothers (ministers in K'taka Govt and mining magnates)". It also refers to the brothers' mining activity in Andhra Pradesh, meaning OMC/Obulapuram. That fits only Gali Janardhana Reddy. Reddy is a common surname, but pairing the first name with the brother Karunakara, the office and the date removes the collision risk. The node's DIN and CIN are null, which is fine for a politician identified by office and dates.
verdicts.baseRate: The report named about 100 companies and 787 officials, so being named is not unusual among Bellary mining operators. Among Karnataka cabinet ministers, though, only about five of roughly 34 were named: Yeddyurappa, the two Reddy brothers, Sriramulu and Somanna. That makes it discriminating at the minister level. On symmetry, the same report named JD(S) leader Kumaraswamy (in the graph as c046) and Congress MP Anil Lad, or his wife. Lad is not in the graph, and neither are Karunakara Reddy, Sriramulu or Somanna. That is a partisan-coverage gap, although it does not affect this edge.
verdicts.denialFound: No direct denial of the report after publication was found. Reporters did ask: DH, "In trouble, Reddys avoid media" (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/179617/in-trouble-reddys-avoid-media.html), says the brothers avoided the press and met the CM privately. The cited source itself records their position before the report, which works as the contra: "the two Reddy brothers, who have been claiming that their mining activity was confined to Andhra Pradesh and they were not involved in mining in Karnataka" (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2011/20110728/main1.htm). Hegde is reported elsewhere as saying: "They (OMC) may deny many times... But we have said they did engage in that through documents we produced."
verdicts.innocentReading: Being "named" in a Lokayukta report is a recommendation from an ombudsman, not a finding by a court. The Lokayukta cannot prosecute on its own, and the report named about 890 companies and officials. So the edge on its own records only that he was named, not that he was guilty. The Reddys' position was that their mining was in Andhra Pradesh (OMC), not Karnataka.
verdicts.reason: The source opens and says exactly what the claim says. The Tribune, 28 Jul 2011, reports that the report "also names the two Reddy brothers, Janardhana and Karunakara, both Cabinet ministers in Karnataka, V Somanna, also a member of the Yeddyurappa-led Cabinet." The actor, office, date and co-named persons all match. It is one credible outlet quoting the Lokayukta by name at his press conference, which meets the bar for 'reported'. It is not 'documented' because the report text itself has not been opened and there is no second independent outlet that explicitly says he was named. The claim is worded narrowly ("named"), so it does not imply guilt.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add to 'd' the contra that the same source contains: the Reddy brothers had claimed their mining was confined to Andhra Pradesh and they were not involved in mining in Karnataka. Also add that they avoided the media after the report (DH 179617), so no post-report denial is on record. 2) Add H. Sriramulu to the list of co-named ministers; the Tribune sidebar names him as well. 3) The predicate 'enforce' overstates what the Lokayukta did, which was to recommend prosecution. Add wording to the label such as 'named; PCA prosecution recommended (not adjudicated)'. 4) Add a killIf in place of 'n/a': 'report text shows he was not named, or courts discharged him on the Lokayukta counts'. 5) Symmetry gap: consider adding edges for Anil Lad (Congress), Karunakara Reddy, Sriramulu and Somanna, taken from the same source. 6) upgradeIf: open the Lokayukta report (part II, 2011) or a second independent outlet (e.g. The Hindu or DH, 27–28 Jul 2011) that explicitly says he was named.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, as a sentence: in 2022 the ECI, acting on a reference from the Governor under Art. 192, held s.9A RPA proceedings against CM and Mines Minister Hemant Soren over a stone lease at Angara. Soren's tenure as CM ran from 2019-12-29 to 2024-02-02, so the dates overlap. Deccan Herald (DH, 27 Aug 2022) sets out the sequence. In Feb 2022 Raghubar Das (BJP) made the allegation and Shivshankar Sharma filed a PIL. The ECI then issued a s.9A notice with a hearing set for May 31, moved to June 14 and then June 28. DH 25 Aug 2022 reports the opinion 'was sent to the Jharkhand Raj Bhavan in a sealed cover' that morning. The from/to window of 2022-05-01 to 2022-08-31 is reasonable. The allegation that the lease was allotted while he held office is contested. Soren says he 'had applied for the mining lease at a time when he was not holding any office of profit', so the date of application versus the date of grant is still open. Neither opened source supports 'never published or acted on'.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. Both sources name Hemant Soren, Chief Minister of Jharkhand, JMM, and DH names him as Minister of Mines. There is no risk of a name collision. The ECI is correctly the source node. One caveat: under Art. 192 the ECI gives the Governor an opinion; the Governor makes the decision. So an 'enforce' edge from ECI to Soren is acceptable, but the proceeding was started by the BJP's petition to the Governor, not by the ECI itself.
verdicts.baseRate: Discriminating. Few sitting chief ministers have faced an Art. 192 / s.9A disqualification reference over a lease in their own name. This is not an industry-wide property, so the ≥80% non-discrimination test does not apply. Symmetry: the lens is party-neutral. The complainant was the BJP (Raghubar Das) against a JMM chief minister, and the Governor was a centrally appointed BJP former MP. That partisan setting is part of Soren's defence and has to be recorded.
verdicts.denialFound: FOUND, in the claim's own cited source. The claim says his denial was 'NOT captured in opened sources'; that is wrong. DH 27 Aug 2022 (https://www.deccanherald.com/national/east-and-northeast/storm-brewing-for-jharkhand-cm-soren-heres-what-we-know-so-far-1139789.html): "In his defence, Soren has said that he had applied for the mining lease at a time when he was not holding any office of profit and he has now even surrendered the lease. Moreover, no mining activity has been undertaken by him in the mine in question, thus no question of misusing office of profit arises." The same article says that in an Interlocutory Application (IA) to the Supreme Court, Soren accused the PIL petitioner of trying to tarnish his image and said the PILs rested on false information. DH 25 Aug 2022 (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/ec-favours-disqualification-of-jharkhand-cm-soren-as-mla-raj-bhavan-sources-1139272.html) quotes his secretariat: 'No communication in this regard has been received by the Chief Minister's Office', and Soren: 'It seems that BJP leaders including a BJP MP and his puppet journalists have themselves drafted the ECI report'.
verdicts.innocentReading: Soren may have applied for the lease, or had it renewed, before he held office. He says he surrendered it, and no mining took place. Section 9A covers contracts 'for the supply of goods to, or for the execution of any works undertaken by' the government. Whether a mining lease is such a contract is legally doubtful: Soren argued it is not, and the Governor never acted. The disqualification 'recommendation' rests only on unnamed Raj Bhavan sources, which the Raj Bhavan officially did not confirm, and a BJP MP (Nishikant Dubey) announced it in advance. The content of the opinion has never been verified.
verdicts.reason: The central charge rests on anonymous sourcing, and the claim misstates its own evidence. DH 25 Aug: 'The Election Commission of India is believed to have told ... Governor Ramesh Bais that ... Soren should be disqualified ... Raj Bhavan sources said. However, Raj Bhavan has officially not confirmed the development.' DH 27 Aug frames it as 'speculation that the Election Commission has recommended'. That falls short of the 'reported' bar, which needs named sourcing or published documents. The self-allotment is an allegation by named parties (Raghubar Das/BJP; PIL petitioner Shivshankar Sharma), and a substantive contra exists in the cited DH article: applied before holding office, lease surrendered, no mining done. The claim says no denial was captured, which is false. Wikipedia is not independent; its only citation (ref 12) is the same DH 25 Aug report. The facts that do meet 'reported' are narrower: an s.9A notice was issued, hearings were held May–June 2022, and an opinion was sent in a sealed cover on 25 Aug 2022. The edge as written, with 'self-allotted' plus 'recommending disqualification', should be 'alleged' with a contra.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change the tier from 'reported' to 'alleged', or split the claim: (a) 'reported' for 'ECI issued s.9A notice; hearings May 31 → June 14 → June 28 2022; opinion sent to Governor in sealed cover 2022-08-25'; (b) 'alleged' for 'opinion recommended disqualification (Raj Bhavan sources, unconfirmed)' and for the self-allotment. 2) Delete 'Soren's substantive denial NOT captured in opened sources — weakness' and the 'd' text 'his substantive response was not captured'. Add a contra edge (s: energy:pol-hemant-soren, t: claim:mines:c048) quoting DH 27 Aug: applied when not holding office of profit, lease surrendered, no mining activity. Also add the CMO statement from DH 25 Aug. 3) Change the 'Deccan Herald, 27 Aug 2022' source: the opinion-sent/recommendation fact comes from DH 25 Aug 2022 (…ec-favours-disqualification-of-jharkhand-cm-soren-as-mla-raj-bhavan-sources-1139272.html). Add that URL and describe the sourcing as 'unnamed Raj Bhavan sources, officially unconfirmed'. 4) Mark 'never published or acted on' as unsourced by the opened sources, or source it. 5) Name the complainant (BJP / Raghubar Das, Feb 2022) and the Art. 192 route: Governor refers to ECI, ECI gives an opinion. 6) Remove 'Barhait constituency' from the identity basis unless a source that names it is cited; neither opened source mentions it. 7) Set the killIf wording to match the evidence: the lease-surrender defence is now captured, so killIf should test whether the surrender happened before the complaint.

verdicts.dateTest: NMDC-CMDC Ltd terminated AEL's Deposit-13 iron-ore mining services agreement by a CEO letter dated 2023-08-28. The agreement ran from 2018-12-06 to 2023-08-28. The New Indian Express adds that the show-cause notice was issued on 2023-07-11. FPJ published on 2023-09-28 00:28 IST and NIE on 2023-09-27. NCL was the contracting party for the whole window, so the dates line up. Pass.
verdicts.identityTest: Both outlets name the same two parties: 'NMDC-CMDC Ltd (as joint venture company NCL)' and 'Adani Enterprises Ltd (AEL)'. Both describe the same deposit, Bailadila Deposit-13 at Kirandul, Dantewada, and the same agreement, dated 6 December 2018. There is no risk of a name collision. The NCL node has no CIN (cin null), but the identity is clear from context. Pass. One side note: the '51:49' split in the node's sub-field and in c051 does not appear in the FPJ article, which says only 'a joint venture of NMDC and CMDC'.
verdicts.baseRate: Termination of a stalled MDO or mining-services contract for non-performance is routine among PSU contracts that never started. The discriminating feature here is that an Adani entity lost a contract. The benefit runs against the group, so the edge does not feed a favour inference in either direction. No base-rate objection to recording the event.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it contradicts the claim. verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: the Union Cabinet approved two Tata semiconductor units on 2024-02-29, and Progressive Electoral Trust gave BJP Rs 757.6 cr on 2024-04-02. Scroll gives both dates: "On February 29, 2024, the Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi approved three semiconductor units", and the Tata firms paid PET Rs 915 cr on April 2, 2024, which PET passed to ten parties the same day. The order holds, so the chronology is not collapsed. The gap is 33 days (about 4.7 weeks), so "4–6 weeks" should be written as "33 days". The record's `to` field (2024-04-30) should be 2024-04-02. One date is wrong. The claim says "nil receipts FY21–FY24", but Scroll says "Between 2021-'22 and 2023-'24, the trust did not make any donations." That is nil donations over FY22–FY24, not nil receipts over FY21–FY24. Other reporting says PET's 2019-20 filings "went missing".
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The money came from 15 Tata firms (Tata Sons Pvt Ltd Rs 308 cr, TCS Rs 217.6 cr, Tata Steel Rs 173 cr, among others). They paid Progressive Electoral Trust, and PET paid BJP. Scroll, The Wire, Maktoob and Al Jazeera all identify PET as Tata-controlled. There is no risk of a name collision. The edge grp:tata→bjp skips the trust in the middle. The file already has separate edges for grp:tata→progressive and progressive→bjp, so the analytic edge should point to those rather than stand as a money edge of its own. Separately, the progressive→bjp edge (line ~3603) says "Rs 834.97 cr in two donations per BJP's report". That does not match Rs 757.62 cr and needs its own check.
verdicts.baseRate:
The pattern does not pick Tata out.
(a) BJP's share: PET gave about 83% of its FY25 payouts to BJP. Across all electoral trusts that year, BJP got about 82% of Rs 3,811 cr (Deccan Herald / The Wire). Tata's split is the same as everyone else's.
(b) "Dormant, then a large payment": PET gives only in Lok Sabha election years. It gave nothing in 2014–2017, gave Rs 454 cr in FY2018-19 (about 75%, or Rs 356 cr, to BJP), gave nothing again in FY22–FY24, then gave Rs 915 cr in April 2024. In both of its last two election cycles, the "revival" came right before the general election.
(c) Symmetry: the same Cabinet decision on 29 Feb 2024 also approved a third unit, the CG Power/Murugappa OSAT. On the opposition side, PET gave Congress Rs 77.3 cr and eight other parties Rs 10 cr each, including TMC and DMK. By the "approval preceded donation" test, those look just as suspicious, and the same donation also went to parties that approved nothing for Tata. Any big donor group that got a central approval in the six weeks before a general election would pass this test.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Tata was asked and did not answer. Scroll (27 Nov 2025): "Scroll sent questions to a spokesperson of Tata Sons about the timing of the donations to the BJP but had not received a response at the time of publication. Questions sent to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology...also went unanswered." Al Jazeera (18 Feb 2026, https://aljazeera.com/features/2026/2/18/quid-pro-quo-how-indian-firms-fund-parties-whose-governments-help-them): "Al Jazeera reached out to the Tata Group, the Murugappa Group and the Election Commission of India ... but it has not yet received any response." That makes two outlets that asked and got no reply. c043 should cite both.
verdicts.innocentReading: PET gives only in Lok Sabha election years: 2018-19 and 2024-25, with nothing in between. The April 2024 payment was made days before polling began, so the election calendar alone explains when it happened. The approval date is not needed to explain it. The 83% BJP share matches the 82% BJP share of all electoral-trust money in FY25, and the same payment also went to Congress, TMC, DMK and others. The semiconductor support is a published scheme that pays 50% of project cost to every approved applicant. The same Cabinet decision also approved a non-Tata unit, CG Power/Murugappa.
verdicts.reason:
The main sequence is real and sourced: the approval on 2024-02-29, the Rs 757.6 cr to BJP on 2024-04-02, and no reply from Tata or MeitY. As an analytic edge it needs no more than that. But the claim as written has two errors, and its innocent reading is wrong and misses the strongest explanation.
(1) "declared nil receipts FY21–FY24": the source says no donations, and only from 2021-22 to 2023-24.
(2) "trusts were the only lawful corporate channel left": this is false. Direct company donations under s.182 of the Companies Act 2013 were still lawful after the Supreme Court struck down electoral bonds on 2024-02-15.
The documented pattern that actually explains the timing is left out: PET has given money only in Lok Sabha election years, in 2018-19 and 2024-25. Once that is added, together with the 82% base rate for BJP's share of all trust money, the sequence says nothing specific about Tata. The edge can stay only as a correctly worded analytic sequence with the corrected innocent reading. The alternative is to demote it to context on the PET node. It must not be phrased so that the approval appears to explain the timing.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: <three Reliance Group companies> <hold 50% of Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd> <as of the 21 Mar 2024 report>. The bond purchases ran from 12 Apr 2019 to 24 Jan 2024, with ₹360 cr in FY2021-22. The source gives only a present-tense holding in March 2024 and no acquisition date. The edge's from=2024-03-15 is honest about this. However, the claim text says the holding "bears directly on the 'Reliance bought no bonds' void", which assumes the holding existed when the bonds were bought in FY22. No source in hand shows that. The date test is not failed, but the overlap is unverified. The needed record is Qwik's MGT-7 shareholder lists for FY2021-22.
verdicts.identityTest: Partial. Qwik end: 'Qwik Supply Chain Pvt. Ltd.', Mumbai, matches both sources, but the node has cin=null. Reliance end: The Hindu says "Three Reliance Group companies" without naming them or saying which Ambani group. Frontline says only "the Reliance group". 'Reliance Group' is also the trade name of Anil Ambani's ADAG, so fusing this with grp:reliance (alias 'Reliance Industries group', Mukesh Ambani) rests on context, not on an identifier. Moneylife (Mar 2024) names one shareholder: 'Reliance Group Support Services Pvt Ltd', 16.60%, from MCA data posted by CA Himank Singla on X. That fits three holders of about 16.67% each, which makes up 50%. It does not by itself settle which group owns that company. The Frontline passage sits beside a sentence about Mukesh Ambani's flagship companies being absent, which supports RIL, but no source ties the three holders to RIL with a CIN.
verdicts.baseRate: Reference class: the top-50 electoral-bond purchasers. Buying bonds through a group affiliate rather than the flagship is common: MEIL bought through its subsidiary Western UP Power Transmission (₹220 cr), Bharti bought through group entities, and RP-Sanjiv Goenka through Haldia Energy. So "a group's money reached parties through a group company" is not discriminating (roughly 30-50% of large groups did it). What stands out is narrower. A company 50% held by a large conglomerate that is otherwise completely absent from the list bought ₹360 cr in one fiscal year on ₹21.72 cr net profit, and its share capital was only ₹130 cr (Moneylife). Very few of the top 50 (under 10%) show purchases many times their annual profit. Symmetry check: the same lens applied to MEIL/WUPPTCL (money also went to INC ₹110 cr, BRS and DMK) or to Haldia (₹281 cr to AITC) gives equally striking rows, so affiliate routing alone should not be read as unique to Reliance.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, but it answers a narrower point. Frontline (15 Mar 2024, reprinted by ADR) says: "Qwik, a company purportedly with links to the Reliance group, although Reliance has denied it is a subsidiary, has raised eyebrows as it bought electoral bonds worth Rs.360 crore in the 2021-22 fiscal year, when its net profit was only Rs.21.72 crore." https://adrindia.org/content/eci-reveals-electoral-bonds-data-bjp-tops-beneficiary-list-biggest-donor-little-known-future. The denial rejects subsidiary status, not the 50% holding. The two are consistent, since a 50% holding by three separate companies need not make Qwik a subsidiary of any one of them. I could not find any denial of the 50% figure itself (search budget exhausted).
verdicts.innocentReading: Qwik is an operating warehousing and supply-chain company. Reliance-affiliated entities hold a non-controlling 50%, split across three holders, and Qwik chose to donate on its own. Section 182 of the Companies Act was amended by the Finance Act 2017 to remove the 7.5%-of-profit cap, so donating more than net profit was lawful. The money could have come from reserves, borrowings or capital rather than FY22 profit. Reliance's "not a subsidiary" statement is accurate on these facts. Because Qwik also gave ₹25 cr to the Shiv Sena, it was not an exclusively single-party donor.
verdicts.reason: The key sentence is confirmed word for word in the source. The Hindu Data, 21 Mar 2024 (AMP copy, article67977090), says: "Qwik Supply Chain Pvt. Ltd. – the third biggest donor via the electoral bond route – gave ₹375 crore to the BJP and ₹25 crore to the Shiv Sena. (Three Reliance Group companies own 50% of Qwik.)" Frontline confirms the ₹410 cr total, the ₹360 cr bought in FY22, the ₹21.72 cr net profit and the Reliance denial. The claim is therefore an accurate account of what one credible outlet reported, and `reported` is the right tier. It is not `documented`. The Hindu gives the 50% figure as an unsourced aside, without naming the three companies or citing a filing. Frontline belongs to the same publishing group, so it is not an independent second source, and it says only "purportedly with links". The strongest independent support is Moneylife: one named shareholder (16.60%), traced to MCA data through a chartered accountant's post. What keeps the tier at `reported` and not higher: no MCA filing has been opened, Qwik's CIN is missing, the three holders are unnamed, the 'Reliance Group' versus RIL identity is resolved only by context, and there is no evidence the holding existed during the FY22 purchases.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim: "55 BJP-donor firms bought bonds above the old 7.5% cap in FY2022-23 and FY2023-24." The Finance Act 2017 deletion was in force from 2017 until SC struck it down on 15 Feb 2024, so the window fits and the 2022-04-01 to 2024-01-24 range holds for the 55-firm figure. It does not hold for the 33-firm figure. The Hindu measured that group on seven years of losses (2016-17 to 2022-23) against bond buying from 2019-20 to 2023-24, so it falls outside the edge's 2022-04-01 start. The "(FY23–FY24)" label covers only the first half of the claim.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The nodes are a statute (Companies Act §182(1), cap deleted by Finance Act 2017) and a party (BJP), so no name-collision risk. One attribution is wrong: the analysis was done by "The Hindu and an independent research team" (byline Prasenjit Bose with The Hindu Data Team) using CMIE's Prowess IQ database. CMIE supplied data and did not co-author, so "The Hindu/CMIE" and "joint analysis with CMIE" misattribute authorship.
verdicts.baseRate: 55 of 221 matched firms (~25%) went over the cap, which is well under 80%, so the over-cap property does pick out a subset. The BJP-share comparison fails. The universe was chosen by giving to BJP: "385 companies that had donated bonds totalling ₹5,362.2 crore to the ruling BJP". A sample chosen that way will show a BJP share above BJP's all-bond share of ~47.5% (₹6,060 cr of ~₹12,769 cr) just by how it was built. The right base rate is the BJP share of ALL bond money from the 221 matched firms (or all 385). The Hindu does not publish it. So 71% vs 47.5% is not a like-for-like base rate, and the claim text presents it as if it were. Symmetry: INC got 10% of the over-cap money, about its ~11% share overall. Among the 45 "suspect" firms, category C (positive profits, negative taxes) gave 47% to Congress and 24% to TMC but only 15% to BJP. The same lens turns up opposition-skewed subsets.
verdicts.denialFound: None found; there is no sign BJP was asked about this specific analysis, and neither Hindu article carries a response. Scroll (scroll.in/latest/1066216) and The Wire repeated The Hindu's figures without adding a response, so they are not independent confirmation. BJP's general line on bonds (Amit Shah, March 2024: BJP's bond share was proportionate to its seat strength) is not a reply to this analysis and should not be recorded as a contra.
verdicts.innocentReading: Giving above the cap was lawful from 2017 until the Feb 2024 SC judgment. A sample made up only of BJP donors will skew toward BJP by construction. BJP was the ruling party and got the largest share of all bonds (~47.5%). Large one-off gifts in the 2023-24 pre-election year will exceed 7.5% of a company's three-year average profit even for normal firms with thin or volatile profits. "Negative or near zero" aggregate profit over seven years says nothing about current cash flow or group-level money. Six of the 33 over-cap firms did not report profits for all three prior years, and The Hindu averaged only the years they did report.
verdicts.reason: The figures match the sources. 55 article: "221 of the 385 firms"; "₹1,377.9 crore... more than 69% of their aggregate donation of ₹1,993 crore"; "The BJP alone received close to 71%... (Rs. 1,414 crore)". 33 article: "Thirty-three companies donated an aggregate sum of ₹576.2 crore in EBs, out of which ₹434.2 crore (nearly 75%) was encashed by the BJP". The claim text overreaches in two ways. (1) "Implies the 2017 Finance Act change enabled disproportionate giving" is a causal claim, but the analytic tier is for non-causal comparison only. It is also circular: the deletion made over-cap giving possible by definition, and the sources do not show "disproportionate" in the party-skew sense. (2) The "base rate... 47.5%" is set against a sample chosen for giving to BJP, so 71% vs 47.5% has no meaning as it stands. The record's own innocentReading says so, but the claim text presents the comparison without that caveat. The numbers hold as reported figures; the conclusion drawn from them does not.

Replace with a non-causal statement: "Over-cap giving was lawful between the Finance Act 2017 deletion and the SC's 15 Feb 2024 judgment." (b) Delete "base rate for all matched bond money to BJP is 47.5%" or label it "not comparable: sample chosen on BJP donors". Keep upgradeIf (run on the full purchaser file). (c) Change "(The Hindu/CMIE)" to "(The Hindu Data Team and Prasenjit Bose's research team, using CMIE Prowess IQ data)". Make the same fix to the sec182 node source label ("joint analysis with CMIE Prowess"). (d) Change "33 loss-making firms" to "33 firms with negative or near-zero aggregate profit after tax, 2016-17 to 2022-23". Scope their ₹576.2 cr / ₹434.2 cr to bond buying from 2019-20 to 2023-24, not FY23-FY24. Either widen the edge's 'from' date or split the 33-firm figure into its own edge. Record that the headline says ₹582 cr and the body says ₹576.2 cr, and use the body figure. (e) The figures themselves can be tagged 'reported' (one credible outlet, named analyst, named data source). The edge stays 'analytic' only after (a) and (b) are fixed. Scroll and The Wire repeat The Hindu and do not count as a second independent outlet.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is "Congress (Jairam Ramesh on 14 Mar 2024; Kharge on X on 15 Mar 2024) alleged that 45 companies paid the BJP about ₹400 cr after central-agency action." Frontline/ADR confirms both dates: "The Congress on March 14 alleged…" and the Kharge post is dated "March 15, 2024". The record's from/to of 2024-03-14 to 2024-03-15 is correct. The text credits the 15 Mar date to both men, which is a small slip: the 45/₹400 cr statement was the party's on 14 Mar, and Kharge's post came on 15 Mar. The underlying donations cover FY2018-19 to FY2022-23 and come from ECI contribution reports compiled by Newslaundry/TNM/Scroll (30 firms, ₹335 cr, 21 Feb 2024; 11 more firms plus 4 SEBI-listed shell firms, 12 Mar 2024). The SBI bond data only came out on 14 Mar, so the 45-company figure cannot have been based on bond purchases.
verdicts.identityTest: The actors check out. Mallikarjun Kharge was Congress president and Jairam Ramesh was general secretary (communications) in March 2024, and the node energy:inc is INC. Both sources name the firms in c066 at legal-entity level: Hetero Drugs, Hetero Labs and Hetero Biopharma; MSN Pharmachem and MSN Laboratories; Divi's Laboratories; Aurobindo Pharma; Micro Labs. But nothing links those firms to Congress's list of 45. The Hindu describes them as "under the scanner of the Income Tax Department, the Enforcement Directorate or the U.S. Food and Drug Administration". It does not call them all 'raided', and it does not say they are the same firms as the 45. The '45' also contains 4 SEBI-listed shell firms that did not face central-agency action: Newslaundry, 12 Mar 2024, 'In 15 more donors of BJP, 4 shell firms, 11 companies that faced central action'.
verdicts.baseRate: The allegation is based on declared donations to the BJP (ECI contribution reports and electoral-trust transfers). The BJP gets roughly 70-80%+ of declared corporate and trust money: The Wire says the BJP received over 80% of electoral-trust donations. So a firm that faced agency action and donated to the BJP is close to the default case for any large Indian corporate donor. The Hindu's own finding that "many top donors were under ED and Income Tax Department scanner" points the same way. The edge only becomes informative with a control group of un-raided donors and a raid-versus-donation chronology for each firm. Newslaundry gives a partial chronology (23 of 30 had never donated before the raid; 4 donated within four months of it), but it has no control group. The symmetry test cuts against the inference. The same scrutinised firms gave heavily to state ruling parties: Hetero ₹50 cr to BRS vs ₹10 cr to BJP; MSN ₹20 cr BRS vs ₹16 cr BJP; Micro Labs ₹7 cr SKM, ₹6 cr BJP, ₹3 cr INC; Aurobindo ₹2.5 cr to TDP; Divi's ₹5 cr to INC. Future Gaming, under ED action, gave mostly to TMC and DMK. The killIf baseline of ~47.5% is BJP's share of bonds, which is the wrong reference class for contribution-report data.
verdicts.denialFound: Nirmala Sitharaman, 15 Mar 2024, quoted in Frontline and reprinted by ADR (https://adrindia.org/content/eci-reveals-electoral-bonds-data-bjp-tops-beneficiary-list-biggest-donor-little-known-future): "I think you've based yourself on huge assumptions, that the money was given after the Enforcement Directorate raid happened." She also called the bond system "one bit better" than what came before. The record already carries this as c065. I found no firm-level denials. Newslaundry says it emailed each of the 11 companies ("Their comments will be added to this report if they respond"). I saw no sign that the BJP itself was asked about the firm-level data.
verdicts.innocentReading: Large pharma, infrastructure and real-estate groups both donate to politics and draw regulatory and tax scrutiny, because they are large, cash-rich and operate in heavily regulated sectors. The BJP, as the national ruling party, takes most declared corporate money whether or not a donor has been raided. The same firms gave to BRS, TDP, SKM and INC in states where those parties governed. This fits a hedge-with-whoever-rules pattern at least as well as it fits agency-driven extortion by the BJP.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives as an alleged-tier edge. The primary text is on file: Kharge's post, quoted verbatim in the Frontline/ADR source, says "…making it a total of 45 companies paying BJP nearly Rs 400 crore". It is attributed to named parties and carries two contras (c065 and c066), which is exactly what the alleged tier requires. The Hindu source confirms every amount in c066 word for word. The edge text still misstates what the allegation measured. It says the firms "bought ~₹400 cr of bonds". The 45/₹400 cr figure came from the Newslaundry/TNM/Scroll analysis of ECI contribution reports (₹335 cr + ₹62.27 cr + ₹4.94 cr ≈ ₹402 cr), published before the bond data was released. Kharge's post says "paying BJP", not bonds. Only Frontline's paraphrase says "through electoral bonds". Also, 4 of the 45 were shell firms, not raided companies. The edge must be corrected before publication. The allegation itself holds.

Keep pred 'enforce' only if the schema has no alternative, and flag the non-standard direction. 6) Fix killIf/upgradeIf: the ~47.5% bond-share baseline is the wrong comparison. The source gives no rupee figures for the other five, so the size of the difference is qualitative only. Symmetry check: the same approach would also flag the Rae Bareli SDI (Congress-held seat), but by ThePrint's account it received much less, so the concentration is specific to Bhubaneswar. verdicts.denialFound: ONGC did respond on the SDI specifically, in the same article (ThePrint, Remya Nair, 18 Jun 2021, https://theprint.in/economy/rs-1355-cr-how-much-oil-psus-have-given-temple-towns-pm-cares-statue-of-unity-as-csr/677548/): "In its response, ONGC said IOCL is setting up SDI Bhubaneswar. verdicts.innocentReading: This is ONGC's on-record explanation, not just ours. Bhubaneswar is the only oil-PSU SDI that has bought land and is building its own campus. The other SDIs (Kochi, Rae Bareli, Visakhapatnam, Ahmedabad, Guwahati) run from rented premises and so only need operating funds. The PSUs split costs by fixed shares (ONGC 15% of both operating and capital costs), with IOCL as the implementing agency. Vocational training is an explicit Schedule VII head. verdicts.reason: The amounts and the tenure overlap are confirmed word for word by ThePrint: IOC ₹149 cr + ₹77 cr, GAIL ₹18 cr + ₹10.5 cr, BPCL ₹18.5 cr + ₹11.5 cr, HPCL ₹24 cr + ₹5.5 cr, ONGC ₹20 cr, "more than Rs 330 crore till 2019-20". The claim also says other SDIs' funding "was not compared", but the same article compares them: they got "much lower" amounts, "mainly for operational expenses". Under the tiering rules, a misstated denial is a material error. The claim hides a first-class contra and understates both the discriminating base rate and the innocent explanation. The underlying correlation holds, so the edge should stay as analytic with the corrections below rather than be killed.
