verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: "SHANTI Act (assent 2025-12-20) removes statutory supplier recourse, which governs and benefits EDF". The EDF fact is dated July 2016 (WNA), when EDF submitted its fresh 6xEPR proposal. The claim's windows don't line up. The edge carries from=2025-12-20, which is the assent date, but the file's own entity record says that as of 2026-08-05 the Act had not been notified into force (PIB: reforms "will come into effect once the SHANTI Act is notified"). The s.17(b) removal is therefore not yet operative against any supplier. EDF also has no contract with NPCIL for the provision to govern: it made a binding offer in 2021-04, there was no framework agreement as of 2025-03, the environmental clearance lapsed in 2022-12, and nothing has been signed nine months after assent. So on current evidence the edge describes a benefit that is both prospective and hypothetical, and from=2025-12-20 is wrong for an operative 'law' edge.
verdicts.identityTest: The EDF node is Électricité de France, the Jaitapur EPR proponent. WNA names "EdF", so the identity is consistent. There is no name-collision risk. Note that EDF took over the Jaitapur role from Areva in 2016, so any supplier-liability complaints before 2016 were Areva's, not EDF's. The claim's "since 2016" is correct on that point. Neither the Forbes nor the PRS source names EDF at all.
verdicts.baseRate: The provision applies to every supplier of every Indian nuclear operator: domestic ones (L&T, BHEL, MTAR, Godrej, Walchandnagar) and foreign ones (EDF, Westinghouse, Rosatom, Holtec, KHNP). That is 100% of the reference class, so the property does not single out EDF. The file itself makes the identical edge for Westinghouse (c008). The narrative block in the file also notes that the Indian private operators (Tata Power, Adani, Hindalco) and domestic suppliers carried the same recourse exposure. The symmetry test fails in the same way: the 2010 CLND Act was itself attacked as "written for GE/Westinghouse", so the lens produces the same alarming reading for the UPA-era law.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and there is no sign EDF was ever asked. The web search budget was exhausted in this session, so I could not run a fresh search for an EDF or DAE statement. The only response on record in the file is from 2010: the government denied US pressure over the CLND Act. That does not answer this claim.
verdicts.innocentReading: India replaced CLND s.17(b) with the recourse model used in the international conventions: operator liability channelled to the operator, supplier recourse only by contract or for deliberate acts. The CSC and Vienna conventions use this model, and India ratified the CSC in 2016. The change applies to every domestic and foreign supplier. Its stated purpose (Budget 2025) is to bring in private and Indian capital. Foreign-incorporated companies are barred from holding licences. EDF's 2016 request is one of many vendor and industry requests for the convention-standard regime, not evidence that the provision was written for EDF.
verdicts.reason: The claim joins two individually documented facts into a conclusion neither source states. The facts: (a) PRS says "The Bill removes the right to recourse on the ground of supply of defective equipment or materials", and Forbes India says "Operators may seek recourse against suppliers only if such a right is explicitly provided for in a contract or if the damage resulted from a deliberate act." (b) WNA says that in July 2016 "EdF submitted a fresh proposal ... seeking guarantee of 'the same level of protection' in relation to liability that is available at the international level." The conclusion, that SHANTI benefits EDF specifically, appears in no source. PRS and Forbes do not mention EDF, and WNA does not link SHANTI to EDF. The provision covers 100% of suppliers, the Act is not yet in force, and EDF has no contract for it to govern. So the EDF-specific edge with "Benefit named: EDF" is our own inference and cannot be tiered 'documented'. The provision itself is documented by a primary summary (PRS) plus an independent outlet (Forbes). But it belongs on an edge to the supplier class, not to EDF. The edge text also concedes the beneficiary framing is contested, which is inconsistent with a 'documented' tier.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change the tier from documented to analytic for the SHANTI to EDF edge. Add an innocentReading (convention-standard channelling that applies to all suppliers; foreign companies barred from licences). Set benefit.confidence to "speculative/inferred" and keep amountCr null. 2) If the edge should stay 'documented', retarget t from energy:edf to a supplier-class node (e.g. an industry node "nuclear equipment suppliers (domestic and foreign)"), with EDF and Westinghouse as analytic sub-edges. c008 (Westinghouse) has the same defect. 3) Change from=2025-12-20 (assent date) to null or pending notification. Add a note: "not in force as of 2026-08-05 (PIB PRID 2294814)". 4) Fix the misquotation. The d field puts "liability protection matching international standards" in quotation marks, but WNA's actual wording is "seeking guarantee of 'the same level of protection' in relation to liability that is available at the international level" (July 2016). 5) Add a killIf: "EDF/NPCIL Jaitapur contract signed with a contractual recourse waiver that would have been impossible under CLND s.17(b)". That event would instead support an upgrade to reported. Add an upgradeIf: "EDF or French government statement crediting SHANTI for Jaitapur progress". 6) Record the denial status as "none found, not asked".

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: the SHANTI Act (assent 2025-12-20) removed the operator's statutory recourse against suppliers, and that benefits Westinghouse. The dates fit. GEH's refusal (Sept 2015) and the move of Kovvada to AP1000 (mid-2016) both come before the Act. The Construction World article is datePublished 2024-12-06. It reports a written Lok Sabha reply by Jitendra Singh but gives no date for the reply, so '2024-12-06' is really the article date and the reply was on or before it. The benefit is still only prospective. As of 2026-08-05 the Act had not been notified into force (PIB, cited on the SHANTI node), and Westinghouse still had no techno-commercial offer, so no contract exists yet that could benefit. The 'from' date of 2025-12-20 is the assent date, not the date the change took legal effect.
verdicts.identityTest: Westinghouse Electric Company is identified correctly as the Kovvada 6xAP1000 proponent (WNA says the site was 'subsequently designated for six Westinghouse AP1000 units', and Construction World confirms). There is no name-collision risk. However, neither source ties Westinghouse to the Act. Forbes India and PRS name no company at all. PRS: 'The document does not name any specific companies or foreign vendors.'
verdicts.baseRate: The provision applies to every supplier of nuclear equipment and materials, foreign and domestic: Westinghouse, EDF/Framatome, GE Hitachi, and Indian suppliers such as L&T, BHEL, Godrej and Walchandnagar. Essentially 100% of comparable suppliers benefit, so the property does not single out Westinghouse. This edge is the same as c007 (EDF) with the target node swapped.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Westinghouse was not asked in any source. Its newsroom (info.westinghousenuclear.com/news) has no release on India, SHANTI, Kovvada or liability. The WNN article on the Act says nothing on supplier recourse or vendor reaction. The web-search budget was used up, so a wider search for a response could not be run. The platform has no record that it asked Westinghouse for comment.
verdicts.innocentReading: Channelling nuclear liability solely to the operator is the international norm, under the Paris/Vienna conventions and the CSC Annex. India ratified the CSC in 2016, and CLND s.17(b) was an outlier that deterred every vendor, including Indian ones. Removing it is an industry-wide rule change aimed at bringing in any private or foreign capital. It is not tailored to Westinghouse, which still had no offer on the table. Operators can also still write supplier recourse into contracts, so NPCIL could restore it for Kovvada by contract.
verdicts.reason: The claim joins facts that are each documented into a conclusion none of the sources states. The facts are: recourse was removed (Forbes India: 'Operators may seek recourse against suppliers only if such a right is explicitly provided for in a contract or if the damage resulted from a deliberate act'; PRS: 'The Bill removes the right to recourse on the ground of supply of defective equipment or materials'); GEH declined in 2015-09 (WNA: 'would not proceed with any investment in India until the country's liability regime was brought into line'); and Westinghouse had no offer (Construction World: 'WEC is yet to submit a Techno-Commercial Offer (TCO)'). The two cited sources never mention Westinghouse together with the Act. Forbes India does not mention Westinghouse, GE Hitachi or Kovvada at all, and Construction World says nothing about liability. The claim's wording 'beneficiary named as Westinghouse' is therefore wrong: no source names Westinghouse as a beneficiary. That identification is our own inference. It also fails to discriminate, because 100% of suppliers benefit and the same lens gives the identical EDF edge (c007). It has no innocentReading and no contra. Under SPEC, the Westinghouse-specific benefit can be tiered at most analytic, not documented.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change tier from 'documented' to 'analytic' and add an innocentReading (CSC-aligned, industry-wide channelling of liability to the operator; recourse still available by contract). 2) Remove 'beneficiary named as' from the text. Reword to say the Act removes statutory supplier recourse for all suppliers, and that Westinghouse is one of the vendors affected. 3) Set benefit.confidence to 'low' and state that the benefit is contingent: the Act was not notified as of 2026-08-05 and no Kovvada offer or contract exists. 4) Change the date wording from 'as of 2024-12-06' to 'per Lok Sabha written reply reported 2024-12-06 (reply date not stated)'. 5) The 'd' field cites WNA for the GEH 2015-09 fact, but the claim's short srcs list lacks WNA; keep WNA in srcs because only WNA supports the GEH sentence. 6) Record the denial as 'none found — not asked'. 7) Consider merging c007 and c008 into a single law→supplier-class edge (or law→industry node), because a separate edge per vendor overstates how targeted the provision is.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Manish Tewari (Congress MP for Chandigarh, 2024-06 onward) spoke in the Lok Sabha debate on the SHANTI Bill on 2025-12-17. His term covers that date. The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 2025-12-15 and passed there on 2025-12-17, so the date is right. Deccan Herald is timestamped 17 Dec 2025, 14:39 IST. The Wire's photo caption dates the debate to 17 Dec 2025. The premise of the timing insinuation fails a date test, though. The file's own documented record (Sitharaman node) has the 2025-02-01 Budget speech saying "amendments to the Atomic Energy Act and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act will be taken up". That is about nine months before any announcement "a month" before December 2025.
verdicts.identityTest: Both sources name the speaker as "Manish Tewari", "the Chandigarh MP", Congress, first opposition speaker. There is one slip: The Wire's subhead and caption say "Congress MP Manoj Tewari", but its body text says "Congress MP Manish Tewari opened for the opposition". Manoj Tiwari is a BJP MP, so this is a sub-editing error, not an identity conflict. The t-node, energy:shanti-act-2025, is correct. The "private conglomerate" is unnamed in every source, and the claim rightly leaves it unnamed and unlinked to any company node.
verdicts.baseRate: The insinuation does not single out anyone. The file itself documents that six private groups (Hindalco, JSPL, Tata Power, Reliance Industries, JSW Energy, Adani Power) had submitted documents for NPCIL's Bharat Small Reactor call by 2025-09-29. Private "plans to enter the sector" were announced across the industry, so a Bill following "a conglomerate's announcement" would be true whenever the Bill arrived. Opposition "is it a coincidence?" remarks during debates on opening a sector to private players are also routine. The recorded fact is that he said it, not that it is true.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. Deccan Herald (https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Fshanti-bill-congress-tears-into-modi-govt-over-nuclear-liability-clause-3833987): "'Is it a coincidence?' Tewari said to which Minister of State Jitendra Singh intervened to deny the 'unfounded and politically motivated' claim." The Wire (https://m.thewire.in/article/energy/lok-sabha-passes-shanti-bill-amid-walkout-opening-nuclear-sector-to-private-players): "union minister Jitendra Singh, who introduced the bill, termed the allegation as 'unfounded and politically motivated'." The denial was given on the floor, and it is already recorded as contra c010.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Bill's timing follows a policy path announced in public well before December 2025: the Budget speech of 2025-02-01 (Nuclear Energy Mission, with AEA and CLNDA amendments "will be taken up"), then NPCIL's Bharat Small Reactor call, which six private groups answered by 2025-09-29, then Cabinet approval, then the winter-session Bill. A private group announcing entry shortly before the Bill is what you would expect once the government has signalled it will open the sector. That is a response to the policy, not evidence that the policy was written for that group. The liability cap, supplier-recourse and AERB points are ordinary policy objections, not allegations of wrongdoing.
verdicts.reason: Both cited outlets say what the claim says, nearly word for word: Tewari's "a month after a private conglomerate announced its plans to enter the sector — is it a coincidence?", the dropped supplier recourse (the 2010 consensus), the USD 410 mn cap against Bhopal's USD 470 mn, AERB autonomy concerns, the JPC demand, and Jitendra Singh's "unfounded and politically motivated" response. The claim carries a named accuser and a contra (c010), so it clears the "alleged" bar. It is not refuted. The decisive limit is on how the edge may be read. It records that an allegation was made, not that it has substance. The file's own documented Budget 2025-02-01 entry meets half of this claim's killIf condition and undercuts the timing insinuation. The claim must not be upgraded, and it should carry that context. The two outlets' wording is almost identical (probably shared PTI copy), so they are not independent corroboration. That does not matter for an "alleged" tier.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Predicate: SPEC says `enforce` goes agency→subject (investigation, proceeding, audit, order). An opposition MP's floor speech is none of those, and Tewari is not an agency. The house convention does use `enforce` for 33 alleged edges, so keep it only if that convention is intended; otherwise flag the edge for schema review. (2) Add to `d`/text: "Budget speech 2025-02-01 had already announced AEA/CLNDA amendments; six private groups (Hindalco, JSPL, Tata Power, RIL, JSW, Adani Power) had responded to NPCIL's BSR call by 2025-09-29." This is the documented innocent reading, and it partly meets the killIf. (3) Mark the USD 410 mn cap as Tewari's figure (he also demanded a Rs 10,000 crore cap). Do not state it as the Act's cap without the statute or PRS as a source. (4) Note that the two outlets appear to share wire copy and are not independent. (5) The Wire subhead's "Manoj Tewari" is a sub-editing error, and the body text confirms Manish Tewari; do not let any alias ingest create a Manoj Tiwari link. (6) The Tewari node's `d` tags this allegation "[documented]". Split it: the statement having been made is documented, but its substance is alleged.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: MEIL bought electoral bonds redeemed by BJP (₹586 cr) and other parties, 2019–2023/24. MEIL (Hyderabad EPC firm, founded 1989) existed throughout the scheme window (Apr 2019 – Feb 2024), so the dates overlap and the test passes. One small mismatch: Business Standard says purchases ran "between 2019 and 2023", but the record's `to` is 2024-01-31. The sibling record in enforce.json says "Apr 2019–Feb 2024" for purchases and "Apr 2019–Oct 2023" for BJP encashment. The window is harmless but not tied to any source.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes for MEIL. Every source names "Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd (MEIL)", Hyderabad, founded by P. Pitchi Reddy with P.V. Krishna Reddy. Despite the Reddy surname there is no name-collision risk, because the entity is a company that appears by name in the SBI/ECI purchaser list. BJP is unambiguous. The group figure of ₹1,200 cr is a different set of legal persons. Business Standard attributes ₹266 cr of it to "Western UP Power Transmission Company Ltd, SPEC Power, and Evey Trans Private Ltd", so it must not be put on the MEIL→BJP edge amount (the record correctly keeps a=586). The record gives no CIN for MEIL.
verdicts.baseRate: BJP encashed ₹6,060.51 cr, about half of all bonds redeemed (Moneylife, per the SBI/ECI data). MEIL sent about 61% (586/966) of its bonds to BJP, close to BJP's overall share. Most top-10 bond buyers gave BJP a large share (Future Gaming, which went mainly to TMC, is the main exception). So "top donor gave to BJP" does not discriminate, and on its own it is not evidence of quid pro quo. Symmetry check: the same data gives MEIL→BRS ₹195 cr (BRS ruled Telangana at the time), →DMK ₹85 cr and →Congress ₹17 cr. MEIL spread its bonds across at least 9 parties, which fits hedging across whoever is in power. The edge holds as a donation fact, not as an implication of wrongdoing.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Tribune (the CBI-booking story), Business Standard and Moneylife carry no statement from MEIL, and none of them says MEIL was asked. The WebSearch budget ran out, so I could not search further for a company response. Record this as "no MEIL response in cited sources; not shown to have been asked".
verdicts.innocentReading: Electoral bonds were a legal donation channel from 2018 until the Supreme Court struck them down in Feb 2024. A large infrastructure contractor working in many states donates to whichever parties govern those states: BJP at the Centre and in many states, BRS in Telangana, DMK in Tamil Nadu, YSRCP/TDP in Andhra Pradesh. That pattern alone explains the split, and the split roughly tracks each party's share of power.
verdicts.reason: I opened every source and they say what the claim says. Tribune: "Megha Engineering had donated the highest amount of about Rs 586 crore to the BJP", "Rs 195 crore to the BRS", "Rs 85 crore to the DMK", "Rs 37 crore to the YSRCP", "The TDP got about Rs 25 crore", "the Congress got Rs 17 crore", total "Rs 966 crore". Business Standard (fetched with curl after WebFetch got a 403): "Megha Engineering purchased electoral bonds worth Rs 966 crore between 2019 and 2023" and "along with three associated companies procured bonds worth Rs 1,200 crore". TNM: "MEIL paid Rs 584 crore in electoral bonds to the Bharatiya Janata Party". Nothing is conjoined to imply more than the sources say. The claim flags the ₹584/586 discrepancy and states that it was not reconciled against the ECI file. That makes "reported" the honest tier: the outlets are credible and rely on published ECI data, but the two figures conflict by ₹2 cr and nobody here has read the primary SBI/ECI redemption file, so it does not yet reach documented.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Fix the ₹584 vs ₹586 inconsistency across files. enforce.json (line ~2155) says ₹584 cr for the same MEIL→BJP flow. Use "₹584–586 cr" or settle it from the ECI file (upgradeIf), and pick one value for `a`. (2) Tie the date window to a source. Business Standard says purchases ran "between 2019 and 2023", but the record's `to` is 2024-01-31 and enforce.json says Feb 2024. Either cite a source for the window or set to=2023-12-31 with a note. (3) Business Standard's ₹1,200 cr is rounded; the components are 966 + 266 = ₹1,232 cr. Name the three associates (Western UP Power Transmission Co Ltd, SPEC Power, Evey Trans Pvt Ltd) and flag them as separate legal entities, not MEIL. (4) The TNM source in the record says "Megha group ... contributed Rs 1,186 crores in electoral bonds to the ruling party", which conflates the group's total purchases with BJP receipts. Cite TNM only for the ₹584 cr figure and add a note on its error. (5) Say that the Tribune piece is dated after the CBI booking and uses ECI data "released on March 21" (2024). (6) Add a note: no MEIL response in any cited source; not asked. (7) Add a base-rate note: BJP got about 50% of all bonds, and MEIL's roughly 61% share to BJP is not anomalous. Add MEIL→BRS ₹195 cr as a sibling edge for symmetry.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as written: "MEIL won NPCIL's largest-ever order (Kaiga 5&6 EPC) in April 2025, eleven months after the bond data was published, while under a CBI FIR dated March 2024." The dates in the sources: ECI put the SBI bond data online on 14 March 2024 (the Business Standard source is dated 15 Mar 2024). MEIL was declared L1 on 26 June 2024 (TNM, whose article is dated 26 Jun, not 28 Jun as the file says). WNN reports the award on 24 April 2025 ("the biggest order ever placed by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd (NPCIL)"). One trade report puts the award a day earlier, on 23 April 2025, at Rs 12,786.9 cr. From publication to award is therefore about 13 months, not eleven, and from publication to L1 is about 3 months. The "eleven months" figure is wrong in both `text` and `d`. The tender itself opened in May 2023 and technical bids opened in October 2023, so the procurement started before the bond data was published and before the FIR. Tribune gives the FIR date as 31 March 2024 (preliminary enquiry from 10 Aug 2023); ThePrint gives a complaint date of 18 Mar 2024; Moneycontrol and Infralog say "April 11". "2024-03" follows the cited source, but the exact date varies between outlets. I found nothing on whether the FIR was still open in April 2025, since no chargesheet or closure reporting turned up. So "while under" means the FIR was registered before the award and I found no report of its closure; it is not a verified current status.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. All three sources name the same company, Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd (MEIL), Hyderabad. Tribune ties the FIR and the ₹966 cr in bonds to the same MEIL, and WNN and TNM tie the Kaiga award to MEIL. There is no name-collision risk at company level. The bond figures cover MEIL alone; the three associates (Western UP Power Transmission, SPEC Power, Evey Trans) are correctly left out of the ₹966 cr.
verdicts.baseRate: The "1-of-3" figure measures the chance of winning (MEIL, L&T and BHEL bid; one won). It says nothing about whether buying bonds is discriminating. BHEL is a PSU and could not buy bonds, so there is effectively one private rival, which makes the base rate for the bond-buying property close to meaningless. Among India's top private infrastructure EPC firms, bond purchases were common but well below 80%, so the property is not non-discriminating. It also cannot be tested with n=1 contract. Symmetry: MEIL's bonds also went to BRS (₹195 cr), DMK (₹85 cr) and Congress (₹17 cr). The same lens run on an opposition state that awarded MEIL work (for example Telangana's Kaleshwaram under BRS) gives an equally striking edge. That means the pattern tracks "large EPC contractor that donates to every incumbent", not a particular party.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. Tribune, ThePrint and TNM carry no MEIL comment on the bonds or the FIR, and none says MEIL was contacted. MEIL's only statements on the record are promotional: TNM quotes the project as "a significant milestone in India's journey towards clean and reliable nuclear energy", and meil.in has a purchase-order press release. The claim says "MEIL was never asked". That can't be documented: the record only shows that no response appears in the cited reporting. It should say "no MEIL response to the bond/FIR juxtaposition found; not known to have been asked."
verdicts.innocentReading: MEIL won the tender at ₹12,799.92 cr against L&T and BHEL. By its own June 2024 statement, reported by TNM and NDTV, it was the lowest bidder. The WNN article says it was selected under NPCIL's first use of QCBS for "its strong technical approach and competitive pricing", but WNN itself does not say L1. The tender began in May 2023, and technical bids opened in October 2023, before the bond disclosure and the FIR. The FIR concerns ~₹78 lakh in alleged bribes to NMDC/NISP/MECON officials on a ₹315 cr steel-plant works contract, which has nothing to do with nuclear work. An FIR alone does not debar a firm from central PSU tenders. MEIL's bonds went to at least nine parties: BJP, BRS, DMK, YSRCP, TDP and Congress, plus JD-S, Jana Sena and JD-U at ₹5–10 cr each, according to Tribune. That pattern fits hedging across incumbents.
verdicts.reason: The individual facts check out: ₹966 cr, second-largest buyer, ₹586 cr to BJP (Tribune; TNM says ₹584 cr), the ₹12,800 cr Kaiga EPC as NPCIL's largest-ever order (WNN), and QCBS used for the first time (WNN). But the claim's own framing sentence is wrong. The award came about 13 months after the bond data was published, not eleven. The innocent reading says the bonds were "spread over six parties", but the Tribune source it cites lists nine. "MEIL was never asked" states an absence as a fact when the record only shows that no response was published. The claim is also a four-clause conjunction (bonds, then an unrelated FIR, then L1, then award) that suggests a quid pro quo none of the sources alleges. That is allowed at the analytic tier only if the sequence is dated correctly and the innocent reading is accurate. Here neither holds as written. The edge can stay at the analytic tier once the fixes below are made; as currently worded it should not be published.

verdicts.dateTest: MoPNG raised a USD 2.81 bn demand on the KG-D6 contractors (RIL, BP Exploration, Niko), with a letter received on 3 Mar 2025 and disclosed by RIL on 3–4 Mar 2025. This came after the Delhi HC Division Bench set aside the 2018 award on 14 Feb 2025. MoPNG is the PSC counterparty for the whole period and Hardeep Singh Puri has been minister since 7 Jul 2021, so the dates line up. from=2025-03-04 is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The source names 'Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry' and 'Reliance Industries' (NSE: RELIANCE). No name collision. The demand is addressed to all the contractors (RIL, BP Exploration (Alpha), Niko), not to RIL alone. Pointing the edge at RIL as operator (60%) is fine, but the text should name the co-contractors.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and not suggestive of wrongdoing by either side. A government raising a revised (principal plus interest) demand after winning a set-aside is routine follow-on enforcement. It is the expected next step for any PSC counterparty in this position, and it runs against RIL, not in its favour.
verdicts.denialFound: RIL (via Reuters/ThePrint, 4 Mar 2025): "The company has been legally advised that the division bench judgment and this provisional demand are unsustainable and is taking steps to challenge the judgment." RIL also said it does not expect any financial liability, and it appealed to the SC in May 2025. https://theprint.in/economy/indias-reliance-says-oil-ministry-raised-2-81-billion-demand-in-gas-dispute-case/2530348/
verdicts.innocentReading: The rise from USD 1.55 bn to 2.81 bn most likely comes from interest (LIBOR+2% per the 2016 notice) accruing on the same 11.24 bcm migrated-gas figure. It is a provisional re-computation after the HC ruling, not a new finding or a new penalty. The demand stays contested and is sub judice (SC appeal May 2025, conciliation reported 2026).
verdicts.reason: The main fact holds: the Google News RSS source has multiple headlines dated 4 Mar 2025 (Business Standard, The Hindu, ET, Indian Express: "Reliance says oil ministry raised $2.81 bn demand in ONGC gas dispute case"), and the Reuters text on ThePrint confirms it. But the claim says it "supersedes the 2016 USD 1.73 bn demand", and that is wrong. Reuters/ThePrint: "The Indian government in 2016 sent a notice to Reliance and its partners, asking to deposit about $1.55 billion." The same file's own MoPNG node records the 3 Nov 2016 demand as USD 1.55 bn [documented]. USD 1.73 bn is a headline figure used by ET/Mint in May 2025 for the dispute's value, not the amount of the 2016 demand. As written, the claim contains a false amount, so it fails. With the fix it stands at reported. The only source cited is an RSS headline index, and the full-text article and the RIL exchange filing were not in the record.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Text: replace "supersedes the 2016 USD 1.73 bn demand" with "revises the 3 Nov 2016 USD 1.55 bn demand (the increase is presumably interest)". (2) Add that the demand is provisional and addressed to RIL, BP Exploration and Niko, with the letter received 3 Mar 2025. (3) Add a source: ThePrint/Reuters 4 Mar 2025, https://theprint.in/economy/indias-reliance-says-oil-ministry-raised-2-81-billion-demand-in-gas-dispute-case/2530348/, and remove "headline-index sourcing" for that part. (4) Add a contra edge from co:reliance-industries quoting "provisional demand are unsustainable". (5) Can be upgraded to documented if RIL's 3–4 Mar 2025 BSE/NSE disclosure is opened, or with a second full-text outlet (The Hindu or Business Standard). verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Union of India (AG R Venkataramani, for the Centre/MoPNG) told the SC that the RIL-led consortium 'virtually committed a theft' of ONGC gas, on 20 May 2026. Venkataramani has been Attorney General since Oct 2022 and CJI Surya Kant's bench (with Bagchi and Pancholi JJ) was sitting in May 2026, so the dates overlap. But the date is one day off. Law Trend, published 2026-05-20T11:50 IST, says: "In a dramatic showdown before the Supreme Court on Tuesday...". Tuesday was 19 May 2026. Millennium Post (dateline 20 May) says the hearing "commenced" on Tuesday and continued Wednesday. 20 May is the publication date, not the hearing date.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. Law Trend names the speaker: "The allegation was made by Attorney General R Venkataramani before a three-judge bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi." The proceeding is RIL's appeal against the Delhi HC division bench order of 14 Feb 2025, which set aside the 2018 international arbitral award. The Union, acting through MoPNG as the PSC counterparty, is the respondent. Using min:ministry-of-petroleum-and-natural-gas as the source node for 'Centre' is acceptable. The target is the 'RIL-led consortium' (RIL, BP, Niko). Using co:reliance-industries as operator and appellant is acceptable, though BP and Niko were also accused. There is no risk of confusing these names with other parties.
verdicts.baseRate: Not really applicable, since this is a single named dispute. The allegation is specific to the KG-D6 blocks bordering ONGC's blocks, and nothing suggests it is levelled at every operator. For context, the Centre has pressed the same claim since the 2016 Shah committee and DGH demand ($1.55bn, later raised to about $2.81bn per the Mar 2026 reporting), so the statement repeats an old litigation position rather than adding a new enforcement fact.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. In the same hearing, Senior Advocate A M Singhvi for RIL said: "When you extract by a natural process of pressure, from the nearby sea block, some oil will always flow and migrate. That has nothing to do with voluntariness, deliberation, intent." (https://lawtrend.in/virtually-committed-a-theft-centre-accuses-reliance-led-consortium-of-stealing-ongc-gas-in-kg-basin/). He also said: "It is the single largest success story in domestic gas production... Yet, I stand accused of theft," and called the migration a pressure-differential phenomenon like 'osmosis' (Daily Pioneer, 23 May 2026). Separately, Niko told the SC that ONGC never developed its fields (Livemint, 22 May 2026), and ET EnergyWorld/ETLegalWorld reported on 21–22 May that "RIL, foreign firms refute in SC Centre's claim of 'unjust' extraction". The denial is already recorded as c034.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is adversarial courtroom rhetoric by counsel for one party to a commercial and contractual dispute. It is not a judicial finding. The 2018 international tribunal found for the consortium. The Delhi HC division bench set that award aside in Feb 2025, and RIL's appeal is pending, with the SC on 26 May 2026 allowing the parties to pursue conciliation. Gas migrating across a reservoir boundary under pressure differentials is a known physical effect. The dispute is over who is entitled to the migrated gas, not over a crime that has been proven.
verdicts.reason: The substance holds. A primary-quality news report that I opened (Law Trend, 20 May 2026) quotes the Attorney General verbatim: "You [the RIL-led consortium] virtually committed a theft of my gas and you are accountable for that." Business Standard and Daily Pioneer corroborate it, and the Google News RSS source listed in the record carries the Law Trend headline dated 20 May 2026. 'Alleged' is the right tier: a named party (the Union, through the AG) makes the assertion, it is unproven and sub judice, and a contra is attached (c034, with Singhvi's same-day rebuttal and Niko's later one). The record has two problems, but neither kills the claim. First, the date is wrong: the statement was made at the Tuesday 19 May 2026 hearing, and 20 May is only the publication date. Second, the record says the claim is "sourced only to headline indexes", but the full article is reachable and should be cited directly.
verdicts.corrections: 1. from: change "2026-05-20" to "2026-05-19". Law Trend says the hearing was "on Tuesday", which was 19 May 2026. Change the text and d fields to match: "told the SC on 19 May 2026 (reported 20 May)". 2. srcs: add https://lawtrend.in/virtually-committed-a-theft-centre-accuses-reliance-led-consortium-of-stealing-ongc-gas-in-kg-basin/ as the main source, plus https://www.business-standard.com/industry/news/sc-refuses-to-pause-kg-basin-gas-dispute-as-ril-seeks-mediation-route-126052001766_1.html and https://dailypioneer.com/news/slug-lite/hearing-in-ril-centre-gas-dispute-continues-in-sc?year=2026. Delete the phrase "Sourced only to headline indexes". 3. d: name the speaker as Attorney General R Venkataramani, and the bench as CJI Surya Kant with Bagchi and Pancholi JJ. Note that the appeal is RIL's, against the Delhi HC division bench judgment of 14 Feb 2025. 4. Keep the tier at 'alleged'. The fact that the submission was made could go to 'documented' because two independent outlets report it, but the theft allegation itself stays alleged. 5. Consider adding BP and Niko as co-accused, or noting that the target is the consortium. Consider whether 'enforce' fits an oral submission by a respondent. The enforcement act is the underlying MoPNG/DGH recovery claim (about $2.81bn, per the Mar 2026 reporting), and the edge could be tied to that. 6. killIf/upgradeIf are fine. Also add the 26 May 2026 SC order permitting conciliation (Livemint and BW Businessworld, 26 May 2026) as context.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: MEIL bought electoral bonds from 2019 to 2024, and MEIL won GAs in PNGRB CGD round 11 in January 2022. The bond window (first purchase 12 Apr 2019, last in 2024) covers the round, so the dates overlap and the date test passes. But the claim's date for the award is wrong. 14 Jan 2022 is when financial bids were opened (PNGRB: "the financial bid of 438 bids was opened on 14.01.2022"). The awards came later: PNGRB approved Letters of Intent at its 108th Board meeting on 27 Jan 2022, reported 28–29 Jan 2022. The edge's "from": "2022-01-14" gives the bid-opening date, not the award date. The record also has "to": null. ET and Moneycontrol reported on 27 May 2024 that MEIL planned to sell its city gas business. That sale is unconfirmed, but it should be on the watchlist.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes at company level. The bond buyer is Megha Engineering & Infrastructures Ltd (Hyderabad), named that way in both Indian Express and The Hindu. The CGD bidder is the same MEIL, named that way by PNGRB and in LoI coverage. The GAs were later moved to its wholly owned subsidiary Megha Gas, renamed Megha City Gas Distribution Pvt Ltd (MCGDPL), per TOI on 26 Sep 2022. That makes the "Megha Gas" alias a subsidiary, not the same legal person. The node's CIN is null. It should be filled in, and MCGDPL should be a separate node linked to MEIL by an `own` edge. Name-collision risk: the Reddy family names are not used in the edge, so this is low.
verdicts.baseRate: The reference class is the 13 entities that won LoIs in round 11. Five of them are PSUs (IOC 8, BPCL 4, GAIL 1, HPCL 1, and others), and PSUs could not realistically be bond buyers. Among private winners, few were large bond buyers: MEIL, and possibly the Torrent group, which is not verified for round 11. The biggest winner at the award stage, Adani Total Gas with 14 GAs, does not appear in the bond data. So the property "large bond buyer" does not describe the winners as a group (well under 40%). The pairing is not non-discriminating, but it is still only a juxtaposition. There is no control group and no effect size. The symmetry check cuts against the implied story: the top official winner was not a bond buyer, and MEIL also gave the most to BRS (an opposition party in 2022) and gave to Congress.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, and MEIL was not asked. Neither cited source (Indian Express, 15 Mar 2024; The Hindu Data, Mar 2024) puts the CGD awards to MEIL or reports a response from MEIL on this link. No MEIL statement answering the bonds-to-CGD pairing was found. The search budget was used up before a dedicated denial search could run, so "none found" rests on the RSS headline indexes and the cited articles.
verdicts.innocentReading: PNGRB awards CGD GAs through an open bid with published quantitative criteria (PNG and CNG connections, pipeline inch-km, tariff). 438 of 439 bids passed technical evaluation. MEIL bid for 43 of 61 GAs (Telangana Today), so winning many follows from bidding widely and aggressively. At the award stage the top winner was Adani Total Gas (14), not MEIL (12), and PSUs won the rest (IOC 8, BPCL 4, GAIL 1, HPCL 1). MEIL was already a CGD licensee from round 10. MEIL's bond money went to several parties, including the most to BRS, which was in opposition to the BJP nationally.
verdicts.reason: The central factual claim is wrong at the award stage, and the cited sources do not support it. The "top winner (15 GAs)" figure is the leaderboard from bid opening on 14 Jan 2022, across 61 GAs. The official award tells a different story. PNGRB's 108th Board meeting on 27 Jan 2022 approved LoIs for 52 GAs, and results for UP and Uttarakhand were held back under the model code of conduct. PSU Watch quotes the PNGRB statement and reports: "Adani Total has bagged the largest number of areas at 14, followed by MEIL at 12 and Indian Oil at eight." Telangana Today and ANI both give 12 GAs allotted to MEIL. So MEIL was not the top awardee; Adani Total Gas, a non-bond-buyer, was. The claim's two listed sources confirm only the bond figures. The Hindu has "₹584 crore came from MEIL" and MEIL as the biggest BRS donor. Indian Express says MEIL "has bought bonds worth Rs 1000 crore between 2019 and 2024". Neither mentions CGD. On the edge, the CGD fact rests only on a Google News RSS headline index, which the file itself calls one weak outlet. The analytic tier and its innocentReading are the right form for this edge. But as written the claim overstates the ranking on which the whole pairing depends, so it needs correcting before it enters the graph.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Replace "top winner (15 GAs) … Jan 2022" with: "MEIL led the bid-opening results on 14 Jan 2022 (15 GAs, per Livemint and TOI). At the official LoI stage (PNGRB 108th Board meeting, 27 Jan 2022; 52 of 61 GAs declared) it was awarded 12, second to Adani Total Gas (14)." Change the lab "Bond buyer #2 was CGD round-11's top winner" to something like "Bond buyer #2 was CGD round-11's #2 awardee (12 GAs)". 2. Change "from" from 2022-01-14 to 2022-01-27, the LoI approval date. Add an upgradeIf condition: whether MEIL's 3 withheld UP/Uttarakhand GAs were awarded later. 3. Add CGD sources to the claim's srcs: https://psuwatch.com/national-news/pngrb-issues-loi-meil-adani-total-indian-oil-10-others-11th-cgd-bidding-round (quotes the PNGRB statement), https://telanganatoday.com/meil-bags-12-geographical-areas-for-cgd-project and the ANI piece. Try to get the PNGRB press release or LoI list itself. Drop the Google News RSS index as the only CGD source. 4. In the innocentReading, change "BPCL 6 GAs" to "BPCL 4 GAs at LoI stage" (BPCL's "6" was a 25 Jan press claim made before LoIs), and add "Adani Total Gas (not a bond buyer) was the largest awardee with 14" and "MEIL bid for 43 of 61 GAs". 5. Fix the same 15-GA and "most" wording in the meil node sub/d, the energy:cgd-bidding-rounds node d, and the PNGRB node d (line ~823). 6. Record the May 2024 reports of a planned sale of the city gas business (ET, Moneycontrol) as a watch item that could set a "to" date. Add MCGDPL (Megha City Gas Distribution Pvt Ltd) as the subsidiary node that holds the authorisations. 7. Note "₹1,000 cr" as approximate: IE says Rs 1,000 cr, SBI data gives ₹966 cr for MEIL alone, and The New Indian Express gives ₹586 cr to BJP against The Hindu's ₹584 cr.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd bought electoral bonds encashed by BJP between 2021-01-01 and 2024-01-31. Itemised reporting gives the actual purchase dates as 5 Jan 2022 (₹200 cr to BJP, ₹25 cr to Shiv Sena), 10 Jan 2022 (₹10 cr to NCP), 11 to 14 Nov 2022 (₹125 cr to BJP) and 17 to 20 Nov 2023 (₹50 cr to BJP). The first purchase was in January 2022, not 2021. PTI's "2021-22" means the financial year, not calendar 2021. The window overlaps the donations, but the edge's from/to are wider than the evidence. They should be 2022-01-05 to 2023-11-20.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The source names Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd, registered at Dhirubhai Ambani Knowledge City, Navi Mumbai, and the node is the same company. The node's identity.cin is null. The CIN should be filled from MCA so the node is anchored to a registration number and not just a name. BJP is the recipient party, so no name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating on its own. BJP received about half of all encashed bond value, and most top-10 buyers (Megha, Vedanta, Keventer, Bharti, AB group) gave mostly to BJP. Qwik giving roughly 91% to BJP is above the pool average but in line with the large corporate donors. The unusual features are the donor's opacity and its Reliance linkage, not the share it gave to BJP.
verdicts.denialFound: Reliance was asked, by PTI, and issued a narrow denial: "Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd is not a subsidiary of any Reliance entity." It did not comment on the donations or on its association with the firm (ThePrint/PTI: https://theprint.in/economy/reliance-linked-qwik-supply-gave-rs-385-cr-to-bjp-rs-25-cr-to-shiv-sena/2010339/ ; Scroll: https://scroll.in/article/1065601/reliance-linked-firm-gave-rs-375-crore-to-the-bjp-through-electoral-bonds). No reported statement from Qwik or BJP disputes the amounts.
verdicts.innocentReading: The ₹385 cr figure looks like a PTI arithmetic or matching error (probably the ₹10 cr NCP bond counted as BJP) that Mint, ThePrint, Business Standard and Outlook then copied from the wire. On substance, a company's large bond purchases going mostly to the governing party matches the pattern of most large corporate donors in the scheme, and on its face it was a lawful donation under the scheme as it then stood.
verdicts.reason: The amount is wrong or contested, and the claim rests only on a Google News RSS headline index that shows headlines, not article text. The Mint headline does exist (RSS item, 22 Mar 2024: "Electoral bonds data: Reliance-linked Qwik Supply donated ₹385 crore to BJP"). But that figure is PTI wire copy. Two independent outlets that broke the matched ECI data down (released 21 Mar 2024) date by date both give ₹375 cr to BJP: The Quint (₹200 cr on 5 Jan 2022 + ₹125 cr on 11 Nov 2022 + ₹50 cr in Nov 2023) and Scroll (the same breakdown). The News Minute and Newslaundry headlines also say ₹375 cr. The remainder was ₹25 cr to Shiv Sena and ₹10 cr to NCP, which adds up to ₹410 cr. PTI's version (385 + 25 = 410) leaves out the NCP bond altogether. Under SPEC, a headline-only index is not "one credible outlet with named sourcing", so the edge fails the reported bar as written, and the itemised reporting contradicts its amount. The underlying edge (Qwik to BJP by electoral bond, roughly ₹375 cr) holds up on two independent outlets.
verdicts.corrections: a: 385 -> 375. lab: "₹375 cr to BJP". text/d: replace the Mint headline with "₹375 cr of Qwik's ₹410 cr went to BJP (₹200 cr 5 Jan 2022, ₹125 cr Nov 2022, ₹50 cr Nov 2023); remaining ₹25 cr Shiv Sena, ₹10 cr NCP, per ECI data released 21 Mar 2024 as itemised by The Quint and Scroll. PTI/Mint reported ₹385 cr, which omits the NCP bond." from: 2021-01-01 -> 2022-01-05. to: 2024-01-31 -> 2023-11-20. srcs: add https://www.thequint.com/news/politics/its-confirmed-reliance-linked-firm-donated-crores-to-bjp-via-electoral-bonds and https://scroll.in/article/1065601/reliance-linked-firm-gave-rs-375-crore-to-the-bjp-through-electoral-bonds. Keep the RSS index only as a pointer, not as the evidence. Add contra: the Reliance "not a subsidiary" statement (PTI, via ThePrint). Add sibling edges: qwik->shiv sena ₹25 cr and qwik->ncp ₹10 cr. Node qwik: fill in the CIN; in the d[] headline text change 385 to 375. Tier: reported now. Upgrade to documented once the ECI bond-number PDF rows are opened and cited, which also resolves the 375/385 conflict.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, written out: "Reliance-named companies held 50.04% of Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd when Qwik bought ₹410 cr of electoral bonds." Reuters (15 Mar 2024) bases the shareholding on "The company's latest financial statement for the year to March 2023". It says the purchases were made "in 2022 and 2023". Reporters' Collective gives ₹360 cr in FY2021-22 and ₹50 cr in FY2023-24. Director Tapas Mitra has been on the board since 17 Nov 2014. The ownership and board-link windows overlap the purchase window, so the date test passes. The edge has from/to = null. It should carry the date of the observed shareholding (FY ending 31 Mar 2023). It should not suggest the ownership held for the whole period.
verdicts.identityTest: Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd is an unusual name, so the chance of mixing it up with another company is low. The node's CIN is still null and needs filling from MCA. There is a risk on the other end. "Reliance" is also the name of Anil Ambani's ADA group. Three facts tie this to Mukesh Ambani's RIL: the company secretary uses an RIL email in the filings (Reuters); director Tapas Mitra is "Head of Accounts (Consolidation) at Reliance Industries Limited"; and Parimal Nathwani, a director of a shareholder company, is RIL's Director of Corporate Affairs (Reporters' Collective). So grp:reliance is the right group. But the shareholders are three separate companies: Reliance Group Support Services, Reliance Fire Brigade Services and Reliance Hospital Management Services. Their own link to the RIL promoter group has not been established, and RIL says they are not part of a subsidiary chain.
verdicts.baseRate: Most of the top electoral-bond buyers bought in their own corporate name (Future Gaming, Megha Engineering, Vedanta, Bharti Airtel). A top-3 buyer that is half-owned by non-subsidiary companies carrying a conglomerate's name, where the conglomerate denies a subsidiary link, is rare, well under 10% of the top 20 buyers. So the property is discriminating. The claim is also a direct ownership fact, not a correlation. Checked the other way round: the same method (reading the RoC shareholder list) applied to other top buyers does not produce a hidden group parent, apart from the second Reliance-linked buyer that Reporters' Collective also reported.
verdicts.denialFound: Reliance was asked and answered. Its denial: "Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd is not a subsidiary of any Reliance entity" (RIL spokesperson, 14–15 Mar 2024). Reuters, syndicated on ThePrint (https://theprint.in/india/qwik-a-top-buyer-of-indian-electoral-bonds-is-affiliated-to-ambanis-reliance-filings-show/2002426/), also reported that Reliance "did not respond after Reuters shared the regulatory papers and shareholding details linking it to Reliance." Business Standard ran "RIL denies links with Qwik Supply" (https://www.business-standard.com/elections/lok-sabha-election/ril-denies-links-with-qwik-supply-the-third-largest-electoral-bond-buyer-124031500390_1.html). The denial only covers subsidiary status. It does not address the 50.04% shareholding or the board links.
verdicts.innocentReading: Qwik may be one of the many service and holding companies around RIL that people linked to Reliance own through non-subsidiary vehicles. The group's accounts and consolidation staff may run it as an administrative matter. On that reading, its bond purchases would be its own board's decision and would not be RIL money, and "not a subsidiary" would be literally true under the Companies Act definition. None of this contradicts the claim of affiliation. It does contradict any reading that RIL's balance sheet funded the bonds. Separately, a ₹360 cr purchase against a ₹21.72 cr net profit in FY22 (Reporters' Collective) is not explained by this reading.
verdicts.reason: The substance holds, but the claim as filed rests on a weak and partly misdescribed source chain. The only real source listed is Wikipedia. Wikipedia's article (the "Electoral bond" URL redirects to "Electoral bonds") says Qwik "was accused of being a subsidiary of Reliance Industries, a charge Reliance denied. However, the company's registration details indicated a connection." It cites Reuters and NDTV, not the Indian Express, and it does not give the ₹410 cr figure. The underlying Reuters story, with named bylines and read via ThePrint's syndication because reuters.com and ndtv.com returned 401/403, says: "at least three companies - Reliance Group Support, Reliance Fire Brigade and Reliance Hospital Management - together own 50.04% of its stake", and that Qwik "bought bonds worth 4.1 billion rupees ($50 million)". Reporters' Collective independently read the same MCA filings. That is one credible outlet with published documents plus a second independent investigation, which clears "reported" and nearly clears "documented". "Alleged" is the wrong tier here: no named party is making an accusation; journalists read primary filings. So the edge is under-tiered and mis-sourced, not refuted. It stays short of documented because no one has opened the RoC filings themselves, and because the "own" edge from the RIL promoter group to Qwik runs through three intermediate Reliance-named companies whose link to the RIL promoter group has not been established.
verdicts.corrections:
1. tier: change "alleged" to "reported". Upgrade to documented once the Qwik FY23 MCA financial statement or shareholder list is opened, or cite Reuters and Reporters' Collective together as two independent outlets.
2. srcs: replace Wikipedia and the Google News RSS feed with (a) Reuters, 15 Mar 2024, Kaushik/Kalra/Pandya, https://www.reuters.com/world/india/qwik-top-buyer-indian-electoral-bonds-is-affiliated-ambanis-reliance-filings-2024-03-15/ (readable copy: https://theprint.in/india/qwik-a-top-buyer-of-indian-electoral-bonds-is-affiliated-to-ambanis-reliance-filings-show/2002426/), and (b) Reporters' Collective, https://www.reporters-collective.in/trc/company-with-reliance-links-third-largest-donor.
3. text: remove "Indian Express as summarised by Wikipedia". Wikipedia cites Reuters and NDTV, and the Indian Express 16 Mar item is known only from a headline. Also remove "RoC filings not opened" as the stated basis and say the reporting is based on filings.
4. lab/d: state the actual finding: "Reliance Group Support Services, Reliance Fire Brigade Services and Reliance Hospital Management Services together hold 50.04% (FY ending Mar-2023 financial statement); the company secretary has an RIL email address; director Tapas Mitra is RIL's head of accounts (consolidation)."
5. Consider pointing the edge at the three shareholder companies, with a separate affiliation edge to grp:reliance, because RIL control is not shown.
6. from/to: set from = the FY2023 statement date (2023-03-31), marked as the date the shareholding was observed.
7. Fill the Qwik node's identity.cin from MCA.
8. c053: add Reuters' note that Reliance "did not respond after Reuters shared the regulatory papers", and add Business Standard as a second source for the denial.
9. Amount: ₹410 cr is right (4.1 bn rupees per Reuters), but it comes from Reuters and Reporters' Collective, not from the cited Wikipedia article.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: EDNY grand jury (DOJ) indicted Gautam S. Adani on 20 Nov 2024; he was dismissed on 10 Aug 2026. I checked this against the primary docket on CourtListener (US v. Adani, 1:24-cr-00433-NGG). ECF 1 shows the indictment was returned under seal on 24 Oct 2024. The docket entry for 20 Nov 2024 reads "INDICTMENT UNSEALED". So 20 Nov 2024 is the date the indictment was unsealed, not the date it was returned. ECF 23 is the DOJ's consent Rule 48(a) motion to dismiss, filed 18 May 2026. ECF 49 is the Memorandum & Order of 10 Aug 2026: "Counts Two, Three, and Four of the Indictment as alleged against Appearing Defendants Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani, and Vneet Jaain are DISMISSED WITH PREJUDICE." The alleged conduct overlaps Gautam Adani's chairmanship of the group. The indictment says he "personally met with Foreign Official #1 in Andhra Pradesh … on or about August 7, 2021, … September 12, 2021 and … November 20, 2021". The edge's from/to window of 2024-11-20 to 2026-08-10 is right for him. Counts One and Five against the other five defendants are still open: ECF 57 of 3 Sep 2026 denied dismissal of those counts without prejudice.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. The docket and indictment name "Gautam S. Adani (1)", "Sagar R. Adani (2)" and "Vneet S. Jaain (3)". "Indian Energy Company" is Adani Green Energy, and "U.S. Issuer" is Azure Power. The node gadani (PAN-identified in the SEBI order) is the same person. There is a name-collision risk: the Wikipedia source spells him "Vineet Jain", which is the name of an unrelated Times Group MD. The claim's spelling "Vneet Jaain" matches the indictment and should be kept. The 'doj' node is the right agency: the case was brought by EDNY together with DOJ's Fraud Section.
verdicts.baseRate: Mostly not applicable, because this is a single named criminal proceeding. There is no reference class in which ≥80% of comparable entities share the property. The symmetry check is satisfied inside the source itself. The same indictment charges the rival bidder's side too: Azure Power / CDPQ executives Gupta, Cabanes, S. Agarwal, Malhotra and R. Agarwal face the FCPA conspiracy and obstruction counts. The alleged bribe recipients include Andhra Pradesh officials, and the indictment's "Foreign Official #1" dates to the YSRCP government, which was not BJP. Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and J&K discoms are also named, so the edge does not single out one political side.
verdicts.denialFound: Found and verified word for word on the Adani Group media statement of 21 Nov 2024 (https://www.adani.com/newsroom/media-releases/media-statement-1): "The allegations made by the US Department of Justice and the US Securities and Exchange Commission against directors of Adani Green are baseless and denied … All possible legal recourse will be sought." This is already recorded as c004. After the dismissal, Adani said he accepted the decision with "humility and deep respect". That quote is sourced to Livemint on 11 Aug 2026, cited on Wikipedia; I did not open it directly.
verdicts.innocentReading: An indictment records a prosecutor's accusation, not a finding. DOJ itself asked for dismissal with prejudice, citing evidentiary and jurisdictional problems, the mostly foreign conduct, and no identified losses to US investors. The court dismissed every count against Gautam Adani with prejudice. The judge's accepted basis was that the anti-bribery statements were "non-actionable puffery" (per FCPA Professor, 11 Aug 2026). Adani was never charged with bribery. The FCPA count ran only against the Azure/CDPQ defendants. So the bribery narrative stays an allegation that was never tried and was never charged against him as a bribery offence.
verdicts.reason:
The edge itself holds up. The primary docket (CourtListener 1:24-cr-00433, ECF 1, 23 and 49) confirms that DOJ/EDNY indicted Gautam Adani, that the indictment was unsealed 20 Nov 2024, and that his counts were dismissed with prejudice on 10 Aug 2026. A named party makes the allegation and a verified contra (c004) exists, so the edge meets the SPEC bar for "alleged". But the claim text misstates the indictment in ways that would be defamatory-adjacent if published as written:

(a) "allegedly paid ~US$250m". The indictment (¶49) says the co-conspirators "had offered and promised to Indian government officials approximately 2,029 crore rupees (approximately $265 million) in bribes". That is offered and promised, not paid. The indictment's own figure is ₹2,029 cr, not our ₹2,100 cr conversion.

(b) Grouping "Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani, Vneet Jaain + 5" as bribe payers implies all eight were charged with bribery. In fact Adani, Sagar and Jaain were charged only with Counts 2–4 (securities fraud conspiracy, wire fraud conspiracy, securities fraud on the 2021 144A bond). Count 1 (FCPA conspiracy) and Count 5 (obstruction) were against the other five. The Wikipedia infobox line "5 counts against all defendants" is wrong on this point.

(c) ">US$3bn from US investors" overstates ¶39. The indictment says ">$2 billion" in "bank loans from international financial institutions and United States-based asset management companies", plus ">$1 billion in securities … marketed and sold to investors in the United States, among other places".

(d) The supersession note ("single tertiary source; docket not opened") is out of date. The docket is open and shows ALL counts against Gautam Adani were dismissed with prejudice, not just "securities/wire-fraud counts".

Source check is only partial. The Forbes page returned 403. Wikipedia is tertiary and partly wrong. The SECI manufacturing-linked tender appears in the indictment (¶¶43–49) but in none of the cited sources.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Add primary sources:
   - The indictment, https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nyed.522758/gov.uscourts.nyed.522758.1.0_1.pdf
   - The docket, https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/69394936/united-states-v-adani/
   Demote Wikipedia to context only. Drop or replace Forbes, which returned 403.
2. Change the lab/text to "Indictment returned under seal 24 Oct 2024, unsealed 20 Nov 2024". Keep from=2024-11-20 as the public date, or use 2024-10-24 with a note.
3. Replace "allegedly paid ~US$250m (~₹2,100 cr)" with "allegedly offered and promised ~₹2,029 crore (~US$265m, per indictment ¶49; DOJ press figure 'more than $250m') in bribes, ~₹1,750 cr of it to an Andhra Pradesh official".
4. State the charges. Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain were charged with securities fraud conspiracy, wire fraud conspiracy and securities fraud (Counts 2–4), NOT with FCPA bribery. The FCPA conspiracy (Count 1) and obstruction (Count 5) were against Ranjit Gupta, Cyril Cabanes, Saurabh Agarwal, Deepak Malhotra and Rupesh Agarwal (Azure Power/CDPQ). Remove the "+ 5 allegedly paid" grouping.
5. Replace ">US$3bn from US investors" with ">US$2bn in loans from international banks and US-based asset managers plus >US$1bn in bonds marketed to investors in the US among other places".
6. Update the supersession clause: "DOJ consent Rule 48(a) motion 18 May 2026 (ECF 23); on 10 Aug 2026 (ECF 49) Judge Garaufis dismissed with prejudice all counts (2, 3, 4) against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain; Counts 1 and 5 against the five non-appearing defendants remain, dismissal denied without prejudice 3 Sep 2026 (ECF 57)". Delete "single tertiary source; docket not opened".
7. In c006, set from=2026-05-18 and upgrade the tier to documented, sourced to ECF 49.
8. The killIf has partly triggered: the criminal case against gadani is fully dismissed with prejudice. SEC v. Adani (24-cv-8080) is unverified. Keep c003 as a closed historical edge rather than killing it, and add a note that the SEC civil status is still open.
9. Benefit field: the DOJ "over US$2 bn" profit figure is in the indictment ("more than $2 billion" over ~20 years) and can be cited to it.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is "Hindenburg Research published fraud and manipulation allegations against Adani Group on 24 Jan 2023." Hindenburg was active from 2017 until it shut down in January 2025, so the date falls inside its lifetime. The SEBI final order's Background section (primary source, p.3) confirms the date: "Hindenburg Research, a United States based financial research firm and short seller published a report on January 24, 2023, against Adani Group". Wikipedia only says "In January 2023". The contra dates also check out. The rebuttal is dated 29 January in Wikipedia: "On 29 January, Adani released a 413-page response". The SEBI order is signed "DATE:September 18, 2025" by WTM Kamlesh C. Varshney, and AEL sent it to the exchanges on 19 Sep 2025 (order ref WTM/KV/CFID/CFID-SEC1/31672/2025-26).
verdicts.identityTest: Both ends are the right entities. Hindenburg Research is the US short-seller named in the SEBI order. grp:adani is the Adani Group. The SEBI order names the listed noticees: APSEZ, Adani Power (Adani Power Mundra merged into it), and Adani Enterprises (CIN L51100GJ1993PLC019067, on the intimation letterhead). There is no name-collision risk. One point to note: the contra c009 targets node "gadani" while c007 targets "grp:adani". c010 correctly points at the claim id, so the contra chain is intact.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable in the usual sense. This is a single named accusation, not a shared property. Very few Indian conglomerates have been the subject of a short-seller fraud report followed by a SEBI investigation, so the edge does discriminate. The symmetry check is also fine: the edge only records that a named third party made an attributed accusation, and a Hindenburg-style report on any rival group would produce the same edge.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, two. (1) Adani Group's 413-page response of 29 Jan 2023, which Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adani_Group) quotes as calling Hindenburg's conduct "calculated securities fraud" and the report "a calculated attack on India, the independence, integrity and quality of Indian institutions". Wikipedia also says "Adani denied the fraud allegations as without merit." This is recorded as c008. (2) SEBI's final order of 18 Sep 2025 (AEL intimation PDF), para 61: "I find that the allegations made against Noticees in the SCN are not established ... hereby dispose of the instant proceedings against Noticees without any direction." Para 38.19 adds: "In the matter, no fraud is established by SEBI." This is recorded as c010. Wikipedia also records Hindenburg's reply to the rebuttal, which said the response failed to engage with the issues.
verdicts.innocentReading: The edge records only that a short-seller holding disclosed short positions made an accusation, and the claim is correctly worded as an allegation. The innocent reading applies to what was alleged, not to whether it was alleged. The Milestone/Rehvar strand ended with SEBI finding that the loans were not related-party transactions and that all money had been repaid with interest. On that reading, the >US$104bn fall reflects a market reacting to the report rather than proof of fraud. Wikipedia describes it as a decline "after the accusations"; it does not say the report caused it.
verdicts.reason: Every factual component checks out against the sources I opened. The 24 Jan 2023 date and Hindenburg's authorship are confirmed by the primary SEBI order (p.3). The "decades" quote, the >$104bn decline and the 413-page rebuttal of 29 January are all confirmed verbatim in Wikipedia. The "not established" and "without any direction" disposal on the Milestone/Rehvar strand is confirmed verbatim in SEBI order paras 61 and 38.19. The claim is correctly scoped: it attributes the fraud claim to Hindenburg, names the accuser, carries two contras (c008 and c010), and limits the SEBI disposal to the Milestone/Rehvar transactions rather than the whole report. That meets the SPEC bar for "alleged" (a named party plus a contra). It cannot go higher because no regulator or court has found the manipulation. It should not be killed either: the order is titled "with respect to transactions with Milestone Tradelinks Pvt. Ltd. and Rehvar Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.", so it does not dispose of the report's other strands, such as the offshore entities linked to Vinod Adani and the stock-manipulation claims.
verdicts.corrections: (1) In the people.json record, srcs cite only Wikipedia, and Wikipedia gives "In January 2023", not 24 Jan. Add the AEL/SEBI order PDF (p.3, para 1) as the source for the 24 Jan 2023 date, or the Hindenburg report URL itself. (2) Put "brazen stock manipulation and accounting fraud scheme over the course of decades" in quotation marks as Hindenburg's words; do not paraphrase it as "decades-long". (3) Word the $104bn as "a decline of more than US$104bn in bond and share value after the report [reported, Wikipedia]" so it does not read as an established causal loss. (4) The killIf ("Regulator disposal of the specific allegations (see c009)") must not fire on c009 alone, because c009 covers only the Milestone/Rehvar strand. Reword it to require disposal of all of the report's allegations, including the offshore-fund/Vinod Adani and stock-manipulation strands. (5) The predicate "enforce" is defined in the SPEC as agency→subject, and Hindenburg is a private short-seller, not an agency. Either note in the label that this is a private investigation, or use a more suitable predicate if the vocabulary gets one. Keep the tier at alleged. (6) Node consistency: c009 targets "gadani" while c007/c008 use "grp:adani". Check that c009's subject is intentionally the person node, since the noticees include both the companies and Gautam Adani.

verdicts.dateTest: Two events are fused into one edge. (a) Hindenburg alleged on 24 Jan 2023 that Vinod Adani controls offshore shells. Vinod has lived in Dubai since 1994 and was running the entities Hindenburg names at that time, so the dates overlap and this part passes. (b) In 2014 the DRI (Directorate of Revenue Intelligence) mapped a money trail to a Mauritius company allegedly owned by Vinod. Hindenburg's report says Vinod replaced Chang Chung-Ling as director of Electrogen Infra Holding, and his Wikipedia page dates his control of Electrogen to 2010, so this part overlaps too. But the edge carries from=2023-01-24 while describing a 2014 event. It also leaves out what happened next, which is documented. A DRI adjudicating order of August 2017 dropped proceedings against all accused and found 'the allegation that the impugned goods were over-valued does not hold water'. CESTAT upheld that order in July 2022. Both facts are reported in Hindenburg's own report, which this edge relies on.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The 2017 DRI order names 'Shri Vinod Shantilal Adani @ Vinod Shantilal Shah', and Hindenburg names Vinod Adani, elder brother of Gautam. The node's alias 'Vinod Shantilal Adani' matches. No DIN is recorded, which is expected because he is not a director of the Indian listed companies. The 'Shah' alias should be added to the node's aliases. Name-collision risk is low.
verdicts.baseRate: Holding promoter-group stakes through Mauritius or other offshore vehicles is common among Indian conglomerates with NRI (non-resident Indian) family members, historically because of the Mauritius tax treaty. On its own that is weak evidence, probably in the 40-80% band. What is specific here is the allegation that an undisclosed network of 38 Mauritius shells, plus entities in Cyprus, the UAE, Singapore and the Caribbean, moved money into the listed companies and hid related-party dealings. That is under 10% of comparable groups, so it would discriminate if proven. It is not proven. The only adjudicated piece, the DRI power-equipment case, went against the allegation.
verdicts.denialFound: Group-level denial, documented. Wikipedia quoting Bloomberg says that on 29 Jan 2023 Adani released a 413-page response calling Hindenburg's conduct 'calculated securities fraud' and the report 'a calculated attack on India...' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adani_Group). Wikipedia also says 'Adani denied the fraud allegations as without merit.' I could not retrieve a statement about Vinod specifically. The Adani response PDF at adani.com returned 404/JS, and Hindenburg's rebuttal page returned 'Page not found'. The 413-page response is believed to say he holds no managerial position in the listed entities, but this is unverified. On the DRI half, the exculpatory record is itself the contra: the 2017 DRI adjudication found the transactions 'at arms length' and dropped proceedings, and CESTAT upheld that in July 2022, as quoted in Hindenburg's report (https://hindenburgresearch.com/adani/, 'Scandal #3'). SEBI's 18 Sep 2025 final order does not mention Vinod at all: 'Vinod' gets zero hits in the 45-page PDF text. So c018's reliance on the SEBI disposal does not answer c017.
verdicts.innocentReading: Vinod Adani is a Dubai resident since 1994 and a Cypriot citizen, and he is in the promoter group. He holds his promoter-group stake and his family-office investments through offshore vehicles, which is ordinary for NRI promoters, and Mauritius routing was tax-treaty driven. On the DRI power-equipment case, the adjudicating authority found the Electrogen–Adani Power Rajasthan transactions related but priced at arm's length and dropped the charges. The tribunal (CESTAT) upheld that.
verdicts.reason: The Hindenburg half holds. The primary report says: 'We have identified 38 Mauritius shell entities controlled by Vinod Adani or close associates.' That supports an 'alleged' tier with a group-denial contra. The edge as written still fails on four counts. (1) It fuses a separate 2014 DRI allegation into a Hindenburg-sourced edge. It leaves out that the DRI matter was dropped on the merits in August 2017 and that CESTAT upheld this in July 2022. That meets the claim's own killIf ('DRI matter closed on merits'). The node text's 'did not result in adverse final findings that this sweep could document' understates a documented exoneration. (2) It overstates the ₹2,323 cr link. Wikipedia says the 2014 DRI trail went to a Mauritius company 'allegedly owned by Vinod Shantilal Adani'. Separately, it says DRI sent SEBI a CD 'suggesting the improper diversion of Rs. 2,323 crore'. It never says the ₹2,323 cr was traced to his company, so 'traced ~₹2,323 cr ... to a Mauritius company said to be his' is a conjunction. (3) Hindenburg is not an agency, so pred=enforce from Hindenburg is miscoded. (4) The only source cited is Wikipedia, even though the primary Hindenburg report is reachable. Also, the contra c018 relies on the SEBI Sep 2025 order, and that order does not mention Vinod Adani.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Split the edge. Keep c017 as Hindenburg's allegation only: s=energy:hindenburg, t=energy:vinod-adani, from=2023-01-24, tier=alleged. Add src https://hindenburgresearch.com/adani/ (primary) and quote the '38 Mauritius shell entities controlled by Vinod Adani or close associates' sentence. Recode pred: 'enforce' is for agencies. If the schema has no allegation predicate, note that Hindenburg is a short-seller making an assertion, not a proceeding. 2) Move the DRI content to a separate edge: s=DRI node, t=energy:vinod-adani, pred=enforce, from=2014 (DRI investigation / show-cause notice on power-equipment over-valuation via Electrogen Infra), to=2017-08 (adjudication dropped proceedings). Attach a documented supersede/contra: August 2017 adjudication order ('allegation that the impugned goods were over-valued does not hold water'; transactions found 'at arms length'), upheld by CESTAT in July 2022. Mark that edge's killIf as MET. 3) Reword the ₹2,323 cr sentence to match the source: 'DRI in 2014 sent SEBI a letter and CD suggesting improper diversion of Rs 2,323 crore via over-valued power-equipment imports; separately it mapped a money trail to a Mauritius company allegedly owned by Vinod Adani (Wikipedia).' Do not say the ₹2,323 cr was traced to his company. 4) In the node vinod-adani d[1], replace 'did not result in adverse final findings that this sweep could document' with the 2017 drop and the 2022 CESTAT upholding. Add alias 'Vinod Shantilal Shah'. 5) In c018, state that SEBI's 18 Sep 2025 order (WTM/KV/CFID/CFID-SEC1/31672/2025-26) does not name or examine Vinod Adani. It addressed loans involving Adicorp, Milestone and Rehvar, with noticees including Rajesh Adani, Gautam Adani and Jugeshinder Singh, so it is not a contra on his offshore control. Keep 'Vinod-specific denial not retrieved' as a flagged weakness. 6) upgradeIf should stay on the SEBI FPI/MPS (minimum public shareholding) beneficial-ownership findings, which are still pending.

verdicts.dateTest: Actor, act, object and date: Government of Bihar (energy department and its power companies) ran a reverse e-auction in 2024–25 and signed a PSA with Adani Power in Sept 2025 for the 2,400 MW Pirpainti (Bhagalpur) thermal project. The Nitish Kumar NDA government was in office throughout, and Bijendra Prasad Yadav was energy minister. Adani Power was a live listed company throughout. The dates overlap and nothing is anachronistic. The Wire (7 Nov 2025) refers to a "2024 bidding process". ThePrint (11 Nov 2025) says "the state government and Adani Power signed a PSA agreement in September".
verdicts.identityTest: Target: both outlets name "Adani Power" (Adani Power Ltd, the listed entity), so co:adani-power matches. The source does not name an Adani SPV, but Adani may execute the project through one, and that would not change the edge. Source node: ThePrint says only "the state government". The legal PSA counterparty is probably the Bihar discoms (NBPDCL/SBPDCL) via BSPHCL, but neither source says so. energy:govt-of-bihar is acceptable as an umbrella node. The Wire notes that the land was first acquired by Bihar State Power Generation Company Ltd. The name "Adani" carries no collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: In a reverse e-auction, the award goes to L1 almost by definition. Nearly 100% of competitive tariff-based bids end with the L1 bidder signing. On its own the award edge does not discriminate: it records a transaction, not an anomaly. The tariff-premium allegation (Rs 62,000 cr) is a separate, alleged-tier claim and correctly sits on its own edge. Symmetry: the same lens gives the same kind of edge for any L1 winner in recent state thermal auctions, including awards to JSW, Torrent, or Adani in other states. Nothing here depends on which party runs the state.
verdicts.denialFound: Adani Power (The Wire, 7 Nov 2025) called R.K. Singh's claims "entirely unfounded", stemming from a "misunderstanding" of the project history: https://m.thewire.in/article/government/r-k-singh-blames-nitish-govt-for-rs-62000-crore-loss-in-adani-awarded-bhagalpur-power-project. Bihar Energy Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav (ThePrint, 11 Nov 2025): "The company that bid the lowest (amount) in the tender was selected. The decision was taken in the interest of the state." ThePrint also reports that Adani Power "refused to respond to a detailed questionnaire" (asked, no response): https://theprint.in/india/asked-bihar-govt-about-rs-62k-cr-power-plant-scam-was-told-all-hunky-dory-ex-union-minister-rk-singh/2780894/. These responses concern the overpricing allegation, not the award fact, which nobody disputes.
verdicts.innocentReading: Bihar ran an open reverse e-auction with four bidders, and Adani Power bid lowest at Rs 6.075/kWh. The state signed a 25-year PSA with L1, as the competitive-bidding guidelines require. Recent new-build thermal tariffs have been in a similar range, and the nominal-rent land lease follows Bihar's 2025 industrial policy.
verdicts.reason: Both sources confirm the claim, and ThePrint states the key facts in its own voice, citing a published document: "details submitted by Bihar's energy department to the state's electricity regulatory commission." ThePrint quotes: "Among four bidders, Adani Power made the lowest bid – of Rs 6.075 per kilowatt hours"; "The second lowest bid was by JSW Energy Limited, the submission shows"; "the state government and Adani Power signed a PSA agreement in September." The Wire independently confirms 2,400 MW, Pirpainti/Bhagalpur, Rs 6.075/kWh and Adani as the winner. The claim meets "reported" (one credible outlet citing published documents). It stops short of "documented" because the bidder count, JSW as L2 and the Sept date come from ThePrint alone, and the BERC filing itself has not been opened. The claim is a neutral award edge, with no wrongdoing implied, so no contra is needed.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Replace "Press-only sourcing; tender record not opened" with "Per ThePrint citing the Bihar energy department's submission to BERC; submission not yet opened". Add upgradeIf: the BERC tariff-adoption petition/order or an Adani Power exchange filing on the PSA is retrieved, which would make it documented. (2) Attribute "four bidders", "JSW Energy L2" and "Sept 2025 PSA" to ThePrint only; The Wire states none of the three. (3) Record the PSA counterparty as "state government per ThePrint; legal signatory (BSPHCL/NBPDCL/SBPDCL) unconfirmed". (4) Change "amount unknown" to "contract value not disclosed; 25-year term, Rs 6.075/kWh". (5) Add the Bihar energy minister's response ("lowest bidder was selected ... in the interest of the state") to the record, keeping the Rs 62,000 cr allegation on its separate alleged-tier edge with Adani's "entirely unfounded" as contra.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: R.K. Singh (ex-Power Minister 3 Sep 2017 to 11 Jun 2024, still a BJP member at the time) alleged a ₹62,000 cr overpricing in the Bhagalpur (Pirpainti) PSA and sought a CBI probe in early Nov 2025. That date works for an ex-minister acting as a critic. It does not work for the text's phrase "after his BJP suspension". National Herald (4 Nov 2025) says "the BJP seems to have taken no action against him yet". Wikipedia, and the repo's own energy:rk-singh node, date the suspension and resignation to 15 Nov 2025.
