That is after both polling phases (6 and 11 Nov) and the 14 Nov results. So the allegation came before the suspension. The record's "from": "2025-11-06" is also too late, because National Herald carried the allegation on 4 Nov 2025.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. R.K. Singh is identified by office with dates: Union Minister of Power and MNRE 2017–24, MP for Arrah, BJP. Every source names him as the former Union power minister. The other end, Adani Power Ltd, is named as the lowest bidder and PSA counterparty for the Bhagalpur/Pirpainti thermal project. Adani Power's own statement in The Wire confirms it is the same entity. Name-collision risk is low because the office pins him down, although neither end has a DIN or CIN.
verdicts.baseRate: Not measurable from the sources opened. None of them gives a benchmark of recent competitively bid greenfield thermal PSAs of 2024–25. The ₹2.75/unit "correct" fixed charge (so ₹1.41/unit excess, ₹62,000 cr over 25 years) is Singh's own figure, not a CERC or CEA benchmark. Tariff-based competitive bids for new thermal capacity in 2024–25 have commonly come in around ₹5.4–6.1/kWh. If ₹6.075 falls inside that band, the overpricing claim does not discriminate. The record's killIf and upgradeIf are pointed at the right test, but nobody has run it. On symmetry: the accuser is a BJP insider attacking an NDA government, so this is not an opposition-only reading.
verdicts.denialFound: Adani Power (The Wire, 7 Nov 2025): the allegations are "entirely unfounded" and reflect "a misunderstanding" of the transparent process. It said "certain electorally frustrated individuals and political interests are attempting to further a false and baseless narrative", that it "emerged as the lowest bidder, offering a tariff of Rs 6.075 per kWh", and that "the land had been leased rather than sold ... at a nominal rent, in line with the Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Policy, 2025". Bihar energy minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav (ThePrint, 11 Nov 2025): "The company that bid the lowest (amount) in the tender was selected." According to ThePrint, the Adani spokesperson "refused to respond to a detailed questionnaire" from ThePrint. National Herald (4 Nov) says Adani "has not yet issued any statement", so it cannot back the contra. URL: https://m.thewire.in/article/government/r-k-singh-blames-nitish-govt-for-rs-62000-crore-loss-in-adani-awarded-bhagalpur-power-project
verdicts.innocentReading: The tariff came out of an open competitive tariff-based bid won by the lowest bidder. A ₹4.165 fixed charge reflects the capital cost of a new 2,400 MW ultra-supercritical plant at 2025 prices. Singh's ₹2.75 benchmark is his own assumption and has not been tested against contemporaneous bids. Leasing the land at nominal rent follows the state's published 2025 industrial policy and is not a bespoke concession. The timing, days before polling, points to a political dispute inside the NDA as much as a procurement finding.
verdicts.reason: The core edge survives at alleged. A named party (Singh, quoted verbatim in National Herald: "There must be a CBI investigation") makes the allegation, and there is a documented contra (Adani Power's "entirely unfounded" statement in The Wire). But the text as written contains a chronology error. It says the allegation came "after his BJP suspension", when the suspension was on 15 Nov 2025, after the polls and after the allegation. Getting this wrong changes the reading: it turns a sitting BJP leader attacking his own alliance into an expelled dissident. The text also says "four-bidder tender", which none of the three opened sources supports; The Wire explicitly gives no bidder count. The claim cannot pass in its current wording.
verdicts.corrections: 1. text: delete "and after his BJP suspension". Replace it with "while still a BJP member; he was suspended and resigned on 15 Nov 2025, after the polls". 2. from: 2025-11-06 becomes 2025-11-04 or earlier (National Herald published it on 4 Nov 2025; The Wire traces it to an earlier Indian Express interview). 3. text: remove "four-bidder" unless a source that states the bidder count is opened and added. Say "open competitive tender, lowest bidder" instead. 4. Attribute the CBI-probe element to National Herald only; The Wire and ThePrint do not mention the CBI. 5. c021 srcs: remove National Herald, which reports that Adani had not responded as of 4 Nov. Add ThePrint's note that Adani declined its questionnaire, and the Bihar energy minister's "lowest bidder" statement as a second contra. 6. energy:rk-singh node, d[3]: make it read "Suspended ... and resigned 15 Nov 2025" so the sequence is clear.

verdicts.dateTest: Pass. The claim reads: "US prosecutors allege Adani/Azure executives offered and promised an unnamed AP official ~Rs 1,750 cr between about Aug 2021 and Dec 2021 so that AP discoms would sign the 7 GW PSA." The indictment (EDNY 1:24-cr-00433, Doc 1, filed 10/24/24, ¶48–50) says Gautam Adani met "Foreign Official #1 in Andhra Pradesh … on or about August 7, 2021, … September 12, 2021 and … November 20, 2021", and that AP's discoms "entered into a PSA with SECI on or about December 1, 2021". That falls inside the YSRCP government's term (May 2019–Jun 2024), so the actor window and the act overlap. Later dates also check out. SEC consent judgments were entered 2026-05-14 (SEC LR-26554: Gautam $6m + Sagar $12m = $18m, "without admitting or denying"). Counts 2–4 were dismissed with prejudice on 2026-08-10 (The Wire, 47-page order). On 2026-09-03 DOJ's request to dismiss Counts 1 (FCPA conspiracy) and 5 (obstruction) against the five non-appearing co-defendants was "denied without prejudice" (The Wire, Sep 2026). One problem: the edge's from=2021-01-01 has no source. The earliest AP-specific act in the indictment is 2021-08-07.
verdicts.identityTest: Partial. The AP official is unnamed ("Foreign Official #1, a senior government official of Andhra Pradesh"), and the claim correctly does not name anyone, so there is no name-collision risk. The target node is the problem. DOJ took no enforcement action against the Government of Andhra Pradesh. The indictment's counterparties are an unnamed official and the AP discoms (APPCC, APCPDCL, APEPDCL, APSPDCL), and today's GoAP is a TDP-led government. An 'enforce' edge from DOJ to energy:govt-of-andhra-pradesh implies the state was a defendant. The defendants are correctly scoped: the Adanis and Jaain on counts 2–4; Gupta and R. Agarwal (Azure) and Cabanes, S. Agarwal and Malhotra (CDPQ) on counts 1 and 5.
verdicts.baseRate: Among the offtakers of SECI's Manufacturing-Linked Project, all five (Odisha, J&K, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, AP) appear in the indictment as signing PSAs "following the promise of bribes" (Jul 2021–Feb 2022). That is 100%, so being named is not what sets AP apart. What does set it apart: a specific sum (Rs 1,750 cr of the Rs 2,029 cr total), three dated personal meetings with Gautam Adani, and the largest volume ("by far the largest amount of any Indian state"). The symmetry check holds. The offtaking states were run by YSRCP, BJD, DMK and Congress, plus J&K under central rule, so the lens does not single out one party. Three other states signed at the same Rs 2.49 tariff and were not singled out.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is already linked as contras. Adani Group, 2024-11-21: allegations "baseless", denied. AGEL exchange statement, 2024-11-27: no FCPA charge against the Adanis (BusinessToday URL in c052). YSRCP note: "There is no direct agreement between AP DISCOMs and any other entities including those belonging to the Adani group" (https://www.ysrcongress.com/press-release/greement-seci-brief-note-93009, c053). The Naidu government kept the PSA, saying it "cannot scrap … without obtaining solid proofs" (c054). MEA: "legal matter involving private firms", with no request received (c060). After the dismissal, Gautam Adani said he accepted it with "humility and deep respect" (Wikipedia).
verdicts.innocentReading: AP signed for 7 GW at Rs 2.49/kWh for 25 years, then a record-low tariff, with ISTS charges waived by an MoP order. APERC approved it on 2021-11-11 and CERC also approved it. The contract ran through SECI, not directly with Adani, and SECI was offering the same capacity to every state. A cheap, long-dated, waiver-backed tariff is reason enough for a discom to sign. A hostile successor government with every political motive reviewed the deal and did not cancel it. No Indian agency has investigated. The allegation has never been tested at trial. On the Adani counts, the judge granted dismissal on the "inactionable puffery" ground and said that should not be read "as expressing any opinion about the merits of the case."
verdicts.reason: I could not refute the core allegation, and 'alleged' is the right tier. The primary indictment (DOJ-hosted PDF, ¶49–50) states the claim almost word for word: "Approximately 1,750 crore rupees (approximately $228 million) of the corrupt payments was offered to Foreign Official #1 in exchange for Foreign Official #1 causing Andhra Pradesh's state electricity distribution companies to agree to purchase seven gigawatts", and the PSA was signed "on or about December 1, 2021". The named accusers are DOJ and SEC, and four contras are attached. Every 2026 procedural fact also checks out: $18m SEC settlement without admission (LR-26554, 2026-05-14); dismissal with prejudice 2026-08-10, where the judge disclaimed any view on the merits; FCPA and obstruction counts kept alive on 2026-09-03. The weakness is the source chain in the claim's own srcs, which only partly supports it. SEC PR 2024-181 says "hundreds of millions" but not $250m and does not mention AP. Wikipedia supports the >$250m figure and the 10 Aug 2026 permanent dismissal, but not the SEC settlement, the 3 Sep ruling, or anything specific to AP. South First supports Rs 1,750 cr but says "paid", and gives no PSA date. The $18m settlement, the 2026-09-03 status, 7 GW and 2021-12-01 are not in any listed source. The target node also wrongly makes GoAP the object of enforcement.
verdicts.corrections: 1. srcs: add the indictment PDF (https://www.justice.gov/usao-edny/media/1378001/dl?inline=, ¶48–50) as the primary source for Rs 1,750 cr/$228m, 7 GW and 2021-12-01. Add SEC LR-26554 (https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/litigation-releases/lr-26554) for the settlement: $6m Gautam + $12m Sagar, 2026-05-14, without admitting or denying. Add The Wire Aug 2026 (https://m.thewire.in/article/law/us-judge-dismisses-adani-fraud-charges-but-rejects-doj-claim-that-india-investigated-bribery) and The Wire Sep 2026 (https://m.thewire.in/article/law/us-judge-gautam-adani-bribery-charges-co-defendants-india-claim). Demote or drop Wikipedia as a tertiary source. 2. text: change "(~Rs 1,750 cr per press)" to "(~Rs 1,750 cr / ~$228m per indictment ¶49)". Attribute ">$250m" to the indictment and DOJ, not the SEC complaint; the indictment's own figure is ~Rs 2,029 cr (~$265m). 3. text: change "FCPA count … still pending" to "FCPA-conspiracy (Count 1) and obstruction (Count 5) counts against Azure/CDPQ ex-executives remain; DOJ's dismissal request denied without prejudice 2026-09-03 (DOJ may refile)". 4. text: add the judge's line that dismissal is not "expressing any opinion about the merits", and note that the sole ground accepted was "inactionable puffery". 5. from: change 2021-01-01 to 2021-08-07, the first AP meeting alleged in ¶48. 6. Node/predicate: DOJ did not enforce against GoAP. Retarget t to an unresolved node such as "AP Foreign Official #1 (unnamed)" or the AP discoms, or change pred to "alleges". If the GoAP target stays, the label should make clear the state is not a defendant.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: DOJ (EDNY CR-24-433) alleged on 2024-11-20 that Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain influenced SECI's 2.3 GW reallocation between about April 2022 and March 2024. The Wire dates the trigger to Azure CEO Ranjit Gupta's resignation in April 2022. Reporting on the indictment dates SECI's termination and reallocation letters to 2024-03-18. The indictment was unsealed on 2024-11-20. The record's from/to window of 2023-01-01 to 2023-12-31 is not supported by any source: it leaves out both the April 2022 start and the March 2024 reallocation. Both men held their roles (AGEL Executive Director and AGEL MD) throughout, so their tenure overlaps the conduct. The claim also leaves out that the counts against Sagar Adani and Jaain were dismissed with prejudice on DOJ's motion on 2026-08-10 (recorded elsewhere in the same file as c056).
verdicts.identityTest: The actors are right: Sagar R. Adani and Vneet S. Jaain are named defendants, and the indictment's 'Indian Energy Company' is Adani Green Energy. The target node is wrong. The edge 'doj -> co:adani-green-energy, pred enforce' says DOJ took enforcement action against AGEL. AGEL was not a defendant. The indictment charged individuals, and AGEL appears only as the unnamed 'Indian Energy Company'. The graph already has nodes energy:sagar-adani and energy:vneet-jaain. AGEL belongs in the benefit.who field, which already names it, not as the target of an enforce edge.
verdicts.baseRate: A base rate does not really apply to a quoted indictment allegation. For comparison, PPA reallocation inside the 12 GW manufacturing-linked tender from one co-awardee (Azure) to the other (AGEL) at the same tariff is unusual: there is no other known SECI reallocation of this size. So the property is discriminating, not routine. Symmetry holds: the same indictment charges Azure and CDPQ executives, and their FCPA count is still alive as of 2026-09-03. The lens is not aimed only at the Adani side.
verdicts.denialFound: SECI CMD R.P. Gupta, 2024-11-21, as quoted by The Wire: 'There is nothing against SECI. It has done nothing wrong... There is no mention of any wrongdoing or irregularity on part of SECI.' SECI was asked and did not respond. The Wire wrote to SECI's CMD and said the story would be updated when a response came; none had arrived by publication (https://m.thewire.in/article/government/adani-bribery-did-seci-share-internal-documents-with-accused). AGEL's 2024-11-27 statement (BusinessToday) said the Adanis were not charged under the FCPA count. No denial found that addresses the specific claim about internal SECI documents.
verdicts.innocentReading: SECI terminated Azure's 2.3 GW and substituted the other co-awardee under the same tender at the same tariff, through a supplemental agreement. When a contract is amended, the incoming counterparty routinely receives and marks up draft letters and agreements. Under that reading, 'obtaining and revising internal SECI documents' could describe normal counterparty review of drafts, not a leak. This reading is not ruled out, and no SECI officer has been named or charged.
verdicts.reason: The quote checks out word for word in The Wire (22 Nov 2024), which reproduces the indictment: 'The defendants SAGAR R. ADANI and VNEET S. JAAIN and other Indian Energy Company personnel also secretly influenced the SECI process for reallocation of the 2.3 GW PPAs ... by obtaining and revising internal SECI documents.' The allegation comes from a named party (DOJ), is attributed, and has a contra (c055x), so it clears the bar for 'alleged'. Three field-level problems remain. (a) 'Implicates SECI officials' is The Wire's inference ('could not have accessed... without help from within SECI'); the indictment does not say it. (b) The target node treats AGEL as an enforcement defendant, which it was not. (c) The 2023 date window is wrong, and the dismissal with prejudice of these counts on 2026-08-10 is left out. None of these defeats the core claim that the indictment made this allegation.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change 't' from co:adani-green-energy to energy:sagar-adani, and add a parallel edge or mention for energy:vneet-jaain. Keep AGEL only in benefit.who. 2) Change from/to to from 2022-04-01 (approximate: the Azure CEO resigned in April 2022) and to 2024-03-18 (the SECI termination and reallocation letters). Alternatively, date the enforce event 2024-11-20. 3) Add to the text and to c055x: 'Counts against Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain dismissed with prejudice on DOJ motion, 2026-08-10 (c056); dismissal on prosecutorial discretion, not on the merits.' 4) Reword 'Implicates SECI officials' to 'The Wire inferred that access would have required help from within SECI; no SECI official is named in the indictment or charged.' 5) Add the primary source: the EDNY indictment, 1:24-cr-00433 (justice.gov). 6) c055x: say SECI 'did not respond by publication to The Wire's letter to its CMD'. The Wire does not say its questions were specifically about documents reaching the accused.

verdicts.dateTest: PASS. Claim: the MNRE minister directed SECI on 2023-05-01, and SECI wrote on 2023-07-17 that it "would like to surrender" its 23,000 ha. R.K. Singh ran MNRE from Sept 2017 to June 2024, so both dates fall in his tenure. Scroll names him directly: "at a meeting held on May 1, 2023, chaired by the minister for new and renewable energy, RK Singh". Two date problems in the record. (a) "surrendered in July 2023" is SECI's request letter; Gujarat's high-powered committee only dealt with the land on 2023-08-23/24. So `to` should be 2023-07-17 (request), with the takeback shown in c073. (b) `from: 2020-09-09` comes from Wikipedia's park-approval date, which covered 60,000 ha. Scroll only says parcels were allocated by around the December 2020 inauguration. The per-SECI allotment date is not in any opened source.
verdicts.identityTest: PASS with caveats. SECI (Solar Energy Corporation of India, the central PSU) is the entity Scroll names. The "renewable energy minister" is identified by name only for the 1 May 2023 meeting. Scroll's summary line "on the instructions of the renewable energy minister" does not name him, but the only named minister in the chain is R.K. Singh, so the attribution holds. On the recipient: Scroll says Adani Power, in a consortium with Mundra Solar Technology, was "selected in-principle, as the park developer" on 2023-08-24. That is not a final allotment, and it is a different company from the 2020 allottee, Adani Green. There is no name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating on its own. SECI mostly runs auctions and trades power rather than building plants. Its parcel was limited to wind (Scroll: 3,000 MW approved, only 1,100 MW viable) and SECI had called it "not economically viable". It is routine for a PSU to hand back land it can't use after a ministerial review meeting. Nobody has established how often park land surrendered in Gujarat is re-allotted by competitive process. What makes this unusual is what came next: the surrender happened after the MoD relaxation that fixed the viability problem, Adani's letter of 3 July came before SECI's of 17 July, and the land went to a private allottee despite a rule reserving it for PSUs. Those points belong in c073 and c076, not in this edge. Symmetry check: the same lens applied to NTPC, GSECL or GIPCL shows no surrender-then-private-reallocation. SECI is the only case.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial of the ministerial instruction was found. Scroll (Ravi Nair, 12 Feb 2025) says: "We have contacted the ministry of defence, the Gujarat government, the ministry of renewable energy and SECI, seeking responses ... This story will be updated if we receive any responses." They were asked and did not respond. The Adani Group told The Guardian: "We are fully compliant with all the state and central government laws and regulations and have secured all the necessary approvals" and "The land allocation ... adheres to policy guidelines" (https://scroll.in/article/1076846/...). That addresses the allocation, not the instruction to SECI. Pralhad Joshi (MNRE minister) told the Lok Sabha on 12 March 2025 that "all necessary clearances from the Union government and the state government have been obtained", and the opposition walked out over the reply (https://www.thenewsminute.com/news/adani-solar-project-opposition-walks-out-of-ls-over-ministers-insufficient-reply). He did not address the instruction. There is no record of R.K. Singh responding, and no evidence he was asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: The minister's 1 May 2023 review meeting told SECI to "analyze the option of surrendering" the land "based on the viability of the project". That is an ordinary portfolio review of a PSU asset that had been stuck for about two years at a wind-only 1,100 MW. SECI builds almost nothing itself, and paying ₹15,000/ha/yr rent sized for 3 GW on land yielding a third of that was a real cost. Returning the land fits balance-sheet discipline without implying anyone intended it to reach a particular successor. Scroll itself admits "The records do not show why the SECI did not proceed with this project under the new rules."
verdicts.reason: The claim survives at the reported tier. Scroll (Ravi Nair, 12 Feb 2025, first reported by The Guardian as one joint investigation) quotes SECI's own 17 July 2023 letter to GPCL, so it is one credible outlet relying on published documents. Its sentence: "the firm surrendered the land on the instructions of the renewable energy minister." But the claim quotes wording the source does not use, and it overstates the document. The phrase 'following instructions from the renewable energy minister' does not appear in Scroll. The underlying document records only that the minister's meeting "directed [SECI] to 'analyze the option of surrendering' ... 'based on the viability of the project'." "Instructions to surrender" is Scroll's reading, not the letter's words. Scroll and The Guardian are one investigation, not two independent outlets, so the claim cannot be upgraded to documented. The claim's own hedge ("rests on one investigation ... no MNRE letter opened") is accurate. The quote and figures below must be fixed before publication.
verdicts.corrections: 1) text/d: remove the invented quotation. Replace it with Scroll's own words, marked as Scroll's characterisation: surrendered "on the instructions of the renewable energy minister". Add the primary-document wording: a 2023-05-01 meeting "chaired by the minister for new and renewable energy, RK Singh" directed SECI to "analyze the option of surrendering" the land "based on the viability of the project" (as quoted from SECI's 17 July 2023 letter). 2) lab: remove "11,500 MW". That nominal figure comes from Wikipedia/ThePrint and conflicts with Scroll, which says SECI had MoD approval only for a wind park of 3,000 MW, with 1,100 MW viable. Use "23,000 ha (wind-only; 3,000 MW approved, 1,100 MW viable)". 3) to: change to 2023-07-17 (the date of the surrender-request letter). Note that Gujarat's high-powered committee took up the land on 2023-08-23/24. 4) from: 2020-09-09 is the park-level approval date from Wikipedia and is not sourced for SECI's parcel. Mark it "c. 2020 (by Dec 2020 inauguration)" or cite the GR. 5) "the land that then went to Adani Power": qualify as "Adani Power (consortium with Mundra Solar Technology) selected 'in-principle, as the park developer' on 2023-08-24". 6) srcs: say Scroll/Guardian is a single investigation (byline Ravi Nair, 12 Feb 2025), not two outlets. The Wikipedia source supports only the allotment figure, not the surrender. 7) Add an explicit non-response note: MNRE and SECI were asked and did not respond; there is no record of R.K. Singh responding; Joshi's 12 March 2025 Lok Sabha reply ("all necessary clearances ... obtained") does not address the instruction. 8) Sibling fix: the from-date of c074 (2024-01-01) is wrong. The statement appeared in February 2025 reporting.

verdicts.dateTest: Actor, act and date: the Gujarat CM's high-powered committee (CM Bhupendra Patel, in office since Sep 2021) selected Adani Power as park developer for SECI's surrendered Khavda land on 2023-08-24. The windows overlap. The rest of the sequence matches the source: Adani letters on 2023-07-03 (23,000 ha) and 2023-07-07 (25,500 ha); SECI letter on 2023-07-17 seeking hybrid use and offering to surrender the land; RK Singh's MNRE meeting on 2023-05-01 directing SECI to 'analyze the option of surrendering'. RK Singh was MNRE minister at that time, so that overlaps too. There is one flaw inside the source: Scroll also mentions 'a later meeting chaired by Gujarat's chief minister on August 23, 2023' and calls it 'the August meeting'. That is probably the same meeting as 24 Aug, but the date is not fully pinned down. The '~445 sq km' holding is Scroll's figure as of publication (2025-02-12), not a current one.
verdicts.identityTest: Scroll quotes the committee's decision: 'Adani Power would be "selected in-principle, as the park developer"'. So the node co:adani-power (Adani Power Ltd) is correct. The application itself came from a consortium: 'Adani Power and its sister concern Mundra Solar Technology … bid as a consortium'. The earlier 2020 Khavda allotment went to Adani Green Energy, a different legal entity, and Adani's defence cites 'the credentials and performance of Adani Green Energy'. That fits both with how Adani describes the allocation and with the claim's attribution. The Government of Gujarat is the source node, acting through the CM-chaired committee and GPCL as nodal agency. There is no name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: Unknown, and probably not low. Gujarat's original 2020 Khavda allotments also went to named parties on application, with no auction on record. Those went to two central and two state PSUs plus two private firms, Adani Green (19,000 ha) and Sarjan Realities (9,500 ha). Allotting park land by nomination or committee decision appears to be the state's normal method, not an exception made for Adani. So 'no competitive bidding documented' does not by itself set Adani apart. What does set this case apart is the source's own record: (a) the committee reversed its earlier rule that the land would go only to PSUs; (b) other PSU and private companies had 'demanded' the land, and Adani Power was chosen over them; (c) the result was that one group holds more of the park than all other developers combined (my arithmetic: 44,500/72,400 ha is about 61%). The symmetry check comes out the same way. Sarjan's 2020 allotment, run the same way, would show 'no bidding' but not the reversal or the concentration.
verdicts.denialFound: (1) Adani Group, statement to The Guardian (quoted in Scroll 2025-02-12; Adani did not answer Scroll directly): 'We are fully compliant with all the state and central government laws and regulations and have secured all the necessary approvals from the relevant competent authorities … The land allocation for the project adheres to policy guidelines and is based on the credentials and performance of Adani Green Energy.' https://scroll.in/article/1076846/how-adani-bagged-an-energy-project-on-india-pak-border-for-which-defence-rules-were-relaxed. (2) Union MNRE Minister Pralhad Joshi, Lok Sabha, 2025-03-12: 'all approvals and licences to any proposal are granted after obtaining clearances from the Centre, the state and relevant agencies.' He did not address the allotment, the bidding or Adani. https://m.thewire.in/article/politics/lok-sabha-opp-questions-relaxed-norms-for-adani-power-project-at-indo-park-border-walks-out/amp. (3) Scroll put questions to the Gujarat chief secretary (specifically whether there was any tendering or competitive process), MoD, MNRE and SECI. None had responded at publication. No later answer found.
verdicts.innocentReading: SECI trades power rather than building plants. Its wind-only parcel was unviable (1,100 MW), and the ministry told it to review whether to keep the land. The MoD relaxation of 2023-05-08 was circulated to all states and ministries, and its terms were general, so any developer could have read it and applied. Adani was already the largest private allottee next door and had a module-manufacturing base. The committee's published criteria (experience, financial and technical capacity, capital already invested in Gujarat, a manufacturing base) are the kind a state could honestly apply to meet ambitious renewable targets. Gujarat does not appear to have auctioned any park land at Khavda, so doing without bidding here was consistent with past practice.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives. Scroll (Ravi Nair, 2025-02-12, a joint investigation with The Guardian) quotes directly from the 24 Aug 2023 committee minutes, the Adani letters of 3 and 7 July and SECI's letter of 17 July. Every element of the claim is in the text: the date, the actor, the 23,000/25,500 ha figures, 'selected in-principle, as the park developer', and 445 sq km / more than all other developers combined. Scroll also asked Gujarat whether there was any tender and got no reply. That is one credible outlet relying on published documents, which clears the 'reported' bar. It does not reach 'documented': the minutes themselves were not opened, and the Guardian and Scroll are the same investigation, not two independent outlets. The claim does need some language fixed, because it leaves out facts from the same source that cut both ways (see corrections).
verdicts.corrections: (a) In text/lab, change 'selected' to 'selected in-principle as park developer' (the minutes' wording). (b) Add that the applicant was a consortium of Adani Power and Mundra Solar Technology. (c) Add from the same source that the minutes record the SECI land 'demanded' by 'public sector companies as well as private companies'. Adani Power was chosen from several claimants on criteria the committee stated, and the committee reversed its earlier PSU-only reservation. (d) The upgradeIf condition 'Committee minutes show no alternative applicants' contradicts the source, which already says other companies applied. Replace it with 'Committee minutes/GPCL records show no public notice or evaluation of the other claimants; RTI shows lease terms below the SECI offer'. (e) Mark '~61% of park' as derived (44,500 ha / 72,400 ha). The source says only 'more than all the other developers combined'. Add 'as of Feb 2025' to the 445 sq km figure. (f) Note that the source also mentions a CM-chaired meeting dated 23 Aug 2023. Keep 24 Aug as the committee date but flag the discrepancy. (g) Surrender: the SECI letter of 17 July says it 'would like to surrender' the land. Say 'SECI sought to surrender on 2023-07-17', not a completed July surrender. (h) Fixes to c074: the Adani statement went to The Guardian, and Scroll says Adani did not respond to Scroll, so change 'Scroll/Guardian' to 'The Guardian (quoted by Scroll)'. Change from=2024-01-01 to 2025-02-12. Add Pralhad Joshi's Lok Sabha reply of 2025-03-12 (The Wire) as the only on-record government response, and note it is generic.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: MoD relaxed border rules (meeting 21 Apr 2023, letter 8 May 2023); Adani wrote on 3 Jul 2023; SECI asked for hybrid use and surrendered on 17 Jul 2023; Gujarat's high-powered committee under the CM picked Adani Power on 24 Aug 2023. Scroll confirms each date: "On July 3, 2023, two weeks before the SECI surrendered its land, the Adani group wrote to Gujarat Power Corporation asking for an allotment of 23,000 hectares"; "in a letter sent on July 17, 2023, the SECI asked the Gujarat Power Corporation Limited ... to allow it 'to use the allotted land … for establishment of Hybrid (Solar + Wind) Power Projects'"; "On August 24, 2023, this matter was taken up in the meeting of a high-powered committee under the chairmanship of the chief minister." The officeholders were in post on those dates: R.K. Singh was Power & NRE minister 2021-07 to 2024-06, which covers the 1 May 2023 meeting. The ORDER is wrong, though. SECI had been asking for hybrid use since at least April 2023: it met local defence authorities on 6 Apr, and the 21 Apr MoD meeting was convened to deal with "the defence restrictions that were coming in the way of the Solar Energy Corporation of India's project". The 17 July letter looks back on that request ("the decision on the same has not been communicated to us to date") and then surrenders the land. So "Adani 3 Jul → SECI hybrid request 17 Jul" is false. The sequence also leaves out the event that decides the foreknowledge question: "at a meeting held on May 1, 2023, chaired by the minister for new and renewable energy, RK Singh, the corporation was directed to 'analyze the option of surrendering' the land." That is two months before Adani's letter and one week before the 8 May guideline. There is also a date conflict inside the source: it cites the CM meeting as both 23 Aug 2023 and 24 Aug 2023.
verdicts.identityTest: Partial match. Per Scroll, the 3 July request came from a consortium: "Adani Power and its sister concern Mundra Solar Technology ... bid as a consortium". The 7 July revision to 25,500 ha was made by Adani Power. The 24 Aug selection names "Adani Power ... 'selected in-principle, as the park developer'". Adani Green Energy was the separate 2020 allottee. The edge target co:adani-power is correct, but the text says "Adani request" without mentioning Mundra Solar Technology as co-applicant. No CIN is recorded on the node (cin null). There is no name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: Not measurable from what we have, and the claim says so correctly. There is no record of how Gujarat, or any other state park, reallocates land that a PSU surrenders, so we cannot tell whether a no-bid, in-principle selection is unusual. The MoD relaxation itself does not discriminate. The 8 May 2023 letter went to "all states and union territories" and several ministries, and it covered every developer on every border. The relaxation was also requested by SECI and GPCL, not by Adani. Symmetry: the same test run on NTPC, GSECL or Sarjan Realities at Khavda would show no comparable jump in allotment. That asymmetry is real, but it is the land outcome that is asymmetric, not the rule change.
verdicts.denialFound: Adani Group, in a statement to The Guardian quoted by Scroll: "We are fully compliant with all the state and central government laws and regulations and have secured all the necessary approvals from the relevant competent authorities ... The land allocation for the project adheres to policy guidelines and is based on the credentials and performance of Adani Green Energy" (https://scroll.in/article/1076846/...). Scroll asked Adani specifically how it knew the rules had changed and got no answer. MoD, Gujarat, MNRE, SECI and the Gujarat Chief Secretary were all asked and did not respond. Government reply in Parliament: on 12 Mar 2025 MNRE minister Pralhad Joshi told the Lok Sabha that "all necessary clearances from the Union government and the state government have been obtained" (https://www.thenewsminute.com/news/adani-solar-project-opposition-walks-out-of-ls-over-ministers-insufficient-reply). The record should add this as a contra.
verdicts.innocentReading: The record's innocent reading needs fixing. "Reading a public guideline" is not supported. The 8 May letter was sent to governments, not shown to have been published. And Adani's 7 July letter says "We are given to understand that based on the latest guidelines, additional area has become available", which points to information from officials. A better innocent reading: Adani Green was an existing Khavda developer under the same border restrictions. The 21 Apr MoD minutes record the views of "project developers" who had "already constructed" solar platforms, so existing developers were consulted and would have learned of the relaxation through GPCL. MNRE had been weighing SECI's surrender since 1 May on viability grounds (SECI is a trader, and wind-only on the parcel gave about 1,100 MW), and that was plausibly known within the park. Adani, as the largest adjacent allottee with manufacturing capacity and evacuation access, then applied first. The committee's minutes also say the land "have been demanded" by both PSUs and private companies, so Adani was not the only one asking.
verdicts.reason: This is a sequence test, and the sequence it gives contradicts its only source. The claim places Adani's 3 Jul request ahead of "SECI hybrid request 17 Jul", and c076.d says Adani's letter "precedes SECI's own hybrid request (2023-07-17)". Scroll shows SECI had sought hybrid use since at least April 2023; the MoD relaxation was granted on that request. The 17 Jul letter is SECI's surrender, which looks back on the unanswered earlier request. The claim also leaves out the 1 May 2023 MNRE direction to "analyze the option of surrendering", which moves the start of the surrender track to before both the 8 May guideline and Adani's letter. It states "on ministerial instruction" as fact, when the quoted document says only "analyze the option". Its innocent reading rests on a "public guideline" that the source does not show was public. The core dated facts (3 Jul, 7 Jul, 17 Jul, 24 Aug; no bidding recorded) are confirmed by documents quoted in Scroll, and the Guardian and the Kashmir Times/National Herald/South First pickups carry the same facts. A corrected analytic edge therefore survives. The edge as written does not.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Rewrite the text and lab sequence as: SECI seeks hybrid use (6 Apr 2023 meeting; GPCL writes to PMO) → MoD meeting approves 1–2 km wind / 2–8 km hybrid (21 Apr) → MNRE minister R.K. Singh's meeting directs SECI to "analyze the option of surrendering" (1 May) → MoD guideline letter to all states and UTs (8 May) → Adani Power + Mundra Solar Technology consortium requests 23,000 ha of the "Area Originally Reserved for Exclusive Wind" (3 Jul) → Adani Power revises to 25,500 ha, "given to understand ... additional area has become available" (7 Jul) → SECI's letter recording its earlier hybrid request and surrendering the land (17 Jul) → CM's committee selects Adani Power in-principle (24 Aug; the source also says 23 Aug). 2) Delete "precedes SECI's own hybrid request (2023-07-17)" from d. 3) Replace "on ministerial instruction" with "after a 1 May 2023 MNRE meeting chaired by R.K. Singh directed SECI to 'analyze the option of surrendering' (Scroll characterises this as instruction)". 4) Replace "reading a public guideline" in the innocent reading with "learning of the relaxation as an existing Khavda developer consulted at or after the 21 Apr MoD meeting". Note that the 8 May letter was sent to governments and has not been shown to be public. 5) Add that the 24 Aug minutes record the SECI land was "demanded" by PSUs and private firms, which shows other applicants existed and weakens upgradeIf's premise. 6) Revise killIf: the 1 May surrender direction already partly meets "surrender decided before Adani's 3 July letter". 7) Add contra edges: the Adani spokesperson statement (via Guardian/Scroll) and Pralhad Joshi's Lok Sabha reply of 12 Mar 2025. 8) Name Mundra Solar Technology as co-applicant on 3 Jul. 9) Keep the from date at 2023-04-06 or 2023-04-21 rather than 2023-05-08, so the window covers the start of the sequence.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: ECI recommended to the Jharkhand Governor that Hemant Soren be disqualified as an MLA, 2022-08-25, sent as an opinion in a sealed cover. The alleged act is that Soren, while CM and holding the mining portfolio, took a stone-quarry lease in his own name in 2021. That falls inside his CM term of 2019-12-29 to 2024-02-02, so the dates overlap and the test passes. The field from:"2022-01-01" is a placeholder. The ECI opinion date was 2022-08-25, the day of the Deccan Herald and The Wire reports. The BJP complaint and the Governor's Article 192 reference came earlier in 2022.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. Hemant Soren is the sitting CM of Jharkhand and JMM MLA for Barhait. There is no name-collision risk. Shibu Soren and Basant Soren are separate people; Basant faced a separate 9A reference over a mining company stake in the same period, and that should not be merged into this claim. ECI is the correct constitutional body under Article 192 read with RP Act s.9A.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not apply the way it does to donor or contract edges. ECI office-of-profit or s.9A opinions against a sitting CM are rare, so the edge discriminates. Symmetry check: the same lens caught the 2018 ECI opinion on 20 AAP MLAs (office of profit), which the President acted on. That was also an opposition party, so the lens is not uniquely partisan here. But the complainant here was the BJP, the Governor was a Centre appointee, and the ECI opinion was never made public. Those facts belong in the record.
verdicts.denialFound: A denial exists, so the companion contra states:c008 ("No on-record denial located") is wrong. The Wire, 2022-08-25, quotes Soren verbatim: "It apparently seems that BJP leaders including a BJP MP and his puppet journalists have themselves drafted the ECI report, which is otherwise a sealed cover report." The CMO also said it had not received any communication from the EC or Governor Ramesh Bais. URL: https://m.thewire.in/article/politics/hemant-soren-says-bjp-drafted-ecs-sealed-report-on-his-disqualification. The same quote was carried by India Today on 2022-08-25: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/illegal-mining-case-bjp-drafted-eci-s-report-says-hemant-soren-on-his-disqualification-1992500-2022-08-25.
verdicts.innocentReading: The ECI opinion was never officially published. Its content ("favours disqualification") comes only from anonymous Raj Bhavan sources, relayed by PTI and others. The Governor never announced a decision, and Soren was never disqualified. Soren's side says he surrendered the small quarry lease, and says the leak was a political operation by the BJP, which was the complainant. On this reading the "recommendation" is an unverified leak about a referral process that never produced a legal result.
verdicts.reason: The source chain holds. Wikipedia's "Personal life / legal" section says: "In 2022, the Election Commission of India reportedly recommended his disqualification as an MLA for allegedly violating electoral laws by extending a mining lease to himself." It cites Deccan Herald, 2022-08-25: "EC favours disqualification of Jharkhand CM Soren as MLA: Raj Bhavan sources". The Wire, same day, says the same thing and names RP Act s.9A. So the claim matches its sources, the dates overlap and the identity is clean. The key point is that the recommendation rests on anonymous sourcing ("Raj Bhavan sources"), not named sourcing or a published document. That keeps it at alleged rather than reported or documented. Alleged needs a contra, and one now exists: Soren's on-record denial. The existing contra edge c008 is factually wrong, because it says no denial was found, and it must be replaced.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Replace states:c008. Change lab to "Soren: BJP 'drafted' sealed ECI report". Put Soren's verbatim quote in d. Set from=2022-08-25 and tier=reported (The Wire quotes him on record). Set srcs to The Wire and India Today URLs above. (2) In c007, change from "2022-01-01" to "2022-08-25". (3) In c007, add the primary-news source as well as Wikipedia: Deccan Herald https://www.deccanherald.com/india/ec-favours-disqualification-of-jharkhand-cm-soren-as-mla-raj-bhavan-sources-1139272.html (it returned 403 to this fetch; it is cited by Wikipedia) and The Wire (above). (4) In c007.d, name the legal basis: RP Act 1951 s.9A (government contract), referred by the Governor under Constitution Art. 192. Say the sourcing is anonymous ("Raj Bhavan sources") and that the ECI opinion was never made public. Also say the Governor made no decision public and Soren was not disqualified. Drop "or was overtaken by his subsequent resignation/arrest", which is speculative. (5) Change "extending a mining lease to himself" to "obtaining/renewing a stone-quarry lease in his own name while holding the mining portfolio (2021)". Mark lease specifics (Angara, Ranchi, about 0.88 acre) unverified until a source is fetched.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: MSEDCL issued a Letter of Intent (LoI) for 6,600 MW bundled solar and thermal power to Adani Power, around 13–15 September 2024. The tender was floated in March 2024, before the Lok Sabha model code of conduct. The LoI came before the Maharashtra assembly election was announced (TOI). The award therefore falls under the Shinde-led Mahayuti government, with Fadnavis as Deputy CM. The dates overlap and the date test passes. The record has `from: null`, but the date is findable: The Hindu/PTI is dated 15 Sep 2024, reports the award, and quotes an Adani statement.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes, and the record's own "presumed but not confirmed" hedge is now resolved. The Hindu/PTI quotes the Adani Group's own statement: "Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company (MSEDCL) issues a letter of intent for 6,600 MW to Adani Power." So `s` = energy:msedcl and `t` = co:adani-power are the right legal entities. One caveat: the 5,000 MW solar part is to be supplied by the sister company Adani Green Energy Ltd (fixed ₹2.70/unit, from Khavda). Adani Power supplies 1,496 MW net thermal from a new 1,600 MW ultra-supercritical unit. There is no name-collision risk.
verdicts.baseRate: This was an open competitive tariff-based tender with at least three serious bidders: Adani, JSW Energy and Torrent Power. Adani was lowest at ₹4.08/kWh for 25 years, which TOI says is about ₹1 below Maharashtra's 2024-25 average procurement cost of ₹4.97/kWh. Winning a large discom PPA as L1 is the normal outcome of these auctions, so the award alone does not discriminate. What could discriminate is the tender design: a "unique" bundled 5 GW solar plus 1.6 GW coal format that few bidders can fill. I could not measure that, and it is not shown here. Symmetry: Adani holds long-term supply deals with discoms and SECI-linked contracts in states run by several parties, so an "Adani won a state PPA" edge is not special to BJP-run Maharashtra.
verdicts.denialFound: No rebuttal of the rigging charge was found. The Hindu/PTI (15 Sep 2024) carries only an Adani confirmation of the LoI, not a response to the allegation. The TOI piece (15 Sep 2024) carries no Adani or government response, and neither article says either party was asked. I could not search further because the session's web search budget was used up (200/200). So: none found, not asked in the cited reports. MSEDCL, Adani and MERC-order responses remain unsearched.
verdicts.innocentReading: MSEDCL ran a competitive tender in March 2024 to buy round-the-clock capacity for rising demand. Adani could supply both the 5 GW solar (Khavda) and 1.6 GW of new thermal, bid lowest at ₹4.08/unit against JSW and Torrent, and so received the LoI. That price is below the state's average procurement cost. The timing before the election follows a tender floated in March, not a new decision.
verdicts.reason: The fact holds, but the source chain as recorded does not meet the "reported" bar. The only source is Wikipedia, a tertiary source and not a credible outlet with named sourcing. What rescues the claim is Wikipedia's own citation, which I opened. The Hindu/PTI (15 Sep 2024) says: "the Adani Group won a bid to supply 6,600 MW of bundled renewable and thermal power to Maharashtra for the long term after its quote of ₹4.08 per unit beat the likes of JSW Energy and Torrent Power." It also quotes Adani's own statement naming MSEDCL and Adani Power. TOI (15 Sep 2024) independently gives the same figures and the March tender history. That is one credible outlet with a named, published party statement, so "reported" is justified once the source is swapped. It is not yet "documented": TOI is probably not independent of the PTI copy, and I did not retrieve a primary record such as the Adani Power exchange filing or the MERC tariff-adoption order. The record's "gaps" (date, counterparty, tariff) are all answered by sources it already points to at one remove. It also overstates the award as a "contract": it was an LoI, not a signed PPA.

Also add TOI, 15 Sep 2024: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/shocking-details-soon-congress-alleges-rigging-by-mahayuti-government-in-adani-power-deal/articleshow/113369308.cms. verdicts.dateTest: What the edge says: Devendra Fadnavis denied / answered the charge that the Maharashtra 6,600 MW award was bid-rigged, date not given (from/to are null). What actually happened: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh made the charge on X on 2024-09-15, as reported by The Hindu (PTI) and the Times of India. Fadnavis was Deputy CM in the Shinde Mahayuti government at that time (2022-06-30 to 2024-11-26). He did not become CM until 2024-12-05, which is the date the node's `sub` leads with. So his time in office overlaps the award, but his office then was Deputy CM, not CM. The main problem is that there is no dated act by Fadnavis at all. The edge makes him the actor of a denial that, by its own text, was never found.
verdicts.identityTest: This fails. The source chain names Congress / Jairam Ramesh as the accuser and the 'Mahayuti government' as the target. It does not name Fadnavis at either end, and there is no Fadnavis statement on this deal in any source cited or found. Under SPEC, a `contra` edge runs from the denier to the claim it answers. Setting s=energy:per-devendra-fadnavis therefore says Fadnavis issued a rebuttal, and nothing supports that. The target is also muddled: the `alleged` content (INC's charge) is placed inside a `contra` edge aimed at the `award` claim c021. The accuser (INC) should be the source node of an allegation edge, not a contra from the accused side. On the other end, the award went to Adani Power (about 1,496 MW net thermal) and Adani Green Energy (5,000 MW solar from Khavda), according to The Hindu. Treating it as a single Adani Power contract (c021) is also inaccurate.
verdicts.baseRate: The allegation alone does not discriminate. INC attacks almost every large Adani award (Dharavi, the Uttarakhand project, LIC, the MP coal mine, and others) in 2024-26 coverage, and Mahayuti parties attack awards made by opposition-run states in the same way. An opposition 'rigged deal' tweet made weeks before an assembly election is a routine event, so it carries little evidential weight by itself. What would discriminate is the investigative reporting on how the tender was designed. The Reporters' Collective ran 'Tailored To Fit: Two Lucrative Power Tenders By BJP-Ruled States Favour Adani Group' on 2024-09-23, and the Rajasthan single-bid 11,200 MW row followed. This edge ignores that reporting.
verdicts.denialFound: No on-record denial specific to this charge was found from Fadnavis, the Maharashtra government, MSEDCL or Adani. It is unclear whether any of them were asked. Search was limited: the web-search budget was exhausted, and Google News RSS queries turned up no rebuttal story. The contemporaneous PTI report does carry the counter-facts, though. The Hindu, 15 Sep 2024: "after its quote of ₹4.08 per unit beat the likes of JSW Energy and Torrent Power", and the solar portion is at "a fixed cost of ₹2.70 per unit throughout the entire supply period" (https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/rigged-deal-congress-attacks-mahayuti-government-over-adani-winning-bid-to-supply-power-to-maharashtra/article68645859.ece). These are counter-evidence, not a denial by any party, and they are not attributed to Fadnavis.
verdicts.innocentReading: This was an open long-term procurement by the state discom for bundled renewable and thermal power. Adani won as the lowest bidder at ₹4.08/unit against named rivals (JSW Energy, Torrent Power). Being the only group able to offer 5 GW of solar from its own Khavda park plus new ultra-supercritical coal capacity would explain the win without any rigging. Congress's charge came about two months before the November 2024 assembly election and promised 'shocking details' that do not appear in the sources checked here.
verdicts.reason: The edge contradicts itself and puts words in Fadnavis's mouth. The `contra` predicate with s=Fadnavis says he rebutted c021, while the edge's own text says no rebuttal was found. That is a made-up denial created by the graph structure, which the brief forbids. The actual evidence is different: an INC (Jairam Ramesh) allegation dated 2024-09-15, reported by two outlets (The Hindu/PTI and the Times of India), with no located response from the accused. That belongs in a new `alleged` edge from an INC node to claim:states:c021, not in a contra from Fadnavis. The Wikipedia source does support the bare allegation: "Adani group also faced accusations of bid-rigging by the Indian National Congress after winning a contract to supply 6,600 MW of electricity to Maharashtra". It says nothing about Fadnavis or any rebuttal. As built, the edge should not enter the graph.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Delete states:c022 as built (Fadnavis → contra). 2) Replace it with an allegation edge. s = an INC party node (Jairam Ramesh, Congress general secretary in charge of communications, as the speaker); t = claim:states:c021; tier = alleged; from = 2024-09-15. Sources: The Hindu/PTI (URL above, confirmed) and TOI (https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/shocking-details-soon-congress-alleges-rigging-by-mahayuti-government-in-adani-power-deal/articleshow/113369308.cms), cited directly rather than through Wikipedia. Quote: "Shocking details of this rigged deal will soon start tumbling out." 3) Give it a real contra. Either use the counter-facts from The Hindu (lowest bid ₹4.08/unit beating JSW Energy and Torrent Power; solar fixed at ₹2.70/unit), attributed to the report and not to any official, or record denialFound = 'none located; not known whether asked'. Do not attach any denial to Fadnavis. 4) Add the Reporters' Collective 'Tailored To Fit' piece (2024-09-23) as a candidate source. It is a more substantive, investigative version of the allegation and should be verified before it is used. 5) Fix c021 using The Hindu. The winners were Adani Power (1,496 MW net thermal from a new 1,600 MW USC unit) and Adani Green Energy (5,000 MW solar, Khavda). The award was about 2024-09-14/15, a long-term bundled supply to the Maharashtra discom (Business Standard: 'Adani firms to sign 6.6 GW power supply pact with Maharashtra discom'). It is no longer undated, and c021 can stay at reported or rise to documented, since The Hindu and Business Standard are two independent outlets. 6) Node energy:per-devendra-fadnavis: publicRole should say he was Deputy CM, not CM, when the award was made (Sept 2024). Link him only through a role edge with dates, not a contra.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as written: "US DOJ indicted Gautam Adani over >$250m bribes, Nov 2024; as of Sept 2026 a judge blocked DOJ from dropping the case, so it is open." The 2024 half holds: the grand jury returned the indictment on 2024-10-24 and it was unsealed on 2024-11-20. The 2026 half fails. On 2026-08-10 Judge Garaufis issued a 47-page order granting DOJ's Rule 48(a) motion. It dismissed Counts 2, 3 and 4 (securities-fraud conspiracy, wire-fraud conspiracy, securities fraud) against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain with prejudice (PTI/Indian Express, 12 Aug 2026; CBS, NYT, Reuters, BBC, FT, 10-11 Aug). The September ruling (Politico, 4 Sep 2026: "Judge denies DOJ's request to drop charges against Adani co-conspirators"; The Wire, 5 Sep: "...Against Gautam Adani's Co-Defendants") covers only Count 1 (FCPA) and Count 5 (obstruction). Those counts are against five India-based co-defendants who have not appeared. For Gautam Adani the criminal case has been closed since 2026-08-10, and the SEC civil case was settled in May 2026. So the edge's `to` should be 2026-08-10, not null. Its killIf condition ("DOJ succeeds in withdrawing the indictment") has in fact been met for this subject.
verdicts.identityTest: The edge fails on node and direction. SPEC says `enforce` goes agency→subject, but here s=gadani and t=seci. Gautam Adani is the accused, not the enforcing agency. SECI (Solar Energy Corporation of India) is the central PSU that bought the power, not the enforcer. The indictment alleges state discoms were induced to sign power sale agreements with SECI. The correct edge is US DOJ (EDNY) → gadani, plus a separate SEC → gadani edge. There is also a charge-identity error. Gautam Adani was not charged with bribery. The FCPA bribery count (Count 1) names Ranjit Gupta, Cyril Cabanes, Saurabh Agarwal, Deepak Malhotra and Rupesh Agarwal (linked to Azure Power). Gautam Adani faced only the securities and wire fraud counts. The Wikipedia source's line "charged Adani and executives for five criminal counts of bribery" is itself wrong. "Agarwal" appears twice among the co-defendants, a known name-collision risk, so do not merge them with other Agarwal nodes.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a discriminating comparison. No other top Indian renewable bidder that won SECI's manufacturing-linked solar tender has been indicted in the US. This is an event, not a shared trait. Symmetry works in both directions: the five states named cover YSRCP, INC, BJD and DMK governments and a UT under central rule, so it is not a one-party pattern.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and the record wrongly treats it as missing. States:c024 says the denial text could not be found. Indian Express/PTI (12 Aug 2026) reports: "The Adani Group has consistently denied the allegations, saying it acted in accordance with the applicable law." Gautam Adani said "truth has prevailed" and that "our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering" (post on X after the 10 Aug 2026 dismissal). Adani's lawyers also said the $10bn US investment pledge "was never offered in exchange for dropping the charges". MLex (1 Jun 2026) reports that amended SEC settlement documents allow Adani to deny the SEC's allegations. Source: https://indianexpress.com/article/india/relief-to-adani-us-court-permanently-dismisses-criminal-case-against-him-10828913/
verdicts.innocentReading: This is an unproven indictment. DOJ dropped it, citing jurisdictional and evidentiary problems, the mainly Indian nature of the alleged conduct, scrutiny by Indian authorities and no identified investor losses. The court dismissed the charges against the Adanis with prejudice, and no trial ever tested the evidence. Against that, Garaufis stressed the dismissal was "not a verdict on the allegations", and he criticised DOJ officials' conduct. The bribery allegation therefore stays an attributed, untested claim. It has not been disproved.
verdicts.reason: The claim's main new assertion is false for its named subject. It says a judge blocked DOJ from dropping the case as of Sept 2026, so the case is open and contested. In fact the charges against Gautam Adani were dismissed with prejudice on 2026-08-10. The September ruling concerned only the FCPA and obstruction counts against five co-defendants, and the SEC civil case settled in May 2026. On top of that, the edge runs the wrong way and points at the wrong node: gadani→seci on an agency→subject predicate. It also says Adani was indicted for bribery when he was charged with securities and wire fraud. Its only source is Wikipedia, which gets the charges wrong. verdicts.dateTest: Adani Group denied the DOJ/SEC allegations against Adani Green directors on 21 Nov 2024. The indictment was unsealed on 20 Nov 2024 (US time), so the denial came the next day, and from=2024-11-21 is correct. The party existed and spoke in that window, so the date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The statement is issued in the name of the Adani Group and refers to 'directors of Adani Green', which matches c023's subjects (Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani, AGEL executives). Node IDs do not match across files, though. This edge uses s='grp:adani'. The same denial is already in the repo as solarwind:c052 with s='adani', and people.json carries it too. Merge on a single canonical group node.
verdicts.baseRate: This does not apply in the usual way. A denial by an accused corporate is close to universal, so it says nothing about the merits. That is fine: a contra edge exists to record the response, not to discriminate between parties.
verdicts.denialFound: Found, in the group's own primary statement, and the URL is reachable. I fetched https://www.adani.com/newsroom/media-releases/media-statement-1 this session and got HTTP 200. It reads: "21 November 2024 The allegations made by the US Department of Justice and the US Securities and Exchange Commission against directors of Adani Green are baseless and denied ... All possible legal recourse will be sought." Other sources elsewhere in the repo: an AGEL exchange statement of 27 Nov 2024 saying reports that Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and Vneet Jaain were charged under the FCPA 'are incorrect' (solarwind.json, solarwind:c052), and Forbes, 30 Nov 2024, https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2024/11/30/billionaire-gautam-adani-decries-baseless-us-indictment-accusing-him-of-250-million-bribery-scheme/ (this returned 403 to me, but people.json already cites it).
verdicts.innocentReading: A standard corporate denial issued the day after the indictment was unsealed. It tells us the accused's position, not whether the allegations are true.
verdicts.reason: The edge rests on the premise that no source for the denial could be reached. That premise is false. The group's own primary statement is live at adani.com with the exact wording and date, and the same repo already sources this denial in solarwind:c052, people.json and AUDIT.json. As written, srcs is empty and the text is a note about the session's sourcing gap rather than a claim, so it fails every tier requirement. The denial itself is real, so the fix is to rewrite the edge as a sourced, documented contra, not to kill it.
